75.text:
The verse sets out the difference between two people of the same book. It begins with the one who keeps a trust, "There are some among the People of the Book who", and what is told of them is "if entrusted with a stack of gold", "will readily return it", so that a large sum comes back without pressure. The sources name one of them, and they draw the contrast with the second kind in the phrase that follows, "Yet there are others who", of whom it is told "if entrusted with a single coin", "will not repay it unless you constantly demand it", so that the smallest sum is withheld until it is taken back by force. The reason they give is then quoted: "This is because they say", and the saying is "We are not accountable for exploiting the Gentiles", which the sources explain as their claim that the wealth of those outside their religion may be taken without blame. The verse closes on the judgment of that claim, "And so they attribute lies to Allah knowingly", because no licence to take the property of others was given in the book they carry, and the sources read the sentence as the charge that they put words in the mouth of God. The two halves are held together by the trust, since the same book commands the return of what is held, and the verses after it take up the oath and the pledge in the same way. The verse keeps the two kinds of people of the book apart so that the judgment falls on the practice and not on the name, and the two examples are placed together because the difference between them is not the book they carry but what they do with what they are given. The sources bring out that the praise given to the one who returns the trust is not a praise of his religion, since the verse is about honesty and the honesty of a person is a good in itself, while the other kind is condemned for taking what was not his. The two sentences stand as a test for the reader as well, because the trust named here is not only the money left with a person but every duty that has been placed on him, and the verse measures the man by what he does when no one is watching him.

**The trust that is returned.**

And of the People of the Scripture is he who if you trust him with a hundredweight that is with much money he will return it to you on account of his trustworthiness the like of ‘Abd Allāh b. Among the People of the Scripture is he who, if entrusted with a Qintar (a great amount of wealth), will readily pay it back; and among them there is he who, if entrusted with a single silver coin, will not repay it unless you constantly stand demanding, because they say: (will readily pay it back;) This Ayah indicates that this type would likewise give what is less than a Qintar, as is obvious. (Among the People of the Scripture) i.e. the Jews (there is he who, if you trust him with a weight of treasure, will return it to you) without any problem, hardship or ever thinking to keep it for himself by declaring it lawful for him to take. There are some People of the Scripture who, if you hand over a large amount of wealth, will honour the trust. The reference here is to 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his companions.

**The trust that is not returned.**

Salām to whom a man entrusted 1200 plates of gold which he then returned to him; and of them is he who if you trust him with one dinar will not return it to you on account of his treachery; unless you keep standing over him not leaving him for one minute for as soon as you leave him he will deny it as was the case with Ka‘b b. al-Ashraf to whom a man from Quraysh entrusted a dinar and later denied it. If this is what he would do with one Dinar, then what about what is more than a Dinar? (And among them there is he who, if you trust him with a piece of gold, will not return it to you) and will declare it lawful for him to take (unless you keep standing over him) insisting on taking it back and suing him for it. The reference here is to Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf and his followers. On the other hand, there are some of them who, if you trust them with a small amount, will not return the trust unless you persistently demand it from them.

**The claim of no blame.**

That refusal to return things is because they say ‘We have no duty towards namely no possibility of acquiring sin because of the Gentiles’ the Arabs; for they considered it lawful to be unjust towards any person of a different religion and they attributed the source of this conviction to God exalted be He. (because they say: "There is no blame on us to betray and take the properties of the illiterates (Arabs).") means, what made them reject the truth (or what they owed) is that they said, "There is no harm in our religion if we eat up the property of the unlettered ones, the Arabs, for Allah has allowed it for us. That is because they wrongly claim that there is no sin on them for any crime they commit against the Arabs or if they consume the wealth of the Arabs, since Allah has permitted that for them. That is because they say We have no duty toward the Gentiles. (That) treachery and declaring that it is lawful to take other people's property (is because they say: We have no duty to the Gentiles) there is no harm in taking the property of Arabs. If this 'some' refers to those among the people of the Book who had embraced Islam, praising them poses no problems. But, in case, it does not refer to Muslims particularly and instead, refers to the people of the Book in the absolute sense including non-Muslims as well, then the situation generates the question:

**The lies they attribute to Allah.**

God exalted be He says They speak falsehood against God by attributing such things to Him while they are aware that they are liars. " But they tell a lie against Allah while they know it Yes, whoever fulfills his pledge and fears Allah much; verily, then Allah loves the Muttaqin (the pious) (But they tell a lie against Allah while they know it.) for they invented this lie and word of misguidance. (They speak a lie concerning Allah knowingly) they lie about Allah and know that they are lying. They say such lies knowing that it is a false attribution to Allah. They speak falsehood against God while they are aware.

**What the pledge and the punishment come to.**

In the previous verses (70-72), breach of faith committed by the people of the Book was mentioned. In this verse , some people have been praised for their trustworthiness. (unless you keep standing over him - 75) that Imam Abu Hanifah has deduced the ruling that the lender has the right to keep pursuing the borrower until he receives his due. This included disbelieving in the verses of Allah, confusing the truth with what is false, concealing the truth and conspiring to mislead Muslim believers. From praising something it does not follow that it is acceptable with Allah. When no act of a kafir (disbeliever) is acceptable why praise them? In the verse cited above , their breach of trust in matters of property has been mentioned. Since some of them happened to be trustworthy, both types were identified. The purpose is to point out that something good, even if it be that of a kafir (disbeliever), is good enough in a certain degree, the benefit of which he receives in the form of good reputation in the mortal world, and of course, in the Hereafter, in the form of a reduction in punishment for his disbelief. (Yes, whoever fulfills his pledge and fears Allah much,) fulfills his promise and fears Allah among you, O People of the Book, regarding the covenant Allah took from you to believe in Muhammad when he is sent, just as He took the same covenant from all Prophets and their nations. "There is no blame on us to betray and take the properties of the illiterates (Arabs). (There is no blame on us to betray and take the properties of the illiterates (Arabs).) Rather, Allah would not allow this money for them unless they had a right to it. Whoever avoids Allah's prohibitions, obeys Him and adheres to the Shari'ah that He sent with His Final Messenger and the master of all mankind. And of the people of the scriptures is he who if you trust him with a hundredweight he will return it to you; and of them is he who if you trust him with one dinar will not return it to you; unless you keep standing over him. This statement also makes it, clear that Islam does not resort to prejudice and short-sightedness. Subsequently, Allah mentions the trustworthiness and treachery of the people of the Book, saying:

**What they will lose and what they will be given.**

All of them have broken the trust amāna of the religion dīn but among them are those who have regard for proper [human] interactions. Even though they interact with sincerity it will not benefit them in receiving reward but it will benefit them in lessening [their] punishment since disbelievers are held accountable in the details of the laws. If in their disbelief they sinned less they will suf fer less punishment than those who have lost the most even though their punishment will also be in perpetuity. Then He explained that the judgment is not theirs so that when they say We have no duty toward the Gentiles the situation is not as they would have it nor will these words benefit them. He relates that [the people of the scripture] notwithstanding their error and disbelief vary in their moral qualities. God’s chosen servants are those who fulfill their trusts and do not break their promises. It is people such as these who are showered with God’s blessings. They will be denied God’s mercies and blessings.

76.text:
The verse opens with the answer to the claim made before it, "Absolutely, Those who honour their trusts and shun evil", and the words are there to deny that the return of a trust is optional, since what follows is the other side of the account. The people described are "Those who honour their trusts and shun evil", and the sources explain the trusts as what a person is given to keep, both what is owed to God and what is owed to people, while the second phrase names the guarding of the same person against disobedience. The promise attached to them comes at the end: "surely Allah loves those who are mindful of Him", and the sources read the love of God here as the highest thing a servant can be given, because it carries acceptance and reward with it. The verse answers the traders in the verses before and after it, who sell the pledge for a price in this world, and it places the honesty of the believer against their practice. The answer stands at the head of the verse because the claim in the verse before it would otherwise pass unanswered, and the sources read the word as the plain denial of the licence that the others had taken to themselves. The honesty of the one who keeps a pledge is placed against the practice of the one who sells it, and the verse leaves the reader with the two ends of the same account in view.

**What the trust covers.**

Nay there is a duty incumbent over them in this regard; but whoever fulfils his covenant the one he has made or the covenant of God by restoring a trust and other such things and has fear of God by refraining from disobedience and performing deeds of obedience for truly God loves the God-fearing ‘He loves them’ means that He will reward them the overt noun al-muttaqīn ‘the God-fearing’ has replaced the third person pronominalisation. Allah is here answering them, (but (the chosen of Allah is) he who fulfileth his pledge) He says: but he who keeps his pledge between himself and his Lord or between himself and other people (and wardeth off (evil) ward off breaking his pledge by treachery and turning on his pledge; (for lo! Allah loveth those who ward off (evil) ward off breaking pledges, treachery and being untrustworthy. It is not as they claimed: in fact, there is a sin on them. However, if anyone fulfils his promise to Allah to have faith in Him and His Messenger, as well as his promise to people to honour their trusts, and is mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions, then Allah loves those who are mindful of Him and will give them the best reward. (Yes, whoever fulfills his pledge and fears Allah much,) fulfills his promise and fears Allah among you, O People of the Book, regarding the covenant Allah took from you to believe in Muhammad when he is sent, just as He took the same covenant from all Prophets and their nations. Nay but whoever fulfils his covenant and has fear for truly God loves the God-fearing. Those who hold to the covenant are deserving of being united in friendship honor and the garden.

**What Allah Almighty will not do for them.**

Earlier, in ; ,(they say - 75), there was a refutation of the claim made, by the people of the Book. Onwards from there, in verses 76-77, the same refutation has been re-asserted and the merit of fulfilling a commitment as well as the condemnation for its breach have been clarified. Ahd (pledge or covenant) is what gets settled between parties concerned after mutual discussions and by which both of them have to abide. For instance, right here in verse 77 cited above, five warnings have been given to those who break their solemn pledge: Allah Almighty will not speak to them with glad tidings. Allah Almighty will not look at them mercifully on the Day of Doom. Allah Almighty will not forgive them their sins since they wasted away the rights of a servant of Allah through breach of trust, and Allah will not forgive what a human being owes to another human being. In Islamic terminology, this is known as the hagq al-'abd or the right of a servant of Allah. God’s chosen servants are those who fulfill their trusts and do not break their promises. On the contrary, those who are careless in the fulfillment of trusts and are negligent about keeping their promises are of no value in the eyes of God.

**What the lie against Allah comes to.**

" But they tell a lie against Allah while they know it Yes, whoever fulfills his pledge and fears Allah much; verily, then Allah loves the Muttaqin (the pious) Allah states that there are deceitful people among the Jews. (will readily pay it back;) This Ayah indicates that this type would likewise give what is less than a Qintar, as is obvious. If this is what he would do with one Dinar, then what about what is more than a Dinar? (because they say: "There is no blame on us to betray and take the properties of the illiterates (Arabs).") means, what made them reject the truth (or what they owed) is that they said, "There is no harm in our religion if we eat up the property of the unlettered ones, the Arabs, for Allah has allowed it for us. (But they tell a lie against Allah while they know it.) for they invented this lie and word of misguidance. Rather, Allah would not allow this money for them unless they had a right to it. Those who are in error are deserving of aversion ignominy and shame.

77.text:
The verse names the trade and the price. It begins with the people who make it, "Indeed, those who trade Allah's covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain will have no share in the Hereafter", so that what they sell is what they owe to God and what they receive is a little of this world, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the portion of the sellers in the next life is gone with the price they took. The rest of the verse lists what they lose. "Allah will neither speak to them" is the first, and the sources explain it as speech that carries no welcome, "nor look at them" is the second, and it is read as the turning away of mercy, and "nor purify them on the Day of Judgment" is the third, which the sources take as the statement that no cleansing and no forgiveness reaches them on that day. The verse ends with the sentence that gathers the three: "And they will suffer a painful punishment", and the sources place it here as the outcome of a bargain struck against the promise of God. The verses around it carry the same warning, since the verse before it praises the one who keeps the trust and the verse after it describes the distortion of the book. The punishment is named three times over because the bargain was struck with the name of God, and the verse weighs the gain against the loss in the same sentence. The sources bring out that the small gain is named first so that the reader sees the price before he sees the penalty, and they read the three denials as the loss of what every person hopes for on the day of account, a welcome, a look of mercy and a cleansing of the heart. The verses after it turn to the distortion of the book, so that the passage carries the three faults together, the selling of the pledge, the taking of what is not owed, and the putting of words into the mouth of God.

**The covenant and the oaths that were sold.**

(Lo! those who purchase a small gain) a small gain of in their living (at the cost of Allah's covenant) by breaking Allah's covenant (and their oaths) their pledges with their prophets, (they have no portion in the Hereafter) in Paradise. Those who take a small amount of this world in exchange of Allah’s advice to them to follow His revelation and His messengers, and in exchange of the oaths they took to fulfil Allah’s pledge, will have no share in the reward of the Afterlife. Allah states that whoever prefers the small things of this short, soon to end life, instead of fulfilling what they have promised Allah by following Muhammad , announcing his description [from their books] to people and affirming his truth, then,. Ahd (pledge or covenant) is what gets settled between parties concerned after mutual discussions and by which both of them have to abide. On embracing the faith, the individual enters into a covenant with God that he will obey Him and that, living among human beings, and pledging himself to a life of constraint, he will fulfill all the responsibilities that God’s law imposes upon him. One who is ready to overlook the divine pact whenever his self suffers or his worldly interests are endangered barters the world for the Hereafter at a very paltry price: whenever the question arises of choosing either the world or the Hereafter, he always prefers the world. Those that sell God's covenant and their own oaths for a small price there shall be no share for them in the hereafter; and God shall not speak to them nor look upon them on the Day of Resurrection nor will He purify them and theirs will be a painful chastisement. Those who prefer their caprice hawāhum over their final outcome ʿuqbāhum and have given priority to their desires munāhum over har monious agreement with their Protector mawlāhum will have no share in the hereafter. Contrary to this is wa'dah or promise which issues forth from a single side, that is, ahd (pledge or covenant) is bilateral while wa'dah (promise) is unilateral.

**What they will lose.**

(Allah will neither speak to them) in a nice manner on the Day of Judgement (nor look upon them on the Day of Resurrection) He will have no mercy for them, (nor will He make them grow) He will neither exonerate them for being Jews nor put their minds at peace. (Theirs will be a painful doom) a severe pain which will spread to their hearts. Moreover He will cause them to remain in the punishment beyond the count of time. This Ayah indicates that Allah will not speak words of kindness nor look at them with any mercy,. (nor will He purify them) from sins and impurities. The narrator of the hadith asked if the Fire will become compulsory even if this concerned something very insignificant? In Islamic terminology, this is known as the hagq al-'abd or the right of a servant of Allah. That commitments should be fulfilled has been stressed in the Qur'an and Sunnah time and again. In a hadith, the Holy Prophet has said that one who usurps the right of a Muslim under false oath makes the fire of Hell compulsory for himself.

**What Allah will not do for them.**

Allah Almighty will not speak to them with glad tidings. Allah Almighty will not forgive them their sins since they wasted away the rights of a servant of Allah through breach of trust, and Allah will not forgive what a human being owes to another human being. Allah then mentioned their punishment, i.e. the punishment of the Jews, saying: Because they have chosen to seek pleasure in the present they have lost in the two abodes and they remain apart from the Real. The pleasure they sought in worldly things ḥaẓẓ has brought upon them all kinds of tribulations but they are not aware of what has happened to them: How can one who attaches so little value to the Hereafter be deserving of God’s mercies in the next world? Such a life can be adhered to only by one who has risen above worldly interests. (There are three persons whom Allah will not speak to, look at on the Day of Resurrection or purify, and they shall taste a painful torment. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Who are they, may they gain failure and loss?' He said, repeating this statement thrice, 'The Musbil (man whose clothes reach below the ankles), he who swears while lying so as to sell his merchandize and the one who gives charity and reminds people of it).')" This was also recorded by Muslim, and the collectors of the Sunan.

**What the verses before it show.**

Earlier, in ; ,(they say - 75), there was a refutation of the claim made, by the people of the Book. Onwards from there, in verses 76-77, the same refutation has been re-asserted and the merit of fulfilling a commitment as well as the condemnation for its breach have been clarified. For instance, right here in verse 77 cited above, five warnings have been given to those who break their solemn pledge: The following was revealed with regard to the Jews when they distorted the descriptions of the Prophet s and God’s covenant with them in the Torah and God’s covenant with them regarding one that swears an oath to a falsehood when bearing witness or when selling merchandise Those that sell exchange God’s covenant with them that they believe in the Prophet and return faithfully what has been entrusted to them and their own oaths their invoking God’s name in mendacity for a small price of this world there shall be no share no lot for them in the Hereafter; and God shall not speak to them out of wrath against them nor look upon them nor have mercy upon them on the Day of Resurrection nor will He purify them cleanse them and theirs will be a painful chastisement. It is also said that this was revealed about 'Abdan Ibn al-Ashu' and Imra' al-Qays because of a dispute between them, and it was also revealed about the Jews. Whoever makes an oath knowing well that he is lying in order to usurp the property of another Muslim, Allah will be angry with him when he meets Him . Allah, exalted is He, then revealed (Lo! those who purchase a small gain at the cost of Allah's covenant and their oaths) . Whoever lies in his oath in order to usurp a property, Allah will be angry with him when he will meet Him . There was a land between me and a Jew, but he denied that I was its owner. I reported to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, a dispute that I had with another man and so he asked me: do you have a proof . He will take a (false) oath immediately, and I will lose my property.' Allah revealed the verse,.

78.text:
The verse describes a practice rather than an opinion, and it begins by marking out the group it has in view: "There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this distortion is from the Book". The tongue is named because the change is made in the recitation itself, the words being turned about as they are read out, so that a hearer takes what he hears for the text and has no way of telling where the reading has left the book. The sources explain the distortion as reciting a passage in a way other than the way it was revealed, and they name the places where it was done, the descriptions of the messenger that the earlier books carried and the traits that belonged to another. The subject of the sentence is not the letter of the scripture, which stays as it was given, but the use made of it, since what the reader adds passes with his hearers for what the book contains. The verse then denies the claim in the plainest words: "but it is not what the Book says, They say", and having named the claim it quotes it, "It is from Allah", and answers it in the same breath, "but it is not from Allah". The two halves are set against each other so that the reader sees the sentence made in the very form in which it is refused, and the sources understand the claim as the attribution to God of what was never in the book, a lie given the weight of revelation. The verse closes with the state of the people who do it: "And so they attribute lies to Allah knowingly", and the last word carries the charge, because the one who speaks out of ignorance may yet be taught, while the one who knows what he is doing stands under the verdict of the sentence. The verse was revealed about a party of the Jews during a visit to the Prophet, and the sources record the question that brought it down, so that the distortion it names was answered in the presence of the people who had raised it. It belongs to a run of verses that answer the People of the Book, and it prepares the two that follow, one on the pledge that they broke, and one on the men of the book who were never sent to make themselves lords.

**What the distortion of the tongue means.**

The change the verse names is made in the reading, and the sources are careful about where it takes place. They explain the distortion as reciting a passage in a way other than the way it was revealed, and they give the instances that were known to the first hearers, the reading of the descriptions of the messenger as though they stood for another man, and the reading of words that did not belong to the book as though they were part of it. Ka'b b. al-Ashraf and his companions are named as the party that did this, and the sources describe the act with the picture of a tongue that is turned about with the book, so that the wording is bent while the book itself is untouched. Al-Bukhari reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the verse means that they alter and add, and he keeps the charge exact by adding that no one among creation can remove the words of God from His books, so that what was altered was the outward meaning carried by the recitation, not the text that has been kept. The same explanation is given by Mujahid, Ash-Sha'bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, all of them reported with the sense that they change the words as they read them. What the verse describes is therefore not a scribe at work on a page but a reader at work on a hearing, and the harm is done to the people who cannot check what is being recited to them. That is why the verse puts the tongue first and the book second, and why the deception is described as aimed at the hearer: the one who listens takes the reading for the text because he trusts the one who reads.

**The claim that it is from God.**

The claim itself is quoted in the verse because it is the heart of the matter. What the party did was not only to read a passage in a distorted way but to say of it that it came from God, and the sources bring out that the sentence they made was about the book of God, that what they were reciting was in the scripture when it was not in it. Wahb bin Munabbih is reported to have held that the Torah and the Gospel remain as God revealed them and that no letter in them was removed, so that the people misguided others by addition and false interpretation, relying on books that they wrote themselves, and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that view. The sources also notice the other side of the question, that the books which are in the hands of the People of the Book have certainly been altered and added to and shortened in translation and interpretation, and they keep the two statements apart, one about the scripture as God keeps it and one about the copies and readings that people carry. The verse does not rest on either side of that discussion, since its charge stands on what is said with knowledge: a reading is made to carry what it does not carry, and then the weight of the book is laid on the words so that the people will accept them. The last phrase returns to the same point from the other end, because the lie against God is named as a lie, and the knowledge of the one who tells it is what makes the sentence final.

**Why the book was changed.**

The sources ask why a people who held a book and read it daily should go to such trouble, and they answer with the world that was being bought. Those who sell the next life for this one do not begin by denying religion in public, since a denial would cost them the standing they want; instead they keep their place among the religious and bend the teaching to fit the life they live. Aspirants to honour and influence take the revealed teaching and put their own construction on it, sometimes by altering the wording they recite and sometimes by a reading that carries the meaning they need, and in this way they give a religious colour to ways that their religion had forbidden. The sources describe the trade in plain terms: instead of changing themselves they change the book, so that whatever their conduct requires may be shown to be contained in what God has said. The most serious of these acts is the one the verse is about, the attribution to God of something He did not say, because it puts the authority of the revelation behind the invention of the speaker. The sources add the test that separates the true teaching from the false in a matter like this: a teaching that brings the servants of God nearer to their Lord, and turns their love and their fear to Him, bears the mark of the truth, while a teaching that gathers people around a man, or turns their hearts to any object other than God, is built on falsehood even when it is dressed in the language of religion.

**What the verse alludes to on the path.**

The allusive reading takes the practice the verse names and finds it in every later generation. It says that the verse points to those who make false claims on the path of devotion, who adorn what they say and let their tongues run on about matters that their own hearts have no knowledge or verification of. They do this among the simple and the beginners, who cannot weigh what they hear, and they deceive them by the sound of the words, so that the newcomers take the speaker for one who has arrived at the truth of what he describes. In this the verse supplies the measure of such a person, since the words are made to look as though they came from the book when they did not come from the book, and the deception works on the hearer who has no way to test the claim. The allusive reading then describes the source of the talk: a ruined heart and a veiled innermost self, from which the words come without the verification that would keep them true, so that what is said about God is said from a place that does not know Him. It closes with the refuge that such a description invites, and it leaves the reader with the same charge the verse makes, that words about God must come from what has been given and not from what a speaker wishes to be true.

**The occasion, and the question that was asked.**

The sources give the occasion of the verse, and it explains the shape of the answer. It was during the presence of the delegation from Najran that some Jews and Christians put a question to the Prophet, asking whether he wanted them to worship him in the way the Christians worship Jesus the son of Mary. His answer was a refusal that has been preserved with it: he sought refuge with God from worshipping anyone other than God, or calling others to that, and he said that God had not sent them to do it. The verse came down after that exchange, and the party it names are the men who were bending the book with their tongues, an act that the sources connect with the very claim that had just been made in the gathering. The question asked in the presence of a company, and the verse answered it by describing the practice that produced it, so that the people who heard the claim could see what kind of work it was. The two verses that follow carry the answer on, one naming the pledge they broke and the other clearing the prophets of any ask of worship. The verse therefore stands in the middle of an argument, and the answer it gives is not a defence of the messenger but a description of the method, since the distortion of the book by those who claimed the book was the ground on which the claim had been made.

79.text:
The verse lays down what the men of scripture cannot do. It begins with the denial of the misuse of an office: "It is not appropriate for someone who Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom", and the two gifts are named first because they are the ones the argument had turned on in the verses before, then "and prophethood to say to people" completes the sentence and names the third and highest of them. What such a man may not say is quoted: "Worship me instead of Allah. Rather, he would say, "Be devoted to the worship of your Lord alone", and the sources take the prohibition as aimed at the claims made for the prophets and at any teacher who lets his people make him a lord. What he does say is then described: "in accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught", so that the model is the book they recite and the practice they pass on, and the man of knowledge is placed under both. The verse answers the claim of the delegation that the prophets had asked to be worshipped, and it ends where the earlier passage ended, with the People of the Book answered out of their own scripture. The claim that any of them asked for worship is refused at the root, since the office they were given was to call people to the worship of God and to teach the book they had been given, and the verse leaves the reader with the two models set side by side, the lord taken from among the people and the servant devoted to his Lord. The verses that follow carry the denial further, since the next one carries that no prophet ever asked for the angels or the prophets to be made lords, and the one after that names the pledge taken from them all. The passage is one answer to one delegation, and this verse keeps the first part of it, that the men of the book were never sent to make themselves lords over the people who read with them.

**What the gift of the book does not permit.**

It is not (possible) for any human being to whom Allah has given the Book and Al-Hukm and prophethood to say to the people: No Prophet Ever Called People to Worship him or to Worship Other Than Allah. This Ayah [3:79] means, it is not for a person whom Allah has given the Book, knowledge in the Law and prophethood to proclaim to the people, "Worship me instead of Allah," meaning, along with Allah. It is not right for a man whom Allah gives a book revealed by Him, together with knowledge and understanding and selects him as a prophet, to say then to people, ‘Become servants of me instead of Allah’. 92.text:
"You will never achieve righteousness until you donate some of what you cherish" turns from the argument with the people of the Book to the community of the believers, and the sources begin by explaining the word that is used for righteousness, since it carries the whole reward of the good and the rank of the people of goodness and not merely one deed. The verse makes the gift the road to that state, so that the man who gives what he loves is named as the one who reaches it, while the giving that costs nothing is not the giving the sentence asks for. "And whatever you give is certainly well known to Allah" closes the verse with the knowledge that watches the gift, and the sources read it as the assurance that nothing given in the way of God is lost and as the warning that the quality of what is given is seen by the One who receives it. The verses before it had weighed the claims of the people of the Book, and this verse turns the same measure on the believers, since the earlier passage had asked them to hold to the faith and this one asks them to prove it in what they own. The sources also carry the account of a man who owned the garden he loved most and gave it away for the sake of God, and they bring out that the gift of the dearest thing is what the sentence means.

**What the word righteousness carries.**

Let us first understand what . : birr means and what it really signifies so that the whole sense of the verse becomes clear in our minds. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Righteousness is not that you turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteousness is that one believes in Allah and the last Day... 2:177. The verse further tells us 'you can never claim to have righteousness unless you spend out of what you hold dear.' Thus the meaning is that the perfect fulfillment of the rights of Allah Almighty and a total - self-unburdening from it cannot come to pass unless we spend in the way of Allah what we hold dear to our hearts. Therefore, the sense of the verse is that you give in the way of Allah whatever it may be, the obligatory zakah or the voluntary charity, but that perfect excellence and merit will blossom out from them only-when you spend in the way of Allah what you like and love. So, the outcome is that picking out the bad and the useless to give in charity is unacceptable; contrary to that is the acceptable charity which earns full merit and which is nothing but what is spent out of one's dear belongings. But, what is certainly undesirable and prohibited is getting into the habit of always picking out the extra and the bad to spend in the way of Allah. By no means shall you attain Al-Birr, unless you spend of that which you love; and whatever of good you spend, Allah knows it well. (By no means shall you attain Al-Birr) is in reference to attaining Paradise. (Ye will not attain unto piety) i.e. that which is with Allah of reward, honour and Paradise until you spend of that which you love of property; it is also said this means: you shall not attend to reliance in Allah and God-fearingness (until ye spend of that which ye love. And whatsoever ye spend) of property, (Allah is aware thereof) just as He is aware of your intentions, i.e. whether you intend with it His Countenance or other people's praise. O believers, you will not receive the reward of the people of goodness and their rank until you spend the wealth you love in the way of Allah. You will not attain piety birr until you expend of what mimmā = min mā you love; and whatever thing you expend God knows of it. When the object of seeking is piety and goodness birr [the preposition] min is used which is [the particle of speech] for dividing something into portions. Whoever desires piety and goodness birr should expend some portion of what he loves while whoever desires the One who is All-Goodness al-bārr should expend everything he loves. It is said that if you can only attain piety and goodness birr by expend ing what you love how will you ever reach the One who is All-Goodness al-bārr so long as you prefer your worldly fortunes to Himḍ And whatever thing you expend God knows of it. You will not attain piety that is the reward for it which is Paradise until you expend until you give voluntary alms of what you love of your wealth; and whatever thing you expend God knows of it and He will requite it accordingly.

**What the spending of what is loved means.**

Whatever you spend, big or small, Allah is aware of your intentions and of what you do; and everyone will be rewarded accordingly. Whoever expends what he loves in this world will find what he seeks from the Real most high. Whoever is attached to the fortunes of the lower self man kāna marbūṬan bi-ḥuẓūẓi nafsihi will not find fortune in nearness to his Lord lam yaḥaẓẓu bi-qurbi rabbihi. He trembles because of what has become known in seeking the sublime that his qualities might be mentioned one day before Salmā. So I want to give it in charity in Allah's cause, and I expect its reward and compensation from Allah. Spend it where Allah makes you think is feasible. ' On that, Allah's Messenger said,. (Well-done! It is profitable property, it is profitable property. I have heard what you have said, and I think it would be proper if you gave it to your kith and kin.) Abu Talhah said, 'I will do so, O Allah's Messenger.' Then Abu Talhah distributed that garden among his relatives and cousins." (Retain the land to give its fruits in Allah's cause.) Also stated in this last sentence of the verse is that Allah is fully aware of the real quality of what man spends and knows whether or not it is dear to him, and if he is spending it for the good pleasure of Allah, or for pretense and publicity.

**The question about the direction of prayer.**

According to the Jews’ self-made set of religious laws, eating the meat of the camel and the rabbit was illegal, while it was quite licit in Islam. So the Jews would ask, if Islam was a revealed religion, why it was that the lawful and the unlawful were different in Islam from what had been laid down in the former revealed religions. Similarly, they would ask how it was that a religion revealed by God could command the direction of prayer to be the Ka‘bah instead of al-Bayt al-Maqdis (Bayt al-Maqdis), which had remained the direction for prayer in the teachings of all the prophets up till then. They in fact refused to believe that God could reveal a religion in which the Ka‘bah was held to be the direction for prayer.

95.text:
"Say, O Prophet" opens the verse with the command to declare, and what is declared is the truth that settles the claim about the food of Israel. "Allah has declared the truth" names the decisive word, and the sources read it as the statement that God has spoken about what is lawful and what is not, so that nothing of the matter is left to argument. "So follow the Way of Abraham, the upright" turns the command to the believers, and the sources read the way as the surrender that Abraham held before the books came, with the word for upright naming the man who turned away from every other road to the one God. "who was not a polytheist" closes the verse by clearing him of any share in the worship of other than God, and the sources read the sentence as the answer to the claim of each community that he belonged to it. Say ‘God has spoken the truth in this matter just as He has in all that He has related; therefore follow the creed of Abraham the one which I follow a hanīf inclining away from all religions towards submission islām and he was not an idolater’. God has spoken the truth therefore follow the creed of Abraham a ḥanīf and he was not an idolater. The creed milla of Abraham was complete abandonment to God al-khurūju ilā Allāh bi-l-kulliya and surrender to His decree without hold ing back in any way wa-l-taslīmu li-ḥukmihi min ghayri an tabqā baqiyya. In truth to affirm ithbāt anything [other than God] in accounting for what comes into being is idolatry shirk. Also, tell them to follow the religion Abraham ﷺ: he abandoned all other ways of life for the path of surrendering in devotion to Allah, by worshipping Him and following His sacred law – he only worshipped Allah. In the verses appearing above, there is a continuity of arguments against positions taken by the people of the Book. At some places, it concerns Jews and at others, the Christians.

**What the answer to the Jews shows.**

The fact, as narrated by Sayyidna Ibn Abbas in an authentic re-port, is that Jacob suffered from Sciatica. He had taken a vow that he would abandon what he liked most in what he ate if Allah Almighty cured him of the disease. He was cured and camel meat was what he liked most, so he abandoned it. Then, it, so happened that this prohibition which started because of a vow continued among the Bani Isra'il as a divine injunction. It seems their code recognized a vow as a cause of unlawfulness of something lawful, like in our own Shari'ah, a vow may make the permissible acts as obligatory. However, a vow or pledge which renders things unlawful is, in reality, an oath which is not permissible in our Shari ah. In fact, in such a case, it is obligatory to break the oath and make amends by making Ka ffarah. Imam Ahmad recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said, "A group of Jews came to Allah's Prophet and said, 'Talk to us about some things we will ask you and which only a Prophet would know.' He said, 'Ask me about whatever you wish. And who is his Wali (supporter) among the angels?' The Prophet took their covenant that they will follow him if he answers these questions, and they agreed. Was not the best food to him camel meat and the best drink camel milk?' They said, 'Yes, by Allah.' The Messenger said, 'O Allah, be Witness against them.' The Prophet then said, 'I ask you by Allah, other than Whom there is no deity (worthy of worship), Who sent down the Tawrah to Musa, do you not know that man's discharge is thick and white and woman's is yellow and thin? If the woman's discharge is more than the man's, then the child will be female, by Allah's leave.' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'O Allah, be Witness against them.' He then said, 'I ask you by He Who sent down the Tawrah to Musa, do you not know that the eyes of this unlettered Prophet sleep, but his heart does not sleep?' They said, 'Yes, by Allah!' He said, 'O Allah, be Witness.' They said, 'Tell us now about your Wali among the angels, for this is when we either follow or shun you.' He said, 'My Wali (who brings down the revelation from Allah) is Jibril, and Allah never sent a Prophet, but Jibril is his Wali.' They said, 'We then shun you. Hence, if the man's is more than the woman's, the child will be male, by Allah's leave. What we are allowed in our Law is to spend in Allah's obedience from what we like and covet [but not to prohibit what Allah has allowed]. So the Jews would ask, if Islam was a revealed religion, why it was that the lawful and the unlawful were different in Islam from what had been laid down in the former revealed religions.

96.text:
"Surely the first House of worship established for humanity is the one at Bakkah" answers the boast the people of the Book had made about their place of prayer, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the House at Makkah is the first that was appointed for the worship of the one God, while the word Bakkah names the spot where the House stands. "a blessed sanctuary and a guide for all people" names what the House carries, and the sources read the blessing as the good that is placed in it and the guidance as the direction the whole creation takes from it. The verses before it had set out the way of Abraham, and this verse names the House that is joined to his name, while the verse after it names the signs in it and the pilgrimage to it. The sources also carry the names the place is given and the report that the first sanctuary built on the earth was this one, so that the claim of an older direction is turned back on its own ground. The sources also discuss whether the House was the first building of any kind or the first set apart for worship, and they leave the reader with the point the verse makes, that the standing of the House rests on its being the first appointed for the worship of God and not on the claims of any community about it.

**The first House appointed for people.**

When they said ‘Our direction of prayer qibla came before yours’ the following was revealed The first house for worship established for the people on earth was that at Bakka a variant of Makka Makkah so called because it ‘crushes’ tabukku the necks of tyrants; it was built by the angels before the creation of Adam and after it the Aqsā in Bayt al-Maqdis was built a period of forty years separating them as reported in the hadīth of the two Sahīhs sc. of al-Bukhārī and Muslim and in the hadīth that states ‘The first thing to appear on the surface of the water at the creation of the heavens and the earth was a white foam underneath which the earth was unrolled’; a blessed place mubārakan a circumstantial qualifier referring to la’lladhī ‘that’ meaning a place of blessings and a guidance to all worlds because it is their qibla. The gist of the words used in the verse is that the first House designated for people by Allah is none other than the one which is in Makkah al-Mukarramah. It means that the Ka'bah of Makkah al-Mukarramah is the first House of Worship in this world. One possible interpretation of this phrase may be that the first house of all the houses of the world was made for Divine worship exclusively, in which case, there would have been no place of worship or place of residence prior to it. Then, it is also possible that houses where people lived may have already been made earlier but this may have been the first ever House made exclusively for worship. They were told that they were the first among people and this house was the first House (of worship) appointed for people (Ibn Kathir). (Verily, the first House appointed for mankind) for all people, for their acts of worship and religious rituals. The first House built on earth for all people to worship Allah was the Sacred House of Allah in Makkah: a House of worship full of worldly and sacred blessings, and guidance for all the worlds. The first house established for the people was that at Bakka a blessed place and a guidance to all the worlds. (Lo! the first Sanctuary) mosque (appointed for mankind) for the believers (was that at Becca) where the Ka'bah is, (a blessed place) that the spot where the Ka'bah is built contains forgiveness and mercy, (a guidance to the peoples) it is a Qiblah to every prophet, messenger, veracious one (siddiq) and believer;.

**The names of Makkah and the first of the houses.**

These narrations, first of all, tell us that the Ka'bah is the first house of the world, or at least, the first house of worship. In any case, the verse under reference does prove one of the merits of the Ka'bah, that is, it is the first ever house or place of worship. Bakkah means, 'it brings Buka' (crying, weeping) to the tyrants and arrogant, meaning they cry and become humble in its vicinity. There are many names for Makkah, such as Bakkah, Al-Bayt Al-'Atiq (the Ancient House), Al-Bayt Al-Haram (the Sacred House), Al-Balad Al-Amin (the City of Safety) and Al-Ma'mun (Security). Which Masjid was the first to be built on the surface of the earth?' He said, 'Al-Masjid Al-Haram (in Makkah).' I said, 'Which was built next?' He replied 'Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa (in Bayt al-Maqdis).' I said, 'What was the period of time between building the two?' He said, 'Forty years.' He added,. (Beware! Allah made this town (Makkah) a sanctuary when He created the heavens and earth, and it is sacred by Allah's decree until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in Makkah was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was made legal for me for only a few hours or so on that day. No doubt it is at this moment a sanctuary by Allah's decree until the Day of Resurrection. It is not allowed to uproot its thorny shrubs, hunt its game, pick up its lost objects, except by announcing it, or to uproot its trees.) (In it are manifest signs)[3:97], means, clear signs that Ibrahim built the Ka'bah and that Allah has honored and blessed it. However, they do not perform Hajj to the house that Ibrahim built by Allah's command, and to which he invited the people to perform Hajj. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse .

**The House that the hearts turn to.**

It is the duty of people toward God to make the pilgrimage to the House if he is able to make his way there. The House is a bit of stone ḥajara and the servant is a bit of mud madara. It is said that the House is the object of the circumambulation of bodily selves nufūs while the Real is the object of the quest of hearts qulūb. The House consists of the remains and traces [of the past]. These are but relics and stones yet These traces of ours point to us. A House that is a place you go to seek out your loved ones and visit them mazār [or] where you hear news akhbār of them and see the traces āthār [of their having been there].

97.text:
"In it are clear signs and the standing-place of Abraham" names what the House carries for the one who looks at it, and the sources read the signs as the marks that show the House was built by Abraham by the command of God, with the station named as the stone on which he stood while he built. "Whoever enters it should be safe" states the security that belongs to the place, and the sources read the sentence as the sanctuary that God made for the town when He created the heavens and the earth. "Pilgrimage to this House is an obligation by Allah upon whoever is able among the people" turns the signs to a duty, and the sources explain the ability as the means and the provision and the ride, with the obligation placed on the one who can make the journey. "And whoever disbelieves" names the man who refuses what has been made clear, and "then surely Allah is not in need of any of His creation" closes the verse with the statement that the refusal harms no one but the one who refuses. The verses before it had named the House and its blessing, and this verse names what is required at it and what the refusal of it means. The sources dwell on the ability the verse asks for, since the duty is placed on the one who has the means to reach the House and to leave enough for those who depend on him, and they read the closing sentence as the statement that the refusal of the duty takes nothing from the Lord of the House, since the House was not built for His need but for the need of the people who come to it, and the one who stays away has only deprived himself of the good that the place carries.

**The signs and the station of Abraham.**

Therein are clear signs among which is the station of Abraham that is the stone upon which he stood to build the House and on which his footprints remain; and it the House has endured all this length of time and the constant passing of hands over it. (Wherein are plain memorials) clear signs; and it contains (the place where Abraham stood up to pray) as well as the semi-circular wall of white marble (Hatim) of Ishmael and the black stone; (and whosoever entereth it is safe) from violence. In this place of worship are clear signs of its special honour and blessings, such as the acts of worship performed in it, and its landmarks, including the stone that Abraham stood on when he was raising the walls of the Kaaba; and whoever enters it is safe, with no harm coming to them. When came the Qur'anic command: ‌ (And make the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer - 2:125), this stone was removed from there, considering the convenience of those who made tawaf, and placed in front of the Baytullah, but at some distance outside the ma-taf (the area where awaf is made) close to Bi'r Zamzam (the well of Zamzam, the original site of which is now marked with a black marble circle on the floor of the Baytullah with the legend inlaid in Arabic). (In it are manifest signs)[3:97], means, clear signs that Ibrahim built the Ka'bah and that Allah has honored and blessed it. Related in this verse are distinctions and merits of the House of Allah, that is, the Ka bah.

**The duty of the pilgrimage and the ability it asks.**

It is the duty of people towards God to make the pilgrimage to the House read either as hijj al-bayt or hajj al-bayt as two variants of the verbal noun from hajj meaning ‘the intention to journey there’ if he is able to make his way there man istatā‘a ilayhi sabīlan substitutes for al-nās ‘people’. The Prophet s explained this ability as having provisions and a ride as reported by al-Hākim al-Naysābūrī and others. Thirdly, it is obligatory on all Muslims around the world that they make the Hajj of the House of Allah, subject to the condition that one has the means and the ability to reach as far as there. Allah Almighty has made the Hajj of Baytullah an obligation subject to the condition that one has the necessary means and ability to reach there. It is also necessary that his 'means' should be good enough to cover the expenses of his family until his return, for this is an standing obligation on him. This is why Muslim jurists, have said that this is a severe warning to those who do not perform Hajj inspite of having the means and the ability to do so and thus, by this heedless act of theirs, they become the likes of disbelievers. (And to the House) going to the House (is a duty unto Allah for mankind) for the believers, (for him who can find a way thither) for the person who can walk and reach the House while at the same time being in possession of provisions, a mount and has left enough expenditure for his dependents until he returns. People have a duty to Allah to perform the acts of Hajj in this House of worship, if they are able to do so. (for those who are able to undertake the journey;)[3:97] "What does 'able to undertake the journey' mean? Who is the pilgrim?' He said, 'He who has untidy hair and clothes.' Another man asked, 'Which Hajj is better, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'The noisy (with supplication to Allah) and bloody (with sacrifice).' Another man asked, 'What is the ability to undertake the journey, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'Having provision and a means of transportation.'" This is the narration that Ibn Majah collected. It is the duty of people toward God to make the pilgrimage to the House if he is able to make his way there.

**The sanctuary and the signs that mark it.**

Among these signs are the fact that the reward for good deeds is multiplied in it and that birds never fly over it; and whoever enters it is in security not liable therein to be killed or oppressed or otherwise. (Beware! Allah made this town (Makkah) a sanctuary when He created the heavens and earth, and it is sacred by Allah's decree until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in Makkah was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was made legal for me for only a few hours or so on that day. No doubt it is at this moment a sanctuary by Allah's decree until the Day of Resurrection. It is not allowed to uproot its thorny shrubs, hunt its game, pick up its lost objects, except by announcing it, or to uproot its trees.) This is why it is forbidden to pick up pebbles lying near the Jamarat and throw them on the pillars, as part of Hajj rites, since they are from the unaccepted ones. Related in this verse are distinctions and merits of the House of Allah, that is, the Ka bah.

**The one who disbelieves and the one who is not in need.**

As for the one who disbelieves in God or in what He has made obligatory with regard to the Pilgrimage God is Independent of all worlds the humans the jinn and the angels and is Independent of their devotions. (As for him who disbelieveth) in Allah, Muhammad, the Qur'an and the obligation of pilgrimage, (Lo! Allah is Independent of creatures) He is not in need of their belief or pilgrimage. Whoever rejects the duty of Hajj disbelieves in Allah, and Allah is in no need of them or anything all in the worlds. As for the one who disbelieves God is independent of all the worlds.

**The House that the hearts visit.**

The House is a bit of stone ḥajara and the servant is a bit of mud madara. A House that is a place you go to seek out your loved ones and visit them mazār [or] where you hear news akhbār of them and see the traces āthār [of their having been there]. A House-whoever looks to it with the eye of separation returns with an innermost self laid waste kharāb. A House-whoever visits it with his bodily self finds His kindnesses and whoever visits it with his heart finds His unveilings. The first house established for the people was that at Bakka a blessed place and a guidance to all the worlds.

98.text:
"Say, O Prophet" opens the verse with the command to put the question, and the question is carried to the same people the passage has been addressing. "O People of the Book" names the two communities who hold the earlier books, and the sources read the address as the last of the admonitions given to them. "Why do you deny the revelations of Allah" names the charge, and the sources read it as the refusal of the clear verses and of the messenger they had been told about. "when Allah is a Witness to what you do" closes the verse with the knowledge that watches them, and the sources read the sentence as the warning that nothing of their blocking is hidden and that the requital will follow. The verse before it had set the House and the pilgrimage before the people of the Book, and this verse turns from the House to the hearts that refuse the proofs, while the verse after it names the road they block for others.

**The People of the Book addressed again.**

Now once again, the people of the Book are the addressees. Here, the verses begin with an admonition to the people of the Book who had engineered this in triage, and this admonition has been done with great eloquence when, before admonishing them for what they did, they were taken to task for their disbelief as well, which meant that it would have made better sense if they themselves had taken to the right path, and become Muslims, rather than devoting themselves to distract others to the wrong track. The expression ,'translated as 'And whoever holds on to Allah' means one who stays firm in, and totally committed to, his 'iman or faith, for 'i tisam', the act of holding on to Allah firmly, denotes that one should affirm His Being and His Attributes, be staunchly faithful to what He has ordained, and in the process, be sure not to be lured into supporting the position of any adversary whoever that may be. Chastising the People of the Book for Their Disbelief and Blocking the Path of Allah. When the call of truth comes in all its purity, the interests of those who contrived to convince others that their self-styled religion had indeed been revealed by God are put at risk. People serving their own interests oppose the new messenger by raising different kinds of objections based on fallacies in order to turn others away from the true message. Virtue, however, hinges upon the making of sacrifices and not on the mere fact of opting for a religious form. O Prophet, ask the People of the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians, why they reject the proof of the truth of your prophet-hood, including the proofs that came in the Torah and the Gospel, when Allah watches over everything you do, witnessing it, and will reward you accordingly.

**The verses that are denied and the witness over them.**

Why do you reject the Ayat of Allah, while Allah is Witness to what you do? In this Ayah Allah criticizes the disbelieving People of the Book for refusing the truth, rejecting Allah's Ayat and hindering those who seek to believe from His path, although they know that what the Messenger was sent with is the truth from Allah. (Say: O People of the Scripture! Why disbelieve ye in the revelations of Allah) i.e. in Muhammad and the Qur'an, (when Allah (Himself) is Witness of what ye do) of disbelief, by concealing [the Truth] and engaging in sins? O people of the scripture why do you disbelieve in God's verses when God is witness of what you doḍ The divine address in this verse is meant to confirm the obligation of the pilgrimage [for the people of the scripture]. Say ‘O People of the Scripture why do you disbelieve in God’s verses that is the Qur’ān when God is Witness of what you do?’ and will requite you for it?

**The law, the decree, and the witness over them.**

With respect to the law the pilgrimage is obligatory for them166 but with respect to the true state of affairs ḥaqīqa and [divine] subjugation qahr the pilgrimage is barred to them. They are called by the law and command hum madʿuwūna sharʿan wa-amran but banished by the decree and the subjugation maṬrūdūna ḥukman wa-qahran. Allah has warned the People of the Book against this behavior, stating that He is Witness over what they do, indicating their defiance of the knowledge conveyed to them by the Prophets. Why do you reject the Ayat of Allah, while Allah is Witness to what you do? When the Holy Prophet heard about this, he came to them and said: 'What is all this? But they would show no interest in making their daily activities God-oriented.

99.text:
"Say, O People of the Book" opens the verse by turning the address back to the two communities who hold the earlier books, and the question that follows is about the road they block for others. "Why do you turn the believers away from the Way of Allah" names the charge, and the sources read it as the barring of those who have accepted the truth from the religion of God, so that the harm is done not to the message but to the people who would walk in it. "striving to make it appear crooked" names the means, and the sources read it as the attempt to bend the road so that it no longer looks straight to the one who is looking for it, with the bending done by argument and by the pulling away of the heart. "while you are witnesses to its truth" names the knowledge the barrers themselves carry, and the sources read it as the witness of their own books that the messenger had come, which is what makes the charge heavy, since a man who knows a thing and hides it is not as a man who is ignorant of it. "And Allah is never unaware of what you do" closes the verse with the knowledge that keeps everything, and the sources read it as the warning that no part of their blocking is hidden and that the requital will follow, with the respite given only until the appointed time. The verse before it named the House and the pilgrimage, and this verse turns to the hearts that keep others from the road, while the verse after it warns the believers against yielding to them.

**The believers who are turned away.**

Say ‘O People of the Scripture why do you bar believers causing them to turn away from God’s way His religion by denying the truth of the Prophet and concealing His graces desiring to make it crooked ‘iwajan is the verbal noun meaning mu‘awwajatan ‘made crooked’ inclining away from the truth while you yourselves are witnesses while you know that the religion which is upright and pleasing to God is that of Islam as stated in your Book? (Say: O People of the Scripture! Why drive ye back believers) in Allah, Muhammad and the Qur'an (from the way of Allah) from the Religion of Allah and His worship, (seeking to make it crooked, when you are witnesses?) when you know it to be in the Scripture. Why do you stop those who have believed, from the path of Allah, seeking to make it seem crooked, while you (yourselves) are witnesses? O Prophet, ask the People of the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians, why they stop people who have faith from the Religion of Allah, wanting to twist it from the truth to falsehood, and turning its people from guidance to misguidance, when they witness that it is the truth confirming what is in their scriptures. Here, the verses begin with an admonition to the people of the Book who had engineered this in triage, and this admonition has been done with great eloquence when, before admonishing them for what they did, they were taken to task for their disbelief as well, which meant that it would have made better sense if they themselves had taken to the right path, and become Muslims, rather than devoting themselves to distract others to the wrong track. Following this, Muslims have been addressed, and served with a word of caution, especially when they have by their side, the Book and the Messenger of Allah, two powerful, never-failing sources, which would help them stay firm in their belief.

**The truth they deny while they are witnesses.**

In this Ayah Allah criticizes the disbelieving People of the Book for refusing the truth, rejecting Allah's Ayat and hindering those who seek to believe from His path, although they know that what the Messenger was sent with is the truth from Allah. Allah has warned the People of the Book against this behavior, stating that He is Witness over what they do, indicating their defiance of the knowledge conveyed to them by the Prophets. They rejected, denied and refused the very Messenger whom they were ordered to convey the glad tidings about his coming. Why do you reject the Ayat of Allah, while Allah is Witness to what you do?

**The interests that fight against the call.**

When the call of truth comes in all its purity, the interests of those who contrived to convince others that their self-styled religion had indeed been revealed by God are put at risk. People serving their own interests oppose the new messenger by raising different kinds of objections based on fallacies in order to turn others away from the true message. For example, they would shun rabbit’s meat, saying that it was not consumed by their saints, although along with this, many illegal things would have been legalized by them. They would consider it of the utmost importance to face exactly in the direction of al-Bayt al-Maqdis, like a compass needle pointing to the pole. Virtue, however, hinges upon the making of sacrifices and not on the mere fact of opting for a religious form. God’s true servant is one who offers his Lord the gift of love, and for whom no material thing is dearer than God. He is ever ready to pay the price of losing his prestige by recognizing the truth; he is ever ready to spend his wealth for the cause of God. They learned this from the previous Prophets and honorable Messengers, may Allah's peace and blessings be on them all. They all brought the glad tidings and the good news of the coming of the unlettered, Arab, Hashimi Prophet from Makkah, the master of the Children of Adam, the Final Prophet and the Messenger of the Lord of heavens and earth. The expression ,'translated as 'And whoever holds on to Allah' means one who stays firm in, and totally committed to, his 'iman or faith, for 'i tisam', the act of holding on to Allah firmly, denotes that one should affirm His Being and His Attributes, be staunchly faithful to what He has ordained, and in the process, be sure not to be lured into supporting the position of any adversary whoever that may be. It means that such a person is on the 'straight path', and being on the 'straight path' is the key to all that is good and beneficial which the Word of Allah promises to him. Several verses earlier, the text was dealing with the people of the Book, their false beliefs and their doubts. Now once again, the people of the Book are the addressees. This event appears in Ruh al-Ma'ani as narrated by Ibn Ishaq while there are others who narrate it from Zaid ibn Aslam. How can one who is barred himself bar anotherḍ Surely in this is a secret belonging to the [divine] Lordship.

**The warning that is never unaware.**

(Allah is not unaware of what ye do) Allah is not oblivious to your disbelief: concealing the Truth and committing transgressions. Allah states that He is never unaware of what they do, and He will hold them responsible for their actions,. Allah is not unaware of what they do in disbelieving it and preventing people from following it; and they will be repaid accordingly. God is not heedless of what you do’ in the way of unbelief and mendacity; instead He gives you respite until your appointed time and then requites you.

100.text:
"O believers, If you were to yield to a group of those who were given the Scripture" names the danger that comes from trust placed in the wrong quarter, and the sources read the verse as the caution given to the Muslims when the people of the Book were working among them. The address is to those who have accepted the truth, and it names a group within the other communities and not the whole of them, so that the caution is aimed at a manner of following and not at a people as such. "they would turn you back from belief to disbelief" states what follows from that yielding, and the sources read it as the turning of the heart away from the road it had found, since the ones who lead a man back do not do it by argument alone but by the weight of companionship and the pull of old bonds. The verse before it had named those who keep the believers from the way, and this verse shows what their keeping looks like when it succeeds, while the verse after it asks how a man who has the verses recited to him and the messenger among him could come to that.

**The disbelief that is far from them.**

Here, the verses begin with an admonition to the people of the Book who had engineered this in triage, and this admonition has been done with great eloquence when, before admonishing them for what they did, they were taken to task for their disbelief as well, which meant that it would have made better sense if they themselves had taken to the right path, and become Muslims, rather than devoting themselves to distract others to the wrong track. (And how would you disbelieve, while unto you are recited the verses of Allah, and among you is His Messenger?), meaning, disbelief is far from touching you, since the Ayat of Allah are being sent down on His Messenger day and night, and he recites and conveys them to you. Following this, Muslims have been addressed, and served with a word of caution, especially when they have by their side, the Book and the Messenger of Allah, two powerful, never-failing sources, which would help them stay firm in their belief. ("Who among the faithful believers do you consider has the most amazing faith?" They said, "The angels." He said, "Why would they not believe, since they are with their Lord?" They mentioned the Prophets, and the Prophet said, "Why would they not believe while the revelation is sent down to them?" They said, "Then, we are." He said, "Why would not you believe when I am among you?" They asked, "Who has the most amazing faith?" The Prophet said, "A people who will come after you and who will find only books that they will believe in.")

**The turning away and the disbelief it leads to.**

So there is always the possibility of Satan’s succeeding in turning one from belief to unbelief. Any turning away from this path occurs when certain parts of the religion are modified in order to change the order of priorities, e.g. what is important is relegated to a secondary place, and vice versa. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, if you follow a group of the People of the Scripture, from the Jews or the Christians, in what they say, and accept their opinion in what they claim, then you will return to disbelief after your faith because of their envy and their misguidance. (O ye who believe! If ye obey a party of those who have received the Scripture) the Torah (they will make you disbelievers) in Allah and Muhammad (after your belief) in Allah and [the message of] Muhammad. Estrangement is not restricted to just the estranged but also extends to anyone who becomes part of their circle. Whoever follows the enemy of God into this ruinous companionship will be cast down to the same level.

**The event among the Aws and the Khazraj.**

The following was revealed when the Jews passed by the Aws and the Khazraj and were infuriated by their comradeship and set about reminding them of their mutual hostility in the days before Islam such that they caused them to quarrel and the two tribes were on the verge of fighting one another O you who believe if you obey a party of those who have been given the Scripture they will turn you after you have believed into disbelievers. One day, he passed by a group of Companions of the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, from the Aws and the Khazraj who were gathered in an assembly and talking, and was infuriated to see their unity, friendliness and reconciliation when they were enemies in the pre-Islamic period. When they heard his voice, they stopped talking and listened to him.

101.text:
"How can you disbelieve when Allah's revelations are recited to you and His Messenger is in your midst" opens the verse with a question that is meant to amaze the hearer, and the sources read it as an address of amazement and rebuke rather than a request for news, since the two things the question names are the strongest support a people could be given. The verses are heard from the mouth of the reciter, and the messenger is present among them to make them clear, so that the question asks how a people could turn away when the road is being shown to them by both the book and the man. "Whoever holds firmly to Allah is surely guided to the Straight Path" closes the verse with the answer, and the sources read the holding firmly as a staying with the religion, a clinging to the book and the covenant, with the guidance named as the path that leads straight to God. The verse before it had named the road that leads back to disbelief, and this verse shows the two things that stand against it, while the verse after it lays the duty of watchfulness on the believers, and the sources carry the account of the quarrel between the two tribes of Madīnah that the address answered, when the old enmity was raised again among them and the words of the book were sent down to end it. The sources also bring out the shape of the address, since the wonder is that a people who have been given the book and the messenger should turn away while the recitation is in their ears and the one who brings it is among them, and the two tribes had already been led to the edge of war before the words reached them and turned them back to one another.

**How can you disbelieve when the verses are recited.**

This is mentioned by way of amazement, (when it is ye unto whom Allah's revelations) the Qur'an containing commands and prohibitions (are recited, and His messenger) Muhammad (is in your midst?) with you. The verses of Allah are being recited to you, and the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ is making them clear to you. (And how would you disbelieve, while unto you are recited the verses of Allah, and among you is His Messenger?), meaning, disbelief is far from touching you, since the Ayat of Allah are being sent down on His Messenger day and night, and he recites and conveys them to you. How could you disbelieve in Allah after you have had faith in Him, especially when you have the biggest reason for having firm faith with you? How can you disbelieve this is an interrogative of amazement and rebuke while you have God’s verses recited to you and His Messenger is in your midst?

**The Messenger in their midst.**

Following this, Muslims have been addressed, and served with a word of caution, especially when they have by their side, the Book and the Messenger of Allah, two powerful, never-failing sources, which would help them stay firm in their belief. When the Holy Prophet heard about this, he came to them and said: 'What is all this? Upon being informed of what was happening, the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, went to them and this verse was revealed (How can ye disbelieve, when it is ye unto whom Allah's revelations are recited, and His messenger is in your midst?) up to His saying (And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate) [3:103] . ("Who among the faithful believers do you consider has the most amazing faith?" They said, "The angels." He said, "Why would they not believe, since they are with their Lord?" They mentioned the Prophets, and the Prophet said, "Why would they not believe while the revelation is sent down to them?" They said, "Then, we are." He said, "Why would not you believe when I am among you?" They asked, "Who has the most amazing faith?"
