The Prophet said, "A people who will come after you and who will find only books that they will believe in.")

**The one who holds firmly to Allah is guided to the straight path.**

(He who holdeth fast to Allah) he who adheres to Allah's Religion and His Book, (he indeed is guided unto a right path) he is directed along a clear, solid way, which is Islam; it is also said this means: he has become firm on this way. And whoever depends upon Allah, then he is indeed guided to the right path. The one who holds fast to God has [in truth] only found the holding fast from God. How could those who have not been guided by God hold fast to Godḍ The guidance from Him in the beginning bidāya causes you [to] hold fast in the end nihāya. Your holding fast does not cause the guidance hidāya. Whoever holds fast to Him through himself -without being effaced from his own strength and power in his holding-his homeland is idolatry shirk but he is unaware. The expression ,'translated as 'And whoever holds on to Allah' means one who stays firm in, and totally committed to, his 'iman or faith, for 'i tisam', the act of holding on to Allah firmly, denotes that one should affirm His Being and His Attributes, be staunchly faithful to what He has ordained, and in the process, be sure not to be lured into supporting the position of any adversary whoever that may be. It means that such a person is on the 'straight path', and being on the 'straight path' is the key to all that is good and beneficial which the Word of Allah promises to him.

**The warning against obeying the people of the Book.**

Here, the verses begin with an admonition to the people of the Book who had engineered this in triage, and this admonition has been done with great eloquence when, before admonishing them for what they did, they were taken to task for their disbelief as well, which meant that it would have made better sense if they themselves had taken to the right path, and become Muslims, rather than devoting themselves to distract others to the wrong track. Allah warns His believing servants against obeying the People of the Book, who envy the believers for the favor that Allah gave them by sending His Messenger . Warning Muslims Against Imitating People of the Scriptures.

**The verse that was revealed when they almost fought.**

Upon being informed of what was happening, the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, went to them and this verse was revealed (How can ye disbelieve, when it is ye unto whom Allah's revelations are recited, and His messenger is in your midst?) up to His saying (And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate) [3:103] . Then the verse (How can ye disbelieve, when it is ye unto whom Allah's revelations are recited) up to His saying (He did save you from it) . The Aws and the Khazraj had a feud in the pre-Islamic period. One day, they mentioned to each other what had happened in that period and this led them to brandish their swords at each others. The Aws and the Khazraj were one day talking and became angry with each other to the extent that war nearly broke out between them. That is why it is always necessary for man to be cautious: he must become his own keeper. Any turning away from this path occurs when certain parts of the religion are modified in order to change the order of priorities, e.g. what is important is relegated to a secondary place, and vice versa. Such deviation mostly occurs when some secondary aspect is taken to be a fundamental part of religion and is stressed in a manner which should be reserved for the fear of God and concern for the Hereafter. This verse was revealed about Mu'adh [Ibn Jabal] and his companions.

**The deviation that brings disunity.**

Any turning away from this path occurs when certain parts of the religion are modified in order to change the order of priorities, e.g. what is important is relegated to a secondary place, and vice versa. Such deviation mostly occurs when some secondary aspect is taken to be a fundamental part of religion and is stressed in a manner which should be reserved for the fear of God and concern for the Hereafter. When peripheral issues are thus given importance, the upshot is disunity—and this is what brings on all the evils that push man to the brink of Hell. It must be conceded that it is only when all of the emphasis is on taqwa that unity is a natural consequence.

102.text:
"O believers, Be mindful of Allah in the way He deserves" opens the verse with the duty that is placed first, and the sources read the wording as the fear that gives God what His greatness asks, so that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not met with ingratitude. The sources also notice how heavy the command was taken to be by the first hearers, and how the later wording of the book lightened what could not be carried, so that the duty stays within what a person is able to give. "and do not die except in a state of full submission to Him" closes the verse with the manner of the ending, and the sources read it as the keeping of the faith while a person is well and safe, so that the state he lives in is the state he goes out on, since the Most Generous has decided that a man dies upon what he lived upon, and the sources draw the warning from it that the state a man goes out on is the state he is raised upon. The verse before it had named the verses recited and the messenger in the midst, and this verse turns those gifts into a rule of life, while the verse after it names the bond that keeps the community together, and the sources carry the account of the two tribes whose enmity that bond ended.

**The duty of fear that is His due.**

(O ye who believe! Observe your duty to Allah) obey Allah (with right observance) such that one obeys Him and never contravenes against Him, thank Him and never be ungrateful to him, remember Him and never forget Him; it is also said this means: obey Allah as He ought to be obeyed, (and die not save as those who have surrendered (unto Him) sincerely acknowledging that you worship Him and declare His divine Oneness;. O you who believe fear God as He should be feared so that He is obeyed and not disobeyed thanked and not shown ingratitude remembered and not forgotten. O you who have faith, be wary of God as is the rightful due of His wariness. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Messenger, be mindful of Allah as you have been commanded, by following what He instructs you to do, and by staying away from what He prohibits you from doing; and be thankful for His favour, holding firmly to the religion He has given you, so that when you die, you die surrendering in devotion to Him. In the previous verses, Muslims were warned that the people of the Book, and others, want them to go astray from the right path so Muslims must remain vigilant of their moves and take steps to counter their anti-Muslim activities. When He says, "O people," He says, "Be wary of your Lord" along with it. Their godwariness is based on seeing blessings, and their aspiration is nurturing the body to serve the Real.

**Do not die except as one who has surrendered.**

(and die not except as (true) Muslims)[3:102], means, preserve your Islam while you are well and safe, so that you die as a Muslim. The Most Generous Allah has made it His decision that whatever state one lives in, that is what he dies upon and is resurrected upon. (Have Taqwa of Allah as is His due, die not except as (true) Muslims.)[3:102], [then he said;]. ’ But it was then abrogated by His statement So fear God as much as you can Q. 6416; and do not die except as Muslims professing the Oneness of God.

**The fear of God that the religion rests on.**

The actual mainspring of religion is fear of God (taqwa), that is, adopting till one’s dying day an unshakeable sense of accountability to God for all of one’s actions. While an attitude inspired by the fear of God (taqwa) focuses all attention on the one and only God, in the absence of such fear, it is purely trivial matters which are thrust to the forefront. Such deviation mostly occurs when some secondary aspect is taken to be a fundamental part of religion and is stressed in a manner which should be reserved for the fear of God and concern for the Hereafter. Whenever such alterations are made in a religion, it necessarily results in differences which lead to serious schisms, with one group stressing one particular secondary aspect and another group stressing another particular secondary aspect—all of which culminates in the community splitting up into a number of sects. Then, while in this state—devoid of the true spirit of faith—one’s time of departure from this world might come, making it almost impossible for one to make amends. That is why it is always necessary for man to be cautious: he must become his own keeper.

**The watch kept over the right path.**

In the previous verses, Muslims were warned that the people of the Book, and others, want them to go astray from the right path so Muslims must remain vigilant of their moves and take steps to counter their anti-Muslim activities. In the two verses appearing here, two important principles have been given which go to "Pregnable. Any turning away from this path occurs when certain parts of the religion are modified in order to change the order of priorities, e.g. what is important is relegated to a secondary place, and vice versa. Here, man is forever exposed to Satan’s evil temptations. So there is always the possibility of Satan’s succeeding in turning one from belief to unbelief. " This is what he said, but it appears that it is only a statement of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, and Allah knows best.

**The brothers united by Allah.**

(It pleases Allah for you to acquire three qualities and displeases Him that you acquire three characteristics. It pleases Him that you worship Him Alone and not associate anything or anyone with Him in worship, that you hold on to the Rope of Allah altogether and do not divide, and that you advise whoever Allah appoints as your Leader. The three that displease Him are that you say, 'It was said,' and, 'So-and-so said,' asking many unnecessary questions and wasting money.) When Allah brought Islam, those among them who embraced it became brothers who loved each other by Allah's grace, having good ties for Allah's sake and helping each other in righteousness and piety. (He it is Who has supported you with His Help and with the believers. And He has united their hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them)[8:62-63], until the end of the Ayah. (O Ansar! Did I not find you misguided and Allah directed you to guidance because of me? Were you not divided beforehand and Allah united you around me? Were you not poor and Allah enriched you because of me?) (to the Rope of Allah) refers to Allah's covenant, just as Allah said in the following Ayah,.

103.text:
"And hold firmly to the rope of Allah and do not be divided, Remember Allah's favour upon you when you were enemies" opens the verse with the bond and the command that keeps the community one, and the sources read the rope as the religion and the book, with the holding done together so that the hand of one strengthens the hand of another and the scattering that follows from parting is refused. "then He united your hearts, so you by His grace, became brothers" names the change that the bond worked, and the sources read the uniting of the hearts as a work that no spending of the earth's wealth could have bought. "And you were at the brink of a fiery pit and He saved you from it" names the danger that stood behind them, and the sources read it as the state of enmity and disbelief out of which Islam delivered them, so that the rescue is named as the whole of the favour. "This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you" names the purpose of the explanation, and "so that you may be rightly guided" closes the verse with the end that the clear words are meant to serve. The verses before it had placed the duty of watchfulness on the believers, and this verse names the bond that makes the duty possible, while the sources carry the account of the two tribes of Madīnah whose quarrel the verse addresses, and they read the fear of God as the root that keeps the bond from breaking, since the bond is kept by hearts that answer to one Lord and is broken by hearts that follow a hundred small lords. The verse is one of the longest of the passage for that reason, because it gathers the bond, the memory of the favour, the change that the favour worked, and the clear words that were given so that the guided would stay guided. The sources also join the two halves of the verse, since the favour that is remembered is the same favour that saved them, and the guidance that is named at the end is the end the whole passage works toward, so that the mercy of God is set before them as both the reason for the bond and the road the bond leads along.

**Hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not divide.**

(And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah) hold fast to the Religion of Allah and His Book, (and do not separate) in religion. Hold tightly, O you who have faith, to the Book and the traditions of the Prophet, and do not do that which will bring division amongst you. And hold fast to clutch God’s bond namely His religion together and do not scatter after submitting to Islam; remember God’s grace His bestowing of favours upon you O companies of the Aws and the Khazraj when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together through Islam so that by His grace you became brothers in religion and comradeship; and you were upon the brink the edge of a pit of fire such that to fall into it you only had to die disbelieving; but He delivered you from it through belief. This [comes] from confirm ing what is true and right taḥaqquq and remaining devoted taʿalluq to the Book and the sunna. It is rightly said that [the words] and hold fast to God's bond are spoken to the elite khawāṣṣ while [the words] and hold fast to God [4:146 and 22:78] are spoken to the elect of the elect khāṣṣ al-khāṣṣ. This is why all groups and parties around the world invariably ask people to unite, but experience shows that all is not well in world affairs. " This is what he said, but it appears that it is only a statement of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, and Allah knows best.

**The enemies whose hearts were brought together.**

(how ye were enemies) before Islam (and He made friendship between your hearts) through Islam (so that ye became as brothers by His grace) by His religion, Islam; (and ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire) i.e. because of disbelief, (and He did save you from it) by means of faith. Remember the blessings of Allah upon you when you were enemies before Islam, fighting each other for the slightest reason, and He brought your hearts together through Islam, so that you became brothers in your faith through His grace, showing each other love and respect and listening to each other’s advice. They were enemies when they remained with their worldly concerns turning toward the narrowness of human nature and competing with one another as befits the stinginess of [their] lower selves. And He brought your hearts together through deliverance from the cap tivity of created things. (He it is Who has supported you with His Help and with the believers. And He has united their hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them)[8:62-63], until the end of the Ayah. Before Islam, their disbelief had them standing at the edge of a pit of the Fire, but Allah saved them from it and delivered them to faith.

**The brothers brought together by His grace.**

(how ye were enemies) before Islam (and He made friendship between your hearts) through Islam (so that ye became as brothers by His grace) by His religion, Islam; (and ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire) i.e. because of disbelief, (and He did save you from it) by means of faith. Remember the blessings of Allah upon you when you were enemies before Islam, fighting each other for the slightest reason, and He brought your hearts together through Islam, so that you became brothers in your faith through His grace, showing each other love and respect and listening to each other’s advice. And hold fast to God's bond together and do not scatter; remember God's grace upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together so that by His grace you became brothers; and you were upon the brink of a pit of fire; but He delivered you from it. His grace is His safeguard ing ʿiṣma of you as brothers united in aim and aspiration annihilated from the worldly concerns of the lower self and the furtive impulses of stinginess and avarice. When they accepted Islam, all hostilities ended: they became like brothers. And hold fast to clutch God’s bond namely His religion together and do not scatter after submitting to Islam; remember God’s grace His bestowing of favours upon you O companies of the Aws and the Khazraj when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together through Islam so that by His grace you became brothers in religion and comradeship; and you were upon the brink the edge of a pit of fire such that to fall into it you only had to die disbelieving; but He delivered you from it through belief.

**The brink of the fire and the rescue.**

Before that you were on the brink of entering the fire of Hell because of your disbelief. Allah saved you from the fire of Hell through Islam and guided you to faith. And you were upon the brink of a pit of fire by your being held captive to the objects of your desire munākum and [being] bound by the shackles of your worldly concerns and whims hawākum. And hold fast to clutch God’s bond namely His religion together and do not scatter after submitting to Islam; remember God’s grace His bestowing of favours upon you O companies of the Aws and the Khazraj when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together through Islam so that by His grace you became brothers in religion and comradeship; and you were upon the brink the edge of a pit of fire such that to fall into it you only had to die disbelieving; but He delivered you from it through belief. Both were Arabs, but they continuously waged war against each other. The reason for this is that one who denies the truth is faithful only to his own self, while a believer gives his allegiance solely to God. All being bound by one and the same cord, mutual clashes and strife cease altogether.

**The verses made clear so that you may be guided.**

(Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations) His commands, prohibitions and favours (unto you, that haply ye may be guided) from error. In the way that Allah has made this clear to you, He also makes clear to you what will put things right for you in this world and the Afterlife, so that you are guided to the right way of life. So just as He has made clear for you what has been mentioned God makes clear to you His signs that you might be guided. The first principle stated in the said verse is that one must 'fear Allah', that is, one should organize and manage his life with a full sense of responsibility before Allah, avoiding all that is forbidden or undesirable, doing so in a manner 'which is His due'. It is translated as 'fear' in the sense that things one is asked to abstain from are nothing but things that cause fear, or alert one to the danger of Divine retribution. 'A fear which is His due' means that one obeys, then does not disobey; remembers then does not forget; and is grateful, then does not become ungrateful.' (Al-Bahr Al-Muhit) For instance, some say that the due fear of Allah means that, in obedience to Allah, one should dismiss all derogatory criticism, no matter where it comes from, always standing firm on what is just, even if, by being just, he has to hurt his own self, or his children, or his parents.

**Taqwa and dying as a Muslim.**

(and let not yourself die save as Muslims) tells us that Taqwa is, in reality, the whole of Islam since the total obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and the total avoidance of disobedience both to Allah and His Messenger is what Taqwa is all about; and this is what Islam is. (and die not except as (true) Muslims)[3:102], means, preserve your Islam while you are well and safe, so that you die as a Muslim. The Most Generous Allah has made it His decision that whatever state one lives in, that is what he dies upon and is resurrected upon. At several places in the Holy Qur'an, the words, 'Muttaqin' (plural of Muttaqi and 'Taqwa ' have been used in that sense as well. What is really desirable falls under the second degree of Taqwa , that is, to avoid that which is disliked by Allah and His Messenger. The merits and blessings of Taqwa enumerated in the Qur'an and Iiadith have been promised on this degree of avoidance and abstinence. Leaving this wider focus aside, we can turn to the first and present addressees of the Qur'an, the Muslims who believe that in the world as we have found it, the Holy Qur'an is the only way of life revealed by Allah Almighty without any shadow of doubt in it, and since Allah Almighty has Himself taken the responsibility of protecting it, there is just no possibility of interpolation or change in it right through to the Day of Judgment.

104.text:
"Let there be a group among you who call others to goodness" opens the verse with the command that a body of people should carry the work of calling, and the sources read the group as a band set apart within the community for the task, so that the duty is not left to drift. "encourage what is good" names the first half of the work, and the sources read the good as what the law has named fair and the people have learned to recognize, with the calling done by speech and by example and by the patience that the work asks for. "and forbid what is evil" names the second half, and the sources read the evil as what the law refuses, with the forbidding done in the manner the command was given, since a hand raised out of anger is not the work the verse asks for. "it is they who will be successful" closes the verse with the promise, and the sources read the success as the state of those who are saved from the wrath of God and from the punishment. The verses before it had told the believers to hold the rope of God and not divide, and this verse names the work that keeps the bond alive, while the verse after it warns against becoming like the communities that split after the clear proofs had come, and the sources read the place of the group as a duty that stands in the community, since the verses that follow warn a people that split and broke the bond.

**The group that is raised for the call.**

Let there be one community of you calling to good to Islam and enjoining decency and forbidding indecency; those that call bid and forbid are the successful the victorious the particle min ‘of’ in minkum ‘of you’ is partitive since what is mentioned is a collective obligation fard kifāya and is not incumbent upon every individual of the community for not every person such as the ignorant is up to it. Let there arise out of you a group of people inviting to all that is good (Islam), enjoining Al-Ma'ruf (all that Islam orders) and forbidding Al-Munkar (all that Islam has forbidden). (And there may spring from you) there still exists among you (a nation) a group (who invite to goodness) who invite to reconciliation and excellence, (and enjoin right conduct) they enjoin Allah's divine Oneness and the following of Muhammad ﷺ (and forbid indecency) they forbid disbelief, idolatry and rejection, instead following the Messenger. Let there be from you, O believers, a group who calls to all that is good and loved by Allah, instructing people to do what is right from the sacred law and from what you know to be good and just; and forbidding what is wrong, which is prohibited by the sacred law and which you know to be wrong and unjust. The first part of the verse' translated as (And there has to be a group of people from among you) gives a hint that the presence of this group is necessary. The objective of this Ayah is that there should be a segment of this Muslim Ummah fulfilling this task, even though it is also an obligation on every member of this Ummah, each according to his ability. Let there be a community of you inviting to the good.

**Enjoining what is fair and forbidding what is unfair.**

The nature of this obligation requires that one bid the Fair and forbid the Unfair in what is necessary; this would be obligatory. It is common sight these days that people tend to object in case of what is commendable or indifferent rather strongly, but remain silent when people abandon what is obligatory. When it sees people less inclined towards what is good, or sees them indulging in evils, it should not fall short of pointing out what is good and preventing people from taking to the evil, of course, according to its ability. that calls to righteousness, enjoins all that is good and forbids evil in the manner Allah commanded,. (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! You will enjoin righteousness and forbid evil, or Allah shall send down a punishment from Him to you. Then, you will supplicate to Him, but He will not accept your supplication.) The educated should be strenuous in their efforts to enjoin goodness and forbid wrong in the community. Their keen awareness of the need for reform should ensure their continuing concern with the state of the people: they must encourage everyone to follow the path of goodness and shun the path of evil. However, for such an effort to succeed, the public must be submissive; they must be willing to listen to their elders. They must show respect for them, follow them as they are bid and stop where they are told to stop, thus surrendering themselves to their religious reformers. In short, elders motivated by the true religious spirit, should never shirk their responsibility towards their community of enjoining goodness upon them and forbidding evil. This is because each individual from among these blessed souls considered himself personally charged with the responsibility of calling people to good.. The Holy Qur'an could have used the word 'wajib' (what is obligating) instead of 'ma ruf, and the word 'ma asi (sins) instead of 'munkar'., but it did not do so.

**The obligation that rests on the community.**

In order that Muslims have a firm bond of unity, they must relate to Allah, and in order that this bond stays firm through the ages, it is necessary that Muslims consider it their obligation to enjoin what is good in accordance with the dictates of the Qur'an and the Sunnah on their brothers and sisters in faith, and to stop them from what is not good. Ad-Dahhak said, "They are a special group of the Companions and a special group of those after them, that is those who perform Jihad and the scholars." (The People of the Two Scriptures divided into seventy-two sects. This Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one, that is, the Jama'ah. Some of my Ummah will be guided by desire, like one who is infected by rabies; no vein or joint will be saved from these desires.) This command pertains, on the one hand, to the common man and on the other to the intellectuals and the educated class. A Muslim community’s success thus depends respectively upon the attitudes of the religious elders and of the public.

**Those who will be successful.**

However it is also said that this particle is extra and what is meant is ‘so that you are a community calling to good and so on’. (Such are they who are successful) who are saved from Allah's wrath and punishment. The people who do this will have complete success in this world and the Afterlife. (And for those whose faces will become white, they will be in Allah's mercy (Paradise), therein they shall dwell forever.) in Paradise, where they will reside for eternity and shall never desire to be removed. They are not taken aback by the blame of any blamer nor cut off from God by relying on any causes. They have seen the shortcomings of their own souls and immersed their lives in gaining God's approval. They act for God, give counsel for God's religion, and call God's creatures to God. They know God, they call upon God, and they strive in God's religion. Others look from the artisanry to the Artisan, but they look from the Artisan to the artisanry.

105.text:
"And do not be like those who split into sects and differed after clear proofs had come to them" opens the verse with the warning that draws its force from the history of the communities that had the books before, and the sources read the split as the scattering of a people who were one and the dispute as the quarrel that followed, with the proofs already in their hands. What makes the warning heavy is the order of the two things, since the division came after the clear words and not before them, so that no one could plead ignorance. "It is they who will suffer a tremendous punishment" closes the verse with the end of the matter, and the sources read the punishment as the state the quarrel brought upon them, a disagreement that turned into a chastening. The verse before it had named the group that calls to good and turns from evil, and this verse names the road that leads away from that work, while the verses after it show the day on which the difference between the two roads will be seen on the faces of the people, so that the warning against division stands on the history of the communities that had the book before. The sources also follow the argument over the disputing of branches, and they read the ruin of a community as coming from the moment when the small things are lifted above the great.

**The division that came after the clear proofs.**

Be not as those who scattered in their religion and disputed over it after the clear proofs came to them and these are the Jews and the Christians those there awaits a mighty chastisement. It means that Muslims should not be like Jews and Christians who, even after clear injunctions of Allah Almighty had reached them, became divided in the implementation of the basic code of faith simply because they preferred to follow the dictates of their desires. After that, by saying ‌ (and be not divided) in verse 103 and ‌ ; (And do not be like those who became divided) in the present verse, Muslims have been asked to learn a lesson from past communities which were destroyed by mutual dissensions with the good counsel that they should do their best to stay safe against this disease. (And be ye not) divided in religion (as those who separated and disputed) in religion, such as the religious schisms that took place among the Jews and Christians (after the clear proofs) proofs from their Scriptures of Islam (had come unto them. For such) i.e. the Jews and Christians (there is an awful doom) greater than anything one can imagine. Do not be, O believers, like the People of the Scripture who became divided into different groups and divisions, disagreeing about their faith and way of life after clear signs had come to them from Allah. The statement after clear signs had come to them' is an obvious indicator towards this explanation. And do not be like those who became dispersed and disagreed.

**The dispute that brought the punishment.**

Thus, thrown in violent mutual disputations, vocal and physical, they brought Divine punishment upon themselves. This verse is, in fact, a complement of 103) where Muslims were asked to seek unity and strength by attaching themselves to Allah's commands, individually and collectively, which helps make an entire community act like one body, one person, one entity. Such people will have a great punishment from Allah. (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! You will enjoin righteousness and forbid evil, or Allah shall send down a punishment from Him to you. Then, you will supplicate to Him, but He will not accept your supplication.) (The People of the Two Scriptures divided into seventy-two sects. This Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one, that is, the Jama'ah. Some of my Ummah will be guided by desire, like one who is infected by rabies; no vein or joint will be saved from these desires.) This is when the faces of followers of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah will radiate with whiteness, and the faces of followers of Bid'ah (innovation) and division will be darkened, as has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas. According to the report, "When someone makes his concerns one concern, God will spare him the concerns of this world and the next world.

**The disagreements over the branches.**

Even some subsidiaries are so clear that they allow no margin of disagreement, unless of course, there be a selfish motive behind it. They may have no clear support from the texts of the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah, (rather they are deduced by the scholars on the basis of analogy) or the text on which they are based is open to different interpretations. Thus it will not be subjected to reproach under the authority of ‌ ‌ ‌ (Bid the Fair and forbid the Unfair), More so, when it is not unfair, raising an objection against what does not fall under the 'Unfair' would itself be regarded as unfair. Dispersion is one thing and disagreement something else. Dispersion is the opposite of together ness and disagreement the opposite of agreement. As for the disagreement of the community on the branches, it is like a group who set out for one goal by disagreeing roads, some going nearer and some farther. Although they disagree in the traveling, they arrive at one goal and come together. " In other words, this disagreement in branches is God's mercy toward the creatures, so that the work of the religion would not become narrow for them and its road would not be difficult.

**The unity that the believers are given.**

This verse is, in fact, a complement of 103) where Muslims were asked to seek unity and strength by attaching themselves to Allah's commands, individually and collectively, which helps make an entire community act like one body, one person, one entity. The benefit the intellectuals have of being imbued with this spirit is that all their attention remains focussed on goodness, that is, on the basics of religion. They have thus no time for hair-splitting arguments about secondary aspects of religion. Those who become the heralds of God’s greatness and arise both as warners and as harbingers of glad tidings have not the time to waste their expertise on matters of no significance. In this way, the task of exhorting people to lead a life of righteousness and forbidding evil engages them in finding solutions to real problems. Verbal jousting over supposed problems seems to them meaningless and futile, just as a farmer finds the game of chess a futile exercise, a waste of time. In showing willingness to be obedient to well-intentioned religious elders, the people are saved from schism and strife. Unity becomes a common attribute of believers, and unity, without doubt is the greatest of all powers in this world. Ad-Dahhak said, "They are a special group of the Companions and a special group of those after them, that is those who perform Jihad and the scholars." And do not follow the paths, lest they disperse you from His path" [6:153].

106.text:
"On that Day some faces will be bright while others gloomy" opens the verse with the day on which the state of the heart comes out on the face, and the sources read the brightness as the light of faith and the gloom as the darkness that settles on the people of refusal. "To the gloomy-faced it will be said" names the address that meets them, and the sources read the question that follows as a rebuke rather than a request for news. "Did you disbelieve after having believed" names the charge, and the sources read it as the wonder put to people who had been given the proof and then turned from it, and they carry the promise of the bright faces as the other half of the same day. "So taste the punishment for your disbelief" closes the verse with the sentence, and the sources read the tasting as the punishment itself coming upon them, so that the verse ends on the deed and its fruit and not on any decree that is out of measure. The verses before it had warned against becoming like the communities that split, and this verse shows what the split looks like when the day comes, while the verse after it names the mercy in which the bright-faced remain. The sources also draw the line from the deeds of a man to the face he will wear on that day, and they read the brightness as a light that is placed on the faces of the people of faith, and the gloom as the dust that settles on the people of refusal, so that the same day shows two companies and the difference between them is the difference of what they did with the proofs they were given.

**The day the faces are bright and the faces are gloomy.**

The day when some faces are blackened and some faces whitened that is the Day of Resurrection. Some faces on that day shall shine, laughing, joyous. Some faces on that day shall be dusty, overspread with darkness. According to the majority of commentators, 'brightness' signifies the brightness of the light of Faith, that is, the faces of believers shall be resplendent with the light of Faith, fresh and smiling due to happiness (as a result of rewards bestowed upon them by Allah). 'Darkness' signifies the darkness of disbelief, that is, the faces of the disbelievers will be covered with the gloomy anguish of disbelief and the added soot of sin and transgression would turn them still darker. (On the Day when some faces will become white and some faces will become black;)[3:106] on the Day of Resurrection. This great punishment will come upon them on the Day of Judgement, when the faces of those who have faith will become whitened, lighting up with joy and happiness; and the faces of those who denied the truth will become blackened, darkened with sadness and despair. It is said that whoever's heart is white today his face will be white in the future and the one who is the opposite his situation will be the reverse. Let there arise out of you a group of people inviting to all that is good (Islam), enjoining Al-Ma'ruf (all that Islam orders) and forbidding Al-Munkar (all that Islam has forbidden).

**The rebuke to those whose faces are blackened.**

As for those whose faces are blackened these being the disbelievers who are thrown into the Fire and to whom it is said in rebuke ‘Did you disbelieve after you had believed on the day the covenant was made? (Disbelieved ye) in Allah (after your (profession of) belief?) in Allah. (Then taste the punishment for that ye disbelieved) in Allah. As for those whose faces become blackened on that great day, they will be asked how they could reject faith in Allah alone, and deny the promise they made with Him that they would not worship anything besides Him, when they had had faith and acknowledged it. They will be told to taste the punishment Allah has prepared for them because of their disbelief. As for those whose faces are blackened did you disbelieve after you had believedḍ Then taste the chastisement for what you disbelieved!

**The bright faces in the mercy of Allah.**

(And for those whose faces will become white, they will be in Allah's mercy (Paradise), therein they shall dwell forever.) in Paradise, where they will reside for eternity and shall never desire to be removed. About the statement, 'they shall rest in Allah's mercy', the blessed Companion Sayyidna Ibn Abbas says that 'rahmah' or 'mercy' in the verse means 'Jannah' or 'paradise'. But for those whose faces are whitened they shall be in God's mercy abiding therein. As for those whose faces have become white they will be in intimacy and ease rawḥ. The faces of the lords of pretensions daʿāwā will be blackened while the faces of the companions of meanings maʿānī will be whitened. The faces of the people of unveilings kushūfāt will be whitened through illumina tion. The faces of the companions of the veil ḥijāb will be blackened with shame covered with dust taʿlūhā ghabara and overcast with gloom wa-tarhaquhā qatara. It is said that whoever turns away from created beings before His auspi cious occurrences sawāniḥ his face will become white with the spirit of having committed his affairs [to God] rūḥ al-tafwīḌ.

**The faces of the two groups at the resurrection.**

Sayyidna Ibn Abbas says that the faces of the followers of Sunnah shall be 'bright' and those of the followers of Bid'ah (innovation in the revealed Faith, not intended by Allah and His Messenger, nor by his learned dark Companions). Imam Tirmidhi narrates a hadith from Sayyidna Abu Umamah which identifies these as relating to the Khawarij,)the oldest sect of rebels), that is, the 'dark' faces shall belong to the Khawarij, and the 'bright' faces to those whom they shall kill. Imam al-Qurtubi has said in his Tafsir that the expression in the verse means that the faces of sincere Muslims shall be 'bright' but the faces of all those who may have altered their religion, or may have become apostates and disbelievers, or may be concealing their hypocrisy in their hearts, shall be 'dark'. Hadrat Ata' says that the faces of the Muhajirin and Ansar shall be 'bright' and the faces of the Bani Qurayzah and Bani Nadir shall be 'dark' (Qurtubi). (The People of the Two Scriptures divided into seventy-two sects. This Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one, that is, the Jama'ah. Some of my Ummah will be guided by desire, like one who is infected by rabies; no vein or joint will be saved from these desires.) Muslim recorded that Abu Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah said,. Imam Ahmad recorded that Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman said that the Prophet said,. When we arrived at Makkah, he stood up after praying Zuhr and said, 'The Messenger of Allah said,.

107.text:
"As for the bright-faced" opens the verse by naming the other half of the company, and the sources read them as the people of faith whose faces are made white on the day. "they will be in Allah's mercy" names the state they enter, and the sources read the mercy as the garden and the nearness that the word carries, with the whole of it named as a gift and not as a wage. "where they will remain forever" closes the verse with the length of the stay, and the sources read the forever as a stay that is never cut, since the mercy they are placed in is not a thing that passes. The verse before it had named the address to the gloomy-faced and the punishment they taste, and this verse sets the two ends side by side, while the verse after it names the verses that are recited in truth and the justice of God toward His creation.

**The faces that are made white.**

But as for those whose faces are whitened and these are the believers they shall be in God’s mercy that is to say in Paradise abiding therein. (As for those whose faces have been whitened, Lo! in the mercy of Allah) in Allah's Paradise (they dwell for ever) never to die or leave it. As for those whose faces become whitened, they will remain in Paradise, eternally blessed. But for those whose faces are whitened they shall be in God's mercy abiding therein. The faces of the lords of pretensions daʿāwā will be blackened while the faces of the companions of meanings maʿānī will be whitened.

**The mercy that does not end.**

This means that the mercy in which the believers shall rest will not be temporary; it would be forever and eternal. So, later on in verse 108, it was said: ‌ (and Allah wants no injustice for { anyone in the worlds} which means that Allah has no intention of being unjust to His creation. Whatever reward or punishment is there, is nothing but justice and very much the perfect expression of the divine wisdom and mercy. But as for those whose faces are whitened and these are the believers they shall be in God’s mercy that is to say in Paradise abiding therein. (As for those whose faces have been whitened, Lo! in the mercy of Allah) in Allah's Paradise (they dwell for ever) never to die or leave it.

**The goodness that is enjoined and the evil that is forbidden.**

(By He in Whose Hand is my soul! You will enjoin righteousness and forbid evil, or Allah shall send down a punishment from Him to you. Then, you will supplicate to Him, but He will not accept your supplication.) (The People of the Two Scriptures divided into seventy-two sects. This Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one, that is, the Jama'ah. Some of my Ummah will be guided by desire, like one who is infected by rabies; no vein or joint will be saved from these desires.) The benefit the intellectuals have of being imbued with this spirit is that all their attention remains focussed on goodness, that is, on the basics of religion. They have thus no time for hair-splitting arguments about secondary aspects of religion.

108.text:
"These are Allah's revelations We recite to you O Prophet in truth" opens the verse by naming the verses themselves as the proof, and the sources read the reciting as the sending down that carries the commands and the promises, so that what is recited is the truth and not a claim about it. "And Allah desires no injustice to His creation" closes the verse with the statement that clears the Lord of the worlds of any wrong, and the sources read the punishment that the verses name as the fruit of the deeds of the people and not as a decree that falls out of measure, since the generous does not need to wrong the ones He has made and the just does not punish what has not earned the punishment. The verse before it had named the mercy that does not end for the bright-faced, and this verse turns from the two ends of the people to the verses that carry both of them, so that the hearer knows the book is true in what it promises and just in what it warns of.

**The verses that are recited in truth.**

Those that is to say these verses are the verses of God which We recite to you O Muhammad in truth and God desires not any injustice for the worlds punishing them for no crime. (These are the Ayat of Allah. We recite them to you) meaning, 'These are the verses of Allah, His proofs and signs that We reveal to you, O Muhammad,'. (We recite them unto thee) We send them with Gabriel to you (in truth) in order to show what is true and what is an error. O Prophet, these verses recited to you which contain Allah’s promises and threats, are true in what they contain of information, and just in what they contain of laws. Those are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth and God desires not any injustice for the worlds.

**The attention that is given and the time that is not wasted.**

The benefit the intellectuals have of being imbued with this spirit is that all their attention remains focussed on goodness, that is, on the basics of religion. They have thus no time for hair-splitting arguments about secondary aspects of religion. Those who become the heralds of God’s greatness and arise both as warners and as harbingers of glad tidings have not the time to waste their expertise on matters of no significance.

**The injustice that Allah does not will.**

The verse ‌ (now taste the punishment because you have been sinning) indicates that the punishment on that Day is not from Allah but that it is as consequence of what man has earned while living his mortal life, for the truth is that the blessings of paradise and the hardships of hell are simply a changed form of our very deeds. To God belongs all that is in the heavens and in the earth and to Him all matters are returned. This means that the mercy in which the believers shall rest will not be temporary; it would be forever and eternal. So, later on in verse 108, it was said: ‌ (and Allah wants no injustice for { anyone in the worlds} which means that Allah has no intention of being unjust to His creation. Whatever reward or punishment is there, is nothing but justice and very much the perfect expression of the divine wisdom and mercy. (and Allah wills no injustice to the 'Alamin.) for He never treats them with injustice. Therefore, He does not need to treat any of His creatures with injustice, and this is why He said next,. (Allah willeth no injustice to creatures) He does not will to be unjust to the jinn or human beings. Allah does not desire injustice for any creature in the worlds, and no one receives a punishment unless they earned it through their own bad actions. How could it be pos sible to ascribe injustice to Him in the determining of events taqdīr and existence wujūd when all created beings are His creation and what has been determined for them is His wise determination ḥukmḍ To God belongs all that is in the heavens and in the earth by way of possession milk and to Him all matters are returned by way of determi nation ḥukm.

109.text:
"To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" opens the verse with the statement of the owner of all things, and the sources read it as the creation and the decree both belonging to Him, so that nothing in the two worlds stands outside His rule. "And to Allah all matters will be returned for judgment" closes the verse with the return, and the sources read it as the gathering on the day of judgement when every account is closed and every deed is weighed. The verse before it had cleared Allah of any injustice toward His creation, and this verse names the reason the judgement can be trusted, since the one who judges owns the whole and knows the whole, while the verses after it turn to the community that was raised for people and to the warning it carries. The sources also join these two names to the mercy and the punishment that the passage has been setting before the hearer, so that the same Lord who owns everything is the one who shows mercy and the one who brings to account.

**What belongs to Allah in the heavens and the earth.**

(Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings and marvellous things; (and unto Allah all things are returned) in the Hereafter. To Allah alone belongs all that is in the heavens and in the earth, in creation and decree, and everything will return to Him on the Day of Judgement, when everyone will be rewarded according to what they have done. How could it be pos sible to ascribe injustice to Him in the determining of events taqdīr and existence wujūd when all created beings are His creation and what has been determined for them is His wise determination ḥukmḍ To God belongs all that is in the heavens and in the earth by way of possession milk and to Him all matters are returned by way of determi nation ḥukm. Those are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth and God desires not any injustice for the worlds.

**The matters that are all returned to Him.**

To Allah alone belongs all that is in the heavens and in the earth, in creation and decree, and everything will return to Him on the Day of Judgement, when everyone will be rewarded according to what they have done. We make our address to you continuous in all times in all things small and large a cultivation of the way of love widād. (Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings and marvellous things; (and unto Allah all things are returned) in the Hereafter.

**The mercy that is His and the punishment He has set.**

This means that the mercy in which the believers shall rest will not be temporary; it would be forever and eternal. The verse ‌ (now taste the punishment because you have been sinning) indicates that the punishment on that Day is not from Allah but that it is as consequence of what man has earned while living his mortal life, for the truth is that the blessings of paradise and the hardships of hell are simply a changed form of our very deeds. So, later on in verse 108, it was said: ‌ (and Allah wants no injustice for { anyone in the worlds} which means that Allah has no intention of being unjust to His creation. Whatever reward or punishment is there, is nothing but justice and very much the perfect expression of the divine wisdom and mercy. (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! You will enjoin righteousness and forbid evil, or Allah shall send down a punishment from Him to you. Then, you will supplicate to Him, but He will not accept your supplication.) (The People of the Two Scriptures divided into seventy-two sects. This Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one, that is, the Jama'ah. Some of my Ummah will be guided by desire, like one who is infected by rabies; no vein or joint will be saved from these desires.) (And for those whose faces will become white, they will be in Allah's mercy (Paradise), therein they shall dwell forever.) in Paradise, where they will reside for eternity and shall never desire to be removed. The benefit the intellectuals have of being imbued with this spirit is that all their attention remains focussed on goodness, that is, on the basics of religion. They have thus no time for hair-splitting arguments about secondary aspects of religion. Those who become the heralds of God’s greatness and arise both as warners and as harbingers of glad tidings have not the time to waste their expertise on matters of no significance.

110.text:
"You are the best community ever raised for humanity" opens the verse with the honour that is given to the community of the messenger, and the sources read the raising as the bringing out of a people for the good of the whole creation and not for their own glory. "you encourage good, forbid evil" names the work that earned the name, and the sources read the two halves as the mission the community was raised for, so that the honour is tied to the labour and not to the name. "and believe in Allah" names the third mark, and the sources read the faith as the root that makes the other two stand, since a community that calls to good while denying the one who made the good would have nothing to call to. "Had the People of the Book believed it would have been better for them" turns from the community to the communities, and the sources read the turn as the mercy that would have come to them had they accepted what their own books had told them of. "Some of them are faithful but most are rebellious" closes the verse with the division inside the other communities, and the sources read the small band as the ones who kept faith and the many as the ones who broke the pledge. The verses before it had named the returned matters and the owner of all, and this verse shows the community that lives under that owner. The sources read the praise as a description of what the community is when it does the work, and they warn that the name does not carry the people, so that a community which leaves the calling and the faith behind is not the community that was praised.

**The best community raised for humanity.**

You O community of Muhammad are the best community brought forth manifested to men according to God’s knowledge enjoining decency and forbidding indecency and believing in God. In the present verse, it has been further emphasised that these are the very reasons why Allah Almighty has conferred upon the Ummah of Muhammad may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the status of 'Khayr al-Umam', the best of communities, dignified and elevated, when it does what it has been charged to do. This portion deals with the major reason why the Ummah of Muhammad i has been called the best of human communities. The reason is that this community has been raised for the sole purpose of dispensing good to all beings created by Allah. You are the best of peoples ever raised up for mankind; you enjoin Al-Ma'ruf (all that Islam has ordained) and forbid Al-Munkar (all that Islam has forbidden), and you believe in Allah. You are, O Community of Muhammad ﷺ, the best of all communities that Allah has produced for humanity – in your faith and actions – and the most beneficial for other people: instructing what is right according to the sacred law and what you know to be right, and forbidding what is wrong according to the sacred law and what you know to be wrong; and having certain faith in Allah, so that it shows in your actions. You are the best community khayra ummatin brought forth to men enjoining decency and forbidding indecency and believing in God. Because MuṣṬafā is the most honored of the prophets his community is the best of communities. He created them as the last of created beings so that their stay beneath the earth would not be long [before the resurrection]. Their goodness khayriyya has been obtained not by the abundance of their prayers and devotional acts but by the intensity with which He has drawn them near and selected them. Surely the standing of the earlier ones at the door has been long but when the permission comes to enter the later ones will go first. If everyone had been included under Our command they would have attained true glory in this world and the hereafter but they were kept away from acceptance in the choice already made-most of them were branded with associating partners with God shirk.

**The good that is encouraged and the evil that is forbidden.**

Seen in the perspective of past communities, it was this community which contributed most in the mission of 'bidding the Fair and forbidding the Unfair', even though this was already enjoined upon past communities as mentioned in authentic ahadith. However, to begin with, several past communities did not have Jihad as a religious obligation, in which case, the mission of 'bidding the Fair' could only be carried out by heart and tongue only. (Ye enjoin right conduct) you enjoin the divine Oneness of Allah and the following of Muhammad (and forbid indecency) you forbid disbelief, idolatry and the opposition of the Messenger; (and ye believe in Allah) as well as in all revealed scriptures and messengers. The benefit the intellectuals have of being imbued with this spirit is that all their attention remains focussed on goodness, that is, on the basics of religion. Those who become the heralds of God’s greatness and arise both as warners and as harbingers of glad tidings have not the time to waste their expertise on matters of no significance. In this way, the task of exhorting people to lead a life of righteousness and forbidding evil engages them in finding solutions to real problems. Verbal jousting over supposed problems seems to them meaningless and futile, just as a farmer finds the game of chess a futile exercise, a waste of time. In showing willingness to be obedient to well-intentioned religious elders, the people are saved from schism and strife.

**The faith in Allah that makes them what they are.**

The second distinguishing feature of this community is that they 'believe in Allah' ' At this point one may ask why should this be a distinguishing feature of the Muslim community as belief in Allah has been the common factor between all past prophets and their communities. You are the best of peoples ever raised up for mankind; you enjoin Al-Ma'ruf (all that Islam has ordained) and forbid Al-Munkar (all that Islam has forbidden), and you believe in Allah. You are the best community khayra ummatin brought forth to men enjoining decency and forbidding indecency and believing in God. Submitting to an authority unites all of them.

**Had the People of the Book believed.**

(And if the People of the Scripture) i.e. the Jews and Christians (had believed it had been better for them) than what they are in now. If the People of the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians, had faith in Muhammad it would be better for them in this world and in the Afterlife. Towards the end of the verse, it has been said about the people of the Book that there are some Muslims among them. This is the reason why, after Allah praised the Muslim Ummah with the qualities that He mentioned, He criticized the People of the Scriptures and chastised them, saying,. Our religion is better than that to which you call us; and we are also more virtuous and better than you . And Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse as a response to them . This was revealed about [ Abd Allah] Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Salim, the client of Abu Hudhayfah.

**The few who are faithful and the most who are rebellious.**

(Some of them are believers) 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers; (but most of them are evil-livers) unbelievers who break their pledges. Only few of the People of the Scripture believe in what Muhammad ﷺ came with and most of them do not stay within the sacred way of life and sacred law of Allah. Salām may God be pleased with him and his companions; but most of them the disbelievers are wicked. This is because they disobeyed (Allah) and used to transgress (the limits set by Allah) (they have drawn on themselves the wrath of Allah,) means, they earned Allah's anger, which they deserved,. (This is because they disbelieved in the Ayat of Allah and killed the Prophets without right.) meaning, what drove them to this was their arrogance, transgression and envy, earning them humiliation, degradation and disgrace throughout this life and the Hereafter. (This is because they disobeyed and used to transgress (the limits set by Allah).) meaning, what lured them to disbelieve in Allah's Ayat and kill His Messengers, is the fact that they often disobeyed Allah's commands, committed His prohibitions and transgressed His set limits.

111.text:
"They can never inflict harm on you" opens the verse with the pledge that the plans of the hostile will not reach the believers, and the sources read the harm that is denied as the harm that touches the faith and the harm that would end the community. "except a little annoyance" names what is left to them, and the sources read it as the hurt of the tongue, the slander and the threat that touches the ear but not the heart. "But if they meet you in battle" names the trial that is set before them, and the sources read the meeting as the fight in which the men are set against one another. "they will flee and they will have no helpers" closes the verse with the prophecy, and the sources read it as the promise that the enemies will turn their backs and will find no one to stand with them, since the Lord does not give the enemies of His friends a lasting power over them. The verse before it had named the few who are faithful among the people of the Book, and this verse names the many who are not, while the verses after it show the humiliation that follows that path.

**The harm they can do and the harm they cannot.**

They the Jews will not harm you O company of Muslims in any way except a little hurt with their tongues such as slander and threats; and if they fight against you they will turn their backs to you in retreat then they will not be helped against you but you will be helped against them. (They will not harm you) the Jews will not harm you (save a trifling hurt) with their tongue by vilifying and defaming you, (and if they fight against you) in Religion (they will turn and flee) defeated. If they are against you they will not harm you, O believers, in your belief, or in yourselves, except through their words: criticising your faith and making fun of you and so on. They will not harm you except a little hurt; and if they fight against you they will turn their backs to you then they will not be helped. In previous verses (98-101), it was shown how hostile to Muslims the people of the Book were and how they planned to bring religious harm to them.

**The fight from which they will turn back.**

They will not harm you except a little hurt; and if they fight against you they will turn their backs to you then they will not be helped. (And afterward they will not be helped) they will not be saved from your swords or from being taken as captives. Also, if they fight you they will flee from you in defeat, and will never be victorious over you. If [the enemies] imagine themselves to be superior to the friends in truth they suffer lowliness and degradation. The Jewish chieftains Ka'b, Bahra, al-Nu'man, Abu Rafi , Abu Yasir and Ibn Surya went to Abd Allah ibn Salam and his followers, who had believed, and hurt them because of their acceptance of Islam and so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse .

**The pledge that their plans will not succeed.**

Mentioned in the present verse are their plans to harm Muslims materially. The last sentence carries the prophecy that they shall not succeed. Those who come forward for this divine mission have God’s pledge that their opponents will not be able to inflict any real harm upon them. The Real does not give His enemies power over His friends except as much as will prove the sincerity of the flight [of the friends] to God for the reality of their flight firār is nobler before Him than their staying firm qarār. Now the Muslims have undertaken the obligation of guiding people to the true religion of submission to God. The assignment of this role demands that they be true believers in God. (We (Muslims) are the last to come, but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, and the first people to enter Paradise, although the former nations were given the Scriptures before us and we after them. Allah gave us the guidance of truth that they have been disputing about. This (Friday) is the Day that they have been disputing about, and all the other people are behind us in this matter: the Jews' (day of congregation is) tomorrow (Saturday) and the Christians' is the day after tomorrow (Sunday).) (they have drawn on themselves the wrath of Allah,) means, they earned Allah's anger, which they deserved,. (This is because they disobeyed and used to transgress (the limits set by Allah).) meaning, what lured them to disbelieve in Allah's Ayat and kill His Messengers, is the fact that they often disobeyed Allah's commands, committed His prohibitions and transgressed His set limits.

112.text:
"They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they go" opens the verse with the humiliation that is laid on the people who broke the covenant, and the sources read the disgrace as the mark that follows them from place to place so that they are never settled in honour. "unless they are protected by a covenant with Allah or a treaty with the people" names the one door that is left open, and the sources read it as the protection that a pledge from God or a truce made with men can give, so that the humiliation is lifted where the word is kept. "They have invited the displeasure of Allah and have been branded with misery for rejecting Allah's revelations and murdering His prophets unjustly" names the deeds that brought it, and the sources read the killing of the messengers and the refusal of the clear signs as the actions that drew the anger down. "This is a fair reward for their disobedience and violations" closes the verse with the justice of what came upon them, and the sources read the end as the fruit of their own hands and not as a wrong from the Lord of the worlds. The verse before it had named the little hurt of the tongue and the flight in battle, and this verse names the long humiliation that the same people carry. The verse names the end of a people who were given the book and broke the pledge, and the sources follow the mark of the humiliation through their history, so that the disgrace is read as the sign that the blessing was taken from them and the door of honour was closed. The same sources join this end to the deeds that are named in the sentence, since the killing of the prophets and the refusal of the signs are the works that brought the anger down, and they read the covenant and the treaty as the one mercy that stayed open to them.

**The humiliation that follows them wherever they are found.**

Abasement shall be cast upon them wherever they are found so that they have no strength and no protection save if they be clinging to a rope of God and a rope of the believing people this being the latter’s covenant of security for them on the condition that they pay the jizya in other words they have no protection other than this; they have incurred they have ended up with anger from God and poverty shall be cast upon them; that is because they disbelieved in God’s signs and slew the prophets without right; that dhālika is repeated for emphasis is because they disobeyed God’s command and used to transgress passing from what is lawful into what is unlawful. (Ignominy shall be their portion) the humiliation of Jizyah shall be imposed upon them (wheresoever they are found) they cannot stand against the believers (save (where they grasp) a rope from Allah) except if they believe in Allah (and a rope from men) or take a pledge with the rulers to pay the Jizyah. Abasement shall be cast upon them wherever they are found save a rope of God and a rope of the people; they have incurred anger from God and poverty shall be cast upon them; that because they disbelieved in God's signs and slew the prophets without right; that because they disobeyed and used to transgress. The sign of being exiled cannot be hidden the mark of distance cannot be concealed and the evidence of being cut off cannot be veiled. They are in the lowly state of having been banished and abased by rejection. Those who have eyes ulū l-abṣar learn from them while those among the dis believers and the profligates al-kuffār al-fujjār who are of their kind are deceived by them. Humiliation and shame has been made to surround them wherever they are, and they are only safe with a contract or protection from Allah or from people.

**The covenant of Allah and the treaty of the people.**

A detailed discussion on this subject has already appeared under comments on verse 61 of Surah al-Baqarah where the text has not mentioned any exception. For example, a minor child or woman shall not be killed. (This exception is meant by the words 'through a source from Allah'). Through a treaty obligation, that is, (through a source from men). Such patronage may cause their disgrace and misery not to become manifest. The specific words used in the Holy Qur'an i.e., a source from men, cover all men, believers and disbelievers. The possibility that they live with freedom after making a peace treaty with Muslims is included here. Also possible is the situation that they may come under the protection of other non-Muslim powers through a peace treaty (or informal collaboration strategy), a situation that prevails in the form of the present-day state of Israel.

**The anger they deserved and the misery laid on them.**

(They have incurred anger) they deserved anger (from their Lord, and wretchedness is laid upon them) the attire of poverty was imposed upon them. Abasement shall be cast upon them wherever they are found save a rope of God and a rope of the people; they have incurred anger from God and poverty shall be cast upon them; that because they disbelieved in God's signs and slew the prophets without right; that because they disobeyed and used to transgress. They have earned the anger of Allah, and need and poverty has been made to surround them. (they have drawn on themselves the wrath of Allah,) means, they earned Allah's anger, which they deserved,.

**The prophets they killed and the limits they crossed.**

(That) ignominy (is because they used to disbelieve the revelations of Allah) in Muhammad and the Qur'an, (and slew the Prophets wrongfully) i.e. without the prophets having committed any crime. This is due to their rejection of the signs of Allah, killing the prophets unjustly, and because they rebelled and overstepped the limits of Allah. This is because they disbelieved in the Ayat of Allah and killed the Prophets without right. This is because they disobeyed (Allah) and used to transgress (the limits set by Allah) (That) anger and humiliation (is because they were rebellious) against Allah on the Sabbath (and used to transgress) by killing the prophets and take as lawful things that were prohibited. (This is because they disobeyed and used to transgress (the limits set by Allah).) meaning, what lured them to disbelieve in Allah's Ayat and kill His Messengers, is the fact that they often disobeyed Allah's commands, committed His prohibitions and transgressed His set limits.

**The community raised for people and the duty it carries.**

Al-Bukhari recorded that Abu Hurayrah commented on this Ayah, "(You, Muslims, are) the best nation of people for the people, you bring them tied in chains on their necks (capture them in war) and they later embrace Islam. The Ummah of Muhammad achieved this virtue because of its Prophet, Muhammad, peace be upon him, the most regarded of Allah's creation and the most honored Messenger with Allah. (We (Muslims) are the last to come, but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, and the first people to enter Paradise, although the former nations were given the Scriptures before us and we after them. Allah gave us the guidance of truth that they have been disputing about. This (Friday) is the Day that they have been disputing about, and all the other people are behind us in this matter: the Jews' (day of congregation is) tomorrow (Saturday) and the Christians' is the day after tomorrow (Sunday).) (We (Muslims) are the last (to come), but (will be) the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, and will be the first people to enter Paradise...) until the end of the Hadith. Those from this Ummah who do not acquire these qualities will be just like the People of the Scriptures whom Allah criticized, when He said,. This is the reason why, after Allah praised the Muslim Ummah with the qualities that He mentioned, He criticized the People of the Scriptures and chastised them, saying,. (it would have been better for them; among them are some who have faith, but most of them are Fasiqun (rebellious).) There shall always be a group of Muslims in Ash-Sham area until 'Isa, son of Maryam, descends while they are like this [on the truth, apparent and victorious]. 'Isa will at that time rule according to the Law of Muhammad , break the cross, kill the swine, banish the Jizyah and only accept Islam from the people. Subsequently, God sent His religion in its original form through the Prophet Muhammad. Now the Muslims have undertaken the obligation of guiding people to the true religion of submission to God. The assignment of this role demands that they be true believers in God. It devolves upon them to enjoin goodness upon the world and to inform mankind of whatever is evil in the eyes of God. Since this is a mission assigned by Almighty God, He Himself has guaranteed to help His emissaries surmount all obstacles to their performing this task. Those who come forward for this divine mission have God’s pledge that their opponents will not be able to inflict any real harm upon them.

113.text:
"Yet they are not all alike" opens the verse by refusing the broad judgment the passage has been carrying, and the sources read the sentence as the distinction between those who kept the faith of their books and those who broke it. "there are some among the People of the Book who are upright" names the band, and the sources read the upright as the ones who stand by the commands of God and hold to the book, so that the community is not condemned as a whole. "who recite Allah's revelations throughout the night" names their worship, and the sources read the night as the hours in which they stand in prayer, with the reciting done in the watches when the world is asleep. "prostrating in prayer" closes the verse with the posture of the body, and the sources read the prostration as the sign of a heart that has put itself down before its Lord. The verse before it had named the humiliation of those who broke the covenant, and this verse sets beside them the ones who kept it, while the verses after it name the faith and the good works that make them of the righteous. The sources refuse the broad judgment that the passage has been carrying about the people of the book, and they read the sentence as the door that stays open for the ones who kept faith, so that no community is condemned as a whole and no band is praised as a whole. The sources also follow the worth of the small band through the history of the city, since the upright among them are joined to the company of the believers and their night prayer is named as the sign that they belonged to the people of the answer, with the standing in the dark hours set before the reader as the mark of a heart that has turned away from the world.

**Not all the People of the Book are alike.**

(They are not all alike) i.e. those who believed from among the people of the Book are not like those among them who have not. Allah then revealed this verse (They are not all alike) . Having made clear what many of the People of the Scripture are like, Allah then explains that there is a group among them who are upright and stand by the truth – not all the People of the Scripture are the same. This Ayah means that those among the People of the Book whom Allah rebuked earlier are not at all the same as those among them who embraced Islam. Therefore, these two types of people are not equal, and indeed, there are believers and also criminals among the People of the Book, just as Allah said,. In verse 110, it was said that among the people of the Book there are those who believe, yet most of them are disbelievers. This refers here to the conduct of the People of the Book (believers in former revealed scriptures), and their immediate recognition and acceptance, in all humility, of the divine truth as proclaimed from the lips of the Last Prophet.

**The upright community among the People of the Book.**

Yet they the People of the Scripture are not all alike equal; some of the People of the Scripture are a community upright with integrity adhering to the truth such as ‘Abd Allāh b. (Of the People of the Scripture there is a staunch community) He says: there are among them a group of upright people who are guided by Allah's divine Oneness: 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers (who recite the revelations of Allah) the Qur'an (in the night season) in the hours of the night in their prayer, (falling prostrate (before Him) praying to Allah. Rather, there is a group among them who follow the Religion of Allah: doing as Allah instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, reading the verses of Allah in the hours of the night, and praying to Him. (a party of the People of the Scripture stand for the right) for they implement the Book of Allah, adhere to His Law and follow His Prophet Muhammad . Yet they are not all alike; some of the people of the scripture are a community upright who recite God's verses in the watches of the night pros trating themselves. Details appear in the present verse which gives a complementary profile of those who believed from among the people of the Book, and by becoming Muslims, they adopted the distinguishing hallmarks of the Faith that go to make believers the best of communities. Allah then revealed this verse (They are not all alike) .

**The reciting in the watches of the night.**

Salām may God be pleased with him and his companions who recite God’s verses in the watches of the night that is during its hours prostrating themselves performing prayer wa-hum yasjudūn ‘prostrating themselves’ is a circumstantial qualifier.
