Yet they are not all alike; some of the people of the scripture are a community upright who recite God's verses in the watches of the night pros trating themselves. They believe in God and in the Last Day enjoining decency and for bidding indecency vying with one another in good works; those are of the righteous. They often stand in prayer at night for Tahajjud, and recite the Qur'an in their prayer,. (They believe in Allah and the Last Day; they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf and forbid Al-Munkar; and they hasten in good works; and they are among the righteous)[3: 114]. And the verse (They are not all alike. Of the People of the Scripture there is a staunch community who recite the revelations of Allah in the night season, falling prostrate (before Him) was revealed . This was revealed regarding the nightfall prayer which is performed by the Muslims but not by the people of the Book . The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, delayed the time of the nightfall prayer. When he came out to lead the prayer, he found people waiting for the prayer.

**The faith that made them hasten to good works.**

(They believe in Allah and the Last Day; they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf and forbid Al-Munkar; and they hasten in good works; and they are among the righteous)[3: 114]. They believe in God and in the Last Day enjoining decency and for bidding indecency vying with one another in good works; those are of the righteous. Rather, there is a group among them who follow the Religion of Allah: doing as Allah instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, reading the verses of Allah in the hours of the night, and praying to Him. This group existed before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was sent, and became Muslim when they met him and understood his message. This refers here to the conduct of the People of the Book (believers in former revealed scriptures), and their immediate recognition and acceptance, in all humility, of the divine truth as proclaimed from the lips of the Last Prophet. Yet this obstacle was successfully overcome and the religion of the contemporary Prophet was welcomed. Only the evil amongst us believed in Muhammad, for had they been among our best they would not have abandoned the religion of their forefathers .

**The warning against those who waste what they spend.**

Soon after praising those who had embraced Islam from among the people of the Book, the text censures those of them who did not embrace Islam and insisted on retaining their stance of disbelief, not realizing that their wealth and their children will be unable to save them from the punishment of Allah and Hell shall be their eternal abode. Verse 117 declares through a similitude that disbelievers simply waste what they spend in this worldly life, for belief in Islam is a pre-condition in order that such spendings be acceptable with Allah, of whatever sort they may be. The similitude stresses the fact that disbelievers inflict this injustice upon themselves when their spendings go to waste in this world and remain rewardless in the Hereafter. If they were not to wrong themselves, if they were to embrace Islam, they would have been like other Muslims who, on suffering a worldly loss, are compensated by Allah through reward and forgiveness of sins, as reported in ahadith. At that time there was, on the one hand, the religion of Moses, invested with all the strength of historical grandeur and sanctity of tradition. On the other hand stood the religion of the Prophet Muhammad, which had yet to acquire the force of argument, historical grandeur and traditional sanctity to support it. This difference between Moses’ religion and the religion of the Prophet of the time posed the greatest obstacle to the acknowledgment of the latter’s religion. Allah wronged them not, but they wronged themselves. Just as the difference between light and darkness is one of contradiction it has likewise been established that the states of the friends and the states of the enemies are mutually exclusive.

114.text:
"They believe in Allah and the Last Day" opens the verse with the faith of the band that the verses before have named, and the sources read the two names as the whole of the belief, since the trust in God and the trust in the day of reckoning are the two roots from which the rest of the description grows. "encourage good and forbid evil" names the work, and the sources read the two halves as the calling the community was raised for, with the good named as what God has ordained and the evil as what He has refused. "and race with one another in doing good" names the speed of the band, and the sources read the racing as the eagerness that does not wait to be pushed, so that the deeds are done before the crowd has looked. "They are truly among the righteous" closes the verse with the judgment, and the sources read the word as the place of the band among the people of faith. The verses before it had named the upright community among the people of the book, and this verse sets out what that uprightness looks like in the life of the day, while the verse after it names the reward that will not be denied to them, so that the faith, the calling and the racing are held together as one description of a people whose whole life runs in a single direction. The band is named in the middle of a passage about the people of the book, and the verse draws the line between the many who kept their old ground and the few who answered the call of the day they were living in.

They believe in God and in the Last Day enjoining decency and forbidding indecency vying with one another in good works; those described in the way God has mentioned are of the righteous and some of them are not like this and are not righteous. They believe in God and in the Last Day enjoining decency and for bidding indecency vying with one another in good works; those are of the righteous. (They are of the righteous) of the righteous among the community of Muhammad in Paradise, such as Abu Bakr and his fellow believers. 115.text:
"They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done" opens the verse with the pledge that nothing done in faith is lost, and the sources read the denial as the withholding of a wage that is owed, so that the smallest deed of the band is kept and paid. "And Allah has perfect knowledge of those mindful of Him" closes the verse with the knowledge that keeps the account, and the sources read the mindfulness as the guarding of the commands and the staying away from what God has forbidden, with none of it hidden from Him. The verse before it had named the band among the people of the book, and this verse names the wage that waits for them, while the verse after it turns to the wealth and the children of the people who refused. The sources also follow the difference between the two companies inside the one community of the book, so that the promise of the verse is read against the loss that the verses after it name, and the reader is left with the difference between a deed that is kept and a deed that the wind takes.

**The good that is never denied its reward.**

Whatever good these people do, whether it is little or much, their reward for it will not be lost. (And whatever good) that was mentioned above; and it is also said: whatever act of excellence they perform towards Muhammad and his Companions (they do) i.e. 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers, (they will not be denied the meed thereof) its reward will not be forgotten and they shall indeed be rewarded for it. And whatever good you do O community taf‘alū ‘you do’ or if this is read yaf‘alū ‘they do’ then it is referring to them ‘the upright community’ you shall not be denied it read in both ways fa-lan tukfarūhu ‘you shall not be denied it’ or fa-lan yukfarūhu ‘they shall not be denied it’ you shall not be deprived of its reward but you will be rewarded for it and God knows the God-fearing. And whatever good they do they shall not be denied it and God knows the God-fearing. Allah knows those who are Mindful, who follow what He instructs, and stay away from what He prohibits. None of what they do is hidden from Him, and they will be rewarded accordingly. One who is intent shall not be debarred from His door; one who does busi ness shall not suffer loss on His account; one who desires companionship shall not be lonely with Him; and one who seeks shall not be contemptible before Him.

**The knowledge of those who are mindful of Him.**

(Allah is Aware of those who ward off (evil) ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecency-the reference here being to 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers. Allah knows those who are Mindful, who follow what He instructs, and stay away from what He prohibits. And whatever good they do they shall not be denied it and God knows the God-fearing. Not all of them are alike; a party of the People of the Scripture stand for the right, they recite the verses of Allah during the hours of the night, prostrating themselves in prayer They believe in Allah and the Last Day; they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf and forbid Al-Munkar; and they hasten in good works; and they are among the righteous And whatever good they do, nothing will be rejected of them; for Allah knows well the Muttaqin (the pious)Surely, those who disbelieve, neither their properties nor their offspring will avail them against Allah. 116.text:
"Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah" opens the verse with the two things the people lean on, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that neither the riches nor the sons can stand between a man and the judgment of his Lord. "It is they who will be the residents of the Fire" names the end, and the sources read the residence as the long stay from which there is no leaving. "They will be there forever" closes the verse with the length of the stay, and the sources join the endless dwelling to the deeds that earned it. The verses before it had named the band whose good works are kept, and this verse names the people whose goods are of no use to them, so that the two companies are shown side by side. The sources also follow the love of wealth and children as the thing that kept the people of the book from the answer, since the holding of a position among the people was the treasure they would not put down. The verse is short and the judgment in it is heavy, and the sources set it beside the verses that name the band whose works are kept, so that the reader sees what a man keeps and what a man loses, and the verse names the two things the people of the world trust in and shows that neither of them stands in the place of the deed that is done with faith. The wealth and the children are the two treasures that the people of the book counted on, and the verse takes both of them away as a support in the hour when the account is opened.

**The wealth and the children that cannot help.**

(Lo! the riches) the abundance of riches (and the progeny) and the abundance of progeny (of those who disbelieve) in Muhammad and in the Qur'an, i.e. Ka'b [Ibn al-Ashraf] and his followers (will not avail them aught against Allah) will not avail them against the punishment of Allah; (and such are rightful owners of the Fire) the dwellers of hell. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail protect them neither their children against God that is against His chastisement these two are singled out for mention because a person usually avails himself either by paying a ransom or by resorting to the help of his children; those are the inhabitants of the Fire abiding therein. Disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger will not be helped against Allah by their wealth or children: they will not prevent His punishment or bring His mercy to them; rather, their suffering and distress will only increase, and they will be eternally companions of the fire of Hell. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail them neither their children against God; those are the inhabitants of the fire abiding therein.

**Those who are the residents of the Fire.**

Disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger will not be helped against Allah by their wealth or children: they will not prevent His punishment or bring His mercy to them; rather, their suffering and distress will only increase, and they will be eternally companions of the fire of Hell. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail protect them neither their children against God that is against His chastisement these two are singled out for mention because a person usually avails himself either by paying a ransom or by resorting to the help of his children; those are the inhabitants of the Fire abiding therein. They are the dwellers of the Fire, therein they will abide The parable of what they spend in this world is that of a wind of Sir; it struck the harvest of a people who did wrong against themselves and destroyed it. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail them neither their children against God; those are the inhabitants of the fire abiding therein. They are in a state of loss in the here and now and in the future will be in separation and exile affliction and hurt punishment and rejection:

**The love of wealth and children.**

The love of wealth and children becomes an obstacle to accepting a religion, which entails all kinds of sacrifices. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail protect them neither their children against God that is against His chastisement these two are singled out for mention because a person usually avails himself either by paying a ransom or by resorting to the help of his children; those are the inhabitants of the Fire abiding therein. Disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger will not be helped against Allah by their wealth or children: they will not prevent His punishment or bring His mercy to them; rather, their suffering and distress will only increase, and they will be eternally companions of the fire of Hell. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail them neither their children against God; those are the inhabitants of the fire abiding therein. But merely being a member of a community formed of one race in the name of a prophet, is not enough to earn one salvation. What is actually required of an individual is that he binds himself by a covenant with God. Just as a gust of chill air ravages the whole harvest, so will the tempest of the Last Day (qiyamah) render valueless all such ostentatious acts. There were some among the Jews who believed in the Prophet Muhammad.

**What their wealth and their children will not do for them.**

There is no alternate for them in the situation no substitute for them in the final outcome. Alas to anyone who has sought but did not find a replacement to let him forget. God has full knowledge of their actions, for which He will reward them, and He will greatly honour them on the Day of Judgement. This Ayah means that those among the People of the Book whom Allah rebuked earlier are not at all the same as those among them who embraced Islam. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail protect them neither their children against God that is against His chastisement these two are singled out for mention because a person usually avails himself either by paying a ransom or by resorting to the help of his children; those are the inhabitants of the Fire abiding therein. Disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger will not be helped against Allah by their wealth or children: they will not prevent His punishment or bring His mercy to them; rather, their suffering and distress will only increase, and they will be eternally companions of the fire of Hell. As for the disbelievers their riches shall not avail them neither their children against God; those are the inhabitants of the fire abiding therein.

**The band whose deeds are kept and the people whose spending is lost.**

Not all of them are alike; a party of the People of the Scripture stand for the right, they recite the verses of Allah during the hours of the night, prostrating themselves in prayer They believe in Allah and the Last Day; they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf and forbid Al-Munkar; and they hasten in good works; and they are among the righteous And whatever good they do, nothing will be rejected of them; for Allah knows well the Muttaqin (the pious)Surely, those who disbelieve, neither their properties nor their offspring will avail them against Allah. Details appear in the present verse which gives a complementary profile of those who believed from among the people of the Book, and by becoming Muslims, they adopted the distinguishing hallmarks of the Faith that go to make believers the best of communities. Soon after praising those who had embraced Islam from among the people of the Book, the text censures those of them who did not embrace Islam and insisted on retaining their stance of disbelief, not realizing that their wealth and their children will be unable to save them from the punishment of Allah and Hell shall be their eternal abode. Verse 117 declares through a similitude that disbelievers simply waste what they spend in this worldly life, for belief in Islam is a pre-condition in order that such spendings be acceptable with Allah, of whatever sort they may be. They are the dwellers of the Fire, therein they will abide The parable of what they spend in this world is that of a wind of Sir; it struck the harvest of a people who did wrong against themselves and destroyed it.

117.text:
"The good they do in this worldly life is like the harvest of an evil people struck by a bitter wind" opens the verse with the likeness that shows what becomes of the spending of the people who had no faith, and the sources read the wind as the cold blast that takes the whole crop in one night, so that the labour of the season is left as nothing. "destroying it completely" closes the likeness, and the sources read the ruin as the state of every work that was not built on belief in God. "Allah never wronged them" turns from the likeness to the Lord of the harvest, and the sources read the sentence as the clearing of the Lord of the worlds of any share in the loss. "but they wronged themselves" names where the loss falls, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the men who spent without faith were the ones who wasted their own account. The verse before it had named the wealth and the children that cannot help, and this verse shows what happens to the wealth that is spent without belief, while the verses after it turn to the intimates who cannot be trusted. The likeness is set in the middle of a passage about the two companies, so that the reader weighs the wealth that is spent in this life against the account that is kept for the life that does not end, and the sources draw the likeness out through the fields of the farmers, where a single night of cold air takes what a whole season built, and the work of the hands is left on the ground without a harvest to gather.

**The likeness of the harvest and the bitter wind.**

The likeness the description of what they the disbelievers expend in the life of this world in the way of enmity towards the Prophet or in the way of voluntary almsgiving or the like is as the likeness of a wind wherein is a blast of extreme hot or cold that smote the tillage the crops of a people who have wronged themselves through unbelief and disobedience and destroyed it so that they could not profit from it; so it is with what they expend it perishes and they profit nothing from it. (The likeness of that which they spend in this life of the world) He says: the likeness of what the Jews spend when they are following Judaism (is as the likeness of a biting, icy wind which smites the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves) by not giving what is due to Allah from it, (and devastateth it) ruined it; likewise, idolatry destroys one's spending just as wind destroys the harvest. The example of what disbelievers spend in charity, and what they expect to receive of rewards, is like a wind which is extremely cold that hits the crops of a people who wronged themselves by not doing as they were instructed, ruining their crops when they had expected to have a good harvest. (The likeness of what they spend in this world is the likeness of a wind of Sir;) a frigid wind, as Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and others have said. 'Ata' said that Sir, means, 'cold and snow.' Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid are also reported to have said that Sir means, 'fire'. The likeness of what they expend in the life of this world is as the likeness of a wind wherein is a blast that smote the tillage of a people who have wronged themselves and destroyed it. Just as a gust of chill air ravages the whole harvest, so will the tempest of the Last Day (qiyamah) render valueless all such ostentatious acts.

**What they spend and what they hope for.**

The example of what disbelievers spend in charity, and what they expect to receive of rewards, is like a wind which is extremely cold that hits the crops of a people who wronged themselves by not doing as they were instructed, ruining their crops when they had expected to have a good harvest. (The likeness of what they spend in this world is the likeness of a wind of Sir;) a frigid wind, as Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and others have said. 'Ata' said that Sir, means, 'cold and snow.' Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid are also reported to have said that Sir means, 'fire'. Verse 117 declares through a similitude that disbelievers simply waste what they spend in this worldly life, for belief in Islam is a pre-condition in order that such spendings be acceptable with Allah, of whatever sort they may be. (The likeness of that which they spend in this life of the world) He says: the likeness of what the Jews spend when they are following Judaism (is as the likeness of a biting, icy wind which smites the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves) by not giving what is due to Allah from it, (and devastateth it) ruined it; likewise, idolatry destroys one's spending just as wind destroys the harvest. If they were not to wrong themselves, if they were to embrace Islam, they would have been like other Muslims who, on suffering a worldly loss, are compensated by Allah through reward and forgiveness of sins, as reported in ahadith.

**Allah never wronged them.**

God did not wrong them when they lost what they expended but they wronged themselves through unbelief which necessitated this loss. (Allah wronged them not) by thwarting the benefit of their harvest and spending, (but they did wrong themselves) through disbelief and withholding what is due to Allah from the harvest. Allah does not wrong them for He is far above any injustice, rather, they wrong themselves through their disbelief in Allah and His prophets.

**They wronged themselves.**

The similitude stresses the fact that disbelievers inflict this injustice upon themselves when their spendings go to waste in this world and remain rewardless in the Hereafter. Allah does not wrong them for He is far above any injustice, rather, they wrong themselves through their disbelief in Allah and His prophets. If they were not to wrong themselves, if they were to embrace Islam, they would have been like other Muslims who, on suffering a worldly loss, are compensated by Allah through reward and forgiveness of sins, as reported in ahadith. Disbelief also ruins the rewards of good deeds. They found no inheritance for what they spent for other than God except continuous affliction. They obtained nothing from their calculations except one tribulation after another. That is the recompense of those who reject and turn their backs.

**The people whose deeds are kept for them.**

Not all of them are alike; a party of the People of the Scripture stand for the right, they recite the verses of Allah during the hours of the night, prostrating themselves in prayer They believe in Allah and the Last Day; they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf and forbid Al-Munkar; and they hasten in good works; and they are among the righteous And whatever good they do, nothing will be rejected of them; for Allah knows well the Muttaqin (the pious)Surely, those who disbelieve, neither their properties nor their offspring will avail them against Allah. Disbelief also ruins the rewards of good deeds. God has full knowledge of their actions, for which He will reward them, and He will greatly honour them on the Day of Judgement. Remembering God in one’s solitude, worshipping Him, leading one’s life keeping in view the Hereafter, enjoining goodness upon the people around one, discouraging people from committing evil, working unstintingly for the cause of God—all such actions fulfill the divine covenant. Details appear in the present verse which gives a complementary profile of those who believed from among the people of the Book, and by becoming Muslims, they adopted the distinguishing hallmarks of the Faith that go to make believers the best of communities. But merely being a member of a community formed of one race in the name of a prophet, is not enough to earn one salvation. What is actually required of an individual is that he binds himself by a covenant with God.

118.text:
"O believers! Do not associate closely with others who would not miss a chance to harm you" opens the verse with the caution against taking as intimates those who are not of the community, and the sources read the intimates as the ones a man takes into his private business and his counsel, with the harm they would do named as the ruin they work against the believers. "Their only desire is to see you suffer" names the wish that sits behind the friendliness, and the sources read the wish as the loss of the believers that the others would count as their own gain. "Their prejudice has become evident from what they say" names the proof that has already come out, and the sources read the hatred as the thing that shows in the speech before it shows in the deed. "and what their hearts hide is far worse" names the greater danger that is kept back, and the sources read the hiding as the venom that the cool face covers over. "We have made Our revelations clear to you" names the light that has been given, and "if only you understood" closes the verse with the understanding the hearer is asked for, so that the clear words are set before the community and the blame falls on the one who will not use what has been shown to him. The caution is not against dealing with the others in the market or the street but against the counsel and the secret, since that is the door through which the ruin of a community walks. The verses before it had named the harvest that the wind takes, and this verse names the company that must not be trusted with the secrets of the community.

**The intimates who cannot be trusted.**

Allah then forbade the believers from among the Helpers to speak with the Jews or divulge secrets to them, saying: (O ye who believe! Take not) the Jews (for intimates) confidants (others than your own folk) the sincere believers, (who would spare no pains to ruin you; they love to hamper you) they love for you to sin and become idolaters as they themselves have become. O you who believe do not take as intimates as sincere friends revealing to them your secret thoughts anyone apart from yourselves from among the Jews Christians and the hypocrites; such men spare nothing to ruin you khabālan is in the accusative because the preposition that usually precedes it sc. fī’l-khabāl has been omitted that is to say they would not be remiss about corrupting you; they would love they wish for you to suffer al-‘anat means extreme hardship. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, do not take unbelievers as close friends, letting them know your secrets and private business. This was revealed about a group of believers who took some hypocrites as intimate friends and had ties with some Jewish men due to bonds of kinship, friendship, alliance, neighbourhood and milk relations which they had with them. Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse warning them against taking them as intimates for fear lest they turn them away from their religion . So, it has been enjoined upon Muslims through this verse that they should not take persons other than those from their own community as confidants and advisers, in a way that leads one into spilling the sensitive secrets of one's own government, community or state. Individuals from these tribes were also on friendly terms with other individuals from the Jewish settlements. Individuals from these tribes saw no problems in meeting their old Jewish friends with the same love and sincerity.

**The harm they wish and the pains they take.**

They will not stop trying to harm you and ruin things for you, wanting what will hurt you and making things really difficult for you. O you who believe do not take as intimates anyone apart from your selves; such men spare nothing to ruin you; they would love for you to suffer. (O ye who believe! Take not) the Jews (for intimates) confidants (others than your own folk) the sincere believers, (who would spare no pains to ruin you; they love to hamper you) they love for you to sin and become idolaters as they themselves have become. The hypocrites try their very best to confuse, oppose and harm the believers any way they can, and by using any wicked, evil means at their disposal. So, they outwardly went along with the same old relationships with'the Ansars of Madīnah, but inwardly they had turned into their enemies. When these two tribes embraced Islam, they continued to maintain their old ties with them.

**The hatred that appears from their mouths.**

Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, but what their breasts conceal is far worse. (Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, but what their breasts conceal is far worse.) meaning, enmity appears on their faces and in what they sometimes utter, as well as, the enmity they have against Islam and its people in their hearts. (Hatred is revealed by (the utterance of) their mouths) through vilification and defamation, (but that which their breasts hide is greater) but what they hide in their hearts of hatred and enmity is even greater. Their hatred and hostility has appeared in what they say; in their criticism of your faith and worship, in incidents between you, and in them giving away your secrets. Hatred is revealed by their mouths; and what their breasts conceal is yet greater. Hatred enmity towards you is revealed it is manifested by their mouths by sowing discord among you and informing the idolaters of your secret plans; and what their breasts conceal of enmity is yet greater.

**What their hearts hide from the believers.**

All this is what the Muslims can see for themselves, but the venom that lies hidden in their hearts is far too fatal. Hatred enmity towards you is revealed it is manifested by their mouths by sowing discord among you and informing the idolaters of your secret plans; and what their breasts conceal of enmity is yet greater. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, but what their breasts conceal is far worse. Their hatred and hostility has appeared in what they say; in their criticism of your faith and worship, in incidents between you, and in them giving away your secrets. However there are times when they are enraged with their deceptive cool front thrown off and the fangs of their deep hostility become clearly visible. (O ye who believe! Take not) the Jews (for intimates) confidants (others than your own folk) the sincere believers, (who would spare no pains to ruin you; they love to hamper you) they love for you to sin and become idolaters as they themselves have become.

**The revelations made clear to those who understand.**

(We have made plain for you the revelations) the signs of their resentful envy (if you will understand) what is recited to you; it is also said that this means: We have made the revelations, i.e. the commands and prohibitions, clear so that you know what I command you. Allah has made clear to you what is in your interests in this world and in the Afterlife, if you use your intellect to understand what your Lord has revealed to you. Now We have made clear to you the signs of their enmity; if you understand this then do not befriend them. (and you believe in all the Scriptures,) means, you believe in your Book, their Book, and the previous Books, while the hypocrites disbelieve in your Book, and this is why they deserve that you dislike them instead of them disliking you.

**The patience and the mindfulness that keep harm away.**

In such a situation, true believers should refrain from negative reaction and adhere steadily to the path of patience and piety 'taqwa'. If believers give proof of maintaining this kind of positive attitude, no enmity, however great, can harm them. But if you remain patient and have Taqwa, not the least harm will their cunning do to you. They will not stop trying to harm you and ruin things for you, wanting what will hurt you and making things really difficult for you. To trust the adversary after difficulties have become apparent is to further facilitate the deception of the enemy. Upholders of the latter form of faith never tolerate the call of true religion, because this would amount to displacing themselves from their position of eminence.

119.text:
"Here you are" opens the verse with a call that brings the community to look at itself, and the sources read it as a word of wonder at the state of the believers who were giving affection to people who would not give it back. "You love them but they do not love you" names the inequality, and the sources read the love of the believers as the good they wished for the others and the affection they carried for them, while the others wished them harm. "and you believe in all Scriptures" names the reason the inequality is strange, since the believers accept the books that came before without any dislike of the people they were sent to, and the sources notice that the others neither accept the book of the believers nor hold their own books as they should. "When they meet you they say, We believe" names the face they wear in the street, and the sources read the words as the speech of the tongue with no ground beneath it. "But when alone" names the other face, and "they bite their fingertips in rage, Say, O Prophet" carries the verse to the command given to the messenger to answer them. "May you die of your rage" is the answer itself, and the sources read it as the statement that the anger they carry will keep eating them and will not touch the believers. "Surely Allah knows best what is hidden in the heart" closes the verse with the knowledge that opens the breast, so that the hidden envy is named and brought into the open. The verse is set in the middle of a passage about the people of the book, and it draws the line between the affection that the believers carry for everyone and the envy that answers it from the other side, so that the community learns to measure people by what their hearts hold and not by the words their mouths make. The sources also carry the account of the day when the two tribes of Madīnah were set against one another by such talk, and they read the verse as the guard that the community was given against the flattery of the tongue and the secret wish for its ruin. The verse before it had warned the believers against taking such people as intimates, and this verse shows why the warning is needed, while the verse after it names what the others feel when good or evil comes to the believers.

**You love them but they do not love you.**

It is you, O believers, who love these people, and want goodness for them, but they do not love you, and do not wish you well. After that, in verse ; Muslims have been told that it is certainly strange that you go about loving them as friends, yet they are no friends of yours. (Lo! Ye are) O group of believers (those who love them) who love the Jews because of the ties of marriage and suckling (though they love you not) because of the Religion, (and ye believe in all the Scripture) you acknowledge all the revealed Books and messengers while they do not. Lo hā ‘lo!’ is for calling attention to something there you are O believers you love them on account of their kinship and their pretence of friendship towards you but they love you not since they oppose you in religion; you believe in the Book all of it that is to say in the Books all of them but they do not believe in your Book and when they meet you they say ‘We believe’ but when they are alone they bite at you their fingertips in rage in extreme fury at what they see of your mutual affection the biting of the fingertips is used to figuratively express the severity of rage even if there be no biting involved. They wanted good for them and attached their hearts to their submission. They wanted their salvation and did not hold back God's mercy from them-whether they were acquaintances or strangers. They grieved at the good that reached them and became happy at the bad.

**You believe in all the Scriptures.**

Still more unusual is the situation because you believe in all Scriptures without any reservations as to the people they address, the time when they were sent down and the prophet they were revealed to. Rather, they hate you, while you have faith in all of the scriptures, including their scriptures; yet they do not have faith in the Scripture which Allah revealed to your Prophet. (and you believe in all the Scriptures,) means, you believe in your Book, their Book, and the previous Books, while the hypocrites disbelieve in your Book, and this is why they deserve that you dislike them instead of them disliking you. Contrary to this, they do not accept your Book and your Prophet . Their belief in their own Books is not correct either.

**When they meet you they say, We believe.**

(When they) the hypocrites among the Jews (fall in with you they say: We believe) in Muhammad and the Qur'an and we acknowledge that his traits and description are in our Scripture; (but when they go apart) and meet with each other (they bite their finger tips at you, for rage. Say: Perish in your rage! Lo! Allah is Aware of what is hidden in (your) breasts) He is Aware of what is in your heart of hatred and enmity. If they meet you they say with their tongues, ‘We have faith’, yet when they are alone together they bite the tips of their fingers in distress and rage because of how united you are, the strength of Islam, and because of their own humiliation and shame. Lo hā ‘lo!’ is for calling attention to something there you are O believers you love them on account of their kinship and their pretence of friendship towards you but they love you not since they oppose you in religion; you believe in the Book all of it that is to say in the Books all of them but they do not believe in your Book and when they meet you they say ‘We believe’ but when they are alone they bite at you their fingertips in rage in extreme fury at what they see of your mutual affection the biting of the fingertips is used to figuratively express the severity of rage even if there be no biting involved. The hypocrites try their very best to confuse, oppose and harm the believers any way they can, and by using any wicked, evil means at their disposal. Given this state of affairs it would have been expected that they should have been affectionate towards you and you should have been the ones to give them a cold shoulder. But, what is happening here is just the reverse of what it should have been.'.

**They bite their fingertips in rage.**

If they meet you they say with their tongues, ‘We have faith’, yet when they are alone together they bite the tips of their fingers in distress and rage because of how united you are, the strength of Islam, and because of their own humiliation and shame. Lo hā ‘lo!’ is for calling attention to something there you are O believers you love them on account of their kinship and their pretence of friendship towards you but they love you not since they oppose you in religion; you believe in the Book all of it that is to say in the Books all of them but they do not believe in your Book and when they meet you they say ‘We believe’ but when they are alone they bite at you their fingertips in rage in extreme fury at what they see of your mutual affection the biting of the fingertips is used to figuratively express the severity of rage even if there be no biting involved. " As for the unbelievers, those who had no limpidness in their hearts or loyalty in their natures, they never wanted good for the people of faith, nor did they love them. The unbeliever is base and bad-wanting, for what is fitting for unbelief is baseness and unseemliness. Indeed, everyone does what is fitting for him, for "The pot pours what is inside it. " The person of faith is generous and lovingly kind, for what is fitting for faith is generosity and chivalry.

**What Allah knows of what the hearts hide.**

Certainly, Allah knows what is in the breasts (all the secrets). (Say: "Perish in your rage. Certainly, Allah knows what is in the breasts (all the secrets).") for no matter how much you envy the believers and feel rage towards them, know that Allah shall perfect His favor on His believing servants, complete His religion, raise high His Word and give dominance to His religion. Allah knows what faith and disbelief and what good and evil there is in people’s hearts. Say ‘Perish in your rage that is be this way until the end of your lives for you shall not see what will please you; God knows what is in the breasts’ what is in the hearts including that which these conceal. Tell these people, O Prophet, to stay as they are until they die in their rage. What is it with me that I invite you to salvation and you invite me to the Fire?" [40:41].

120.text:
"When you believers are touched with good, they grieve" opens the verse with the state of the others at the sight of a blessing that reaches the believers, and the sources read the good as the victory or the increase that God gives, with the grief of the others named as the sign of what their hearts carry. "but when you are afflicted with evil, they rejoice, Yet" names the other half of the same envy, and the sources read the rejoicing as the pleasure they take in the harm that touches the community. "if you are patient and mindful of Allah" turns the verse to the duty of the believers in the middle of the harm, and the sources read the patience as the steady holding of the heart and the mindfulness as the fear that keeps a person inside the commands of his Lord. "their schemes will not harm you in the least" carries the promise that follows the two duties, and the sources read it as the pledge that the cunning of the others will not reach the believers while the two things stand, since patience and the fear of God have been set by the book as the guard against every trial. "Surely Allah is Fully Aware of what they do" closes the verse with the knowledge that sees the plotting, and the sources read the sentence as the warning that nothing of the scheming is lost and that the One who watches will turn it on its own people. The verse before it had named the love the believers carry and the rage that answers it, and this verse names the test the community meets in the days of trouble.

**The grief at good and the joy at evil.**

If a good befalls you, it grieves them, but if some evil overtakes you, they rejoice at it. (If a lucky chance) conquest and booty (befall you, it is evil unto them) the Jews and hypocrites do not like it, (and if disaster) drought, killing and defeat (strike you they rejoice thereat) they like it. If good fortune a favour such as victory or booty befalls you it is evil for them it grieves them; but if evil such as defeat or drought befalls you they rejoice thereat the conditional statement here is semantically connected to the previous conditional and what comes in between is a parenthetical statement the meaning being that their enmity towards you is endless so why do you befriend them? If a blessing comes to you in the forms of victory over an enemy, or an increase in wealth or children, then worry and sadness overcomes them; and if a misfortune hits you, such as the victory of an enemy over you, or a decrease in wealth or children, then they are happy, rejoicing at your misfortune. If good fortune befalls you it is evil for them; but if evil befalls you they rejoice thereat. The mentality of disbelievers has been further clarified by saying: in the first part of verse 120 which has been translated as, 'if something good happens to you, it annoys them and if something evil befalls you, they are delighted with it.'.

**If you are patient and mindful of Allah.**

And if you keep patience and fear Allah, their cunning shall not harm you at all. The Holy Qur'an has prescribed Sabr (patience, endurance) and Taqwa (fear of Allah) as an effective measure against all hardships. This elemental teaching has been conveyed to Muslims not only here but also at many other places in the Qur'an. (But if you persevere) in the face of their harm (and keep from evil) transgressing against Allah (their guile) their enmity and deeds (will never harm you. Lo! Allah is Surrounding) Allah knows (what they do) of contravention and enmity. If you are patient with Allah’s commands and decree, and are mindful of not earning Allah’s anger, then their tricks and attempts to hurt you will not harm you. Yet if you endure and fear [God] their guile will not hurt you at all; God encompasses what they do. Here too, prosperity and success have been tied with Sabr and Taqwa.

**Their schemes will not harm you in the least.**

(But if you persevere) in the face of their harm (and keep from evil) transgressing against Allah (their guile) their enmity and deeds (will never harm you. Lo! Allah is Surrounding) Allah knows (what they do) of contravention and enmity. Yet if you endure their harm and fear God by not befriending them and so on their guile will not hurt you read either lā yadirkum or lā yadurrukum at all; God encompasses what they do ya‘malūn or may be read ta‘malūn ‘what you do’ He has knowledge of it and will requite them for it. If you are patient with Allah’s commands and decree, and are mindful of not earning Allah’s anger, then their tricks and attempts to hurt you will not harm you. Yet if you endure and fear [God] their guile will not hurt you at all; God encompasses what they do. If you stay patient and fear Allah and they come upon you in this heat of theirs, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels having distinct marks.

**Allah is Fully Aware of what they do.**

Allah encompasses all their plotting and what they do, and will make them fail. Yet if you endure and fear [God] their guile will not hurt you at all; God encompasses what they do. And if you keep patience and fear Allah, their cunning shall not harm you at all. (Say: "Perish in your rage. Certainly, Allah knows what is in the breasts (all the secrets).") for no matter how much you envy the believers and feel rage towards them, know that Allah shall perfect His favor on His believing servants, complete His religion, raise high His Word and give dominance to His religion.

**The heart that is opened to all people.**

The existence of love in the hearts of true believers for the People of the Book and the lack of love in the hearts of the latter for the believers shows who really subscribes to the truth and who does not. God is the Creator and Sustainer of all human beings, so whoever finds God in the real sense of the word, will open his heart to all God’s creatures. For him all human beings equally become the family of God. Then he begins to like for everyone what he likes for himself. But those who have not found God in the real sense of the word, those who have not subordinated their will to the will of God and who live only on the plane of the self, regard life’s possessions as paramount, both at the personal and the communal level. This mentality makes them inimical to anyone who appears to be against their interests—who is not, in short, a member of their own community.

**The patience and the fear of Allah.**

And if you keep patience and fear Allah, their cunning shall not harm you at all. The Holy Qur'an has prescribed Sabr (patience, endurance) and Taqwa (fear of Allah) as an effective measure against all hardships. O those who believe, be patient, be more patient than others, and guard your frontiers, and fear Allah so that you may be successful. Yet if you endure and fear [God] their guile will not hurt you at all; God encompasses what they do. This elemental teaching has been conveyed to Muslims not only here but also at many other places in the Qur'an. Here too, prosperity and success have been tied with Sabr and Taqwa. In spite of believing in God, they tend to forget that this world was made by God, and that no strategy can be effective here without God’s approval. This verse alludes to those who abandon the path of spiritual desire irāda and return to the states of the people of habit ahl al-ʿāda. They are not happy to see an aspirant murīd have a breakthrough nafādh; rather they are glad when they see listlessness in a seeker qāṣid.

121.text:
"Remember, O Prophet" opens the verse with the call to hold a day of the past in view, and the sources read the remembering as the bringing of the morning of Uhud back before the community. "when you left your home in the early morning to position the believers in the battlefield" names the deed that is recalled, and the sources read the leaving as the going out from the family and the house at dawn, with the posting of the men named as the placing of each band at its station before the fighting began. "And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" closes the verse with the two names that watch the day, and the sources read them as the hearing of every word spoken in the ranks and the knowledge of every plan kept in the breast. The verses before it had named the schemes of the others and the patience that guards the believers, and this verse turns to the battle in which the guard was tested, while the verses after it name the two bands whose hearts were about to fail and the help that held them. The sources carry the account of the men who broke away on the road and of the archers who were set at the foot of the mountain, so that the day is read with its stations and its orders, and the reader sees the placing of the lines as the work of the man who was told where to stand. The day is named in the book so that the community that reads it later learns how the help of God met a people who had done what they could with the means in their hands, and how the standing of the lines on that morning was the work of the man who led them.

**The morning when the believers were placed at their stations.**

And mention O Muhammad when you went forth at dawn from your family at Medina to assign the believers to have them occupy their places stations for them to stand at for battle and God hears what you say knows your circumstances this was the day of the battle of Uhud. (And remember when thou settedst forth at daybreak from thy housefolk) when you left Medina for Uhud (to assign to the believers their positions for the battle) against their enemies, (Allah was Hearer) of your speech, (Knower) of what befell you and of your leaving the positions which were assigned to you. And (remember) when you left your household in the morning to post the believers at their stations for the battle (of Uhud). Verse 121 begins with the words, (When you left your house in the morning in order to place the believers in positions for fighting). you went forth at dawn from your family to assign the believers their places for battle and God hears knows. Remember, O Prophet, when some of the believers disobeyed the instruction of Allah and His Messenger, and this happened when you left Medina to fight the idolaters in the Battle of Uḥud, after you had posted the believers in their places for battle, and their positions were clear.

**The home that was left at daybreak.**

The word , indicates that the Holy Prophet was with his family at that time and when the time came to leave, he left, leaving his family behind him, even though this attack was aimed at Madīnah. When there is the command of Allah, it is expected that the love of family and home should not stop one from obeying it. In the meantime, the Holy Prophet went to his house and when he came out, he had his armour on. The answer was: 'It does not behoove a prophet, once he has put on his armour and taken up his arms, to put them off without fighting.' This one sentence is sufficient to clarify the difference between a prophet and a non-prophet. (And when thou settedst forth at daybreak from thy housefolk) up to His saying (Then, after grief, He sent down security for you) [3:154]' .

**What Allah hears and what Allah knows.**

The verse ends with the words, (And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing). Allah hears whatever you say and knows whatever you do. you went forth at dawn from your family to assign the believers their places for battle and God hears knows. And Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower When two parties from among you were about to lose heart, but Allah was their Wali (Supporter and Protector). I said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf: 'Uncle, tell me about what happened to you at Uhud?' He said: 'Read the first one hundred and twenty verses of Al 'Imran you will find your answer: However, Allah gave victory to His Messenger , supported His revelation, and illuminated success on the faces of the Prophet and his following.

**The thousand who marched out with the Prophet.**

When the Holy Prophet left Madīnah on his way to confront the enemy, he had about a thousand men with him, but the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy broke off enroute with about three hundred men, saying: 'When my advice was rejected and action was taken on the advice of others, why should we fight and why should we endanger our lives?' Obviously, most of his comrades were hypocrites, yet there were some Muslims too who swallowed the bait and tugged along with them. The Prophet s set out with 1000 or 950 men while the idolaters numbered 3000. The Prophet pitched camp at the ravine on Saturday 7th of Shawwāl in year 3 of the Hijra. He arranged their lines and placed a group of archers under the command of ‘Abd Allāh b. Jubayr at the foot of the mountain and said to them ‘Defend us with your arrows in case they come up from behind us and remain here whether we are being defeated or on the verge of victory’. He had his back and that of his troops to Uhud. (Keep the horsemen away from us, and be aware that we might be attacked from your direction. If victory was for or against us, remain in your positions. And even if you see us being picked up by birds, do not abandon your positions.)

**The battlefield and the succour that came.**

These verses were revealed after the Battle of Uhud which took place in the third year after hijrah. The enemy forces numbered three thousand, while the Muslims who rose in defence were initially only one thousand in number. When three hundred hypocritical Muslims, led by ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy, deserted, some of the Madinan Muslims were disheartened at this, so the Prophet reminded them that they had come forth to defend themselves, relying on God rather than only on themselves. This special succour of God was sent to the whole group of believers at a time when, by exploiting the weakness of the Muslims, the enemies had overcome them, and had every opportunity to crush the Muslim forces completely. But the enemy army, in spite of being victorious, retreated from the battlefield. This astonishing event in military history took place because of the special divine succour, which diverted the enemy towards ‘Makkah’ rather than ‘Madīnah’ (the Muslim area). When the Holy Prophet left Madīnah on his way to confront the enemy, he had about a thousand men with him, but the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy broke off enroute with about three hundred men, saying: 'When my advice was rejected and action was taken on the advice of others, why should we fight and why should we endanger our lives?' Obviously, most of his comrades were hypocrites, yet there were some Muslims too who swallowed the bait and tugged along with them. Defeat was about to come when, in the right moment, the Companions scattered on the battlefield came to know that the Holy Prophet was alive.

**The command that was laid on him for the battle.**

(And (remember) when you left your household in the morning to post the believers at their stations for the battle)[3:121], designating them to various positions, dividing the army to the left and right sides and placing them wherever you command them. He put [the Prophet] in charge of assigning the places for battle del egating His command to him. And (remember) when you left your household in the morning to post the believers at their stations for the battle (of Uhud). Then He made manifest in this matter the hidden things of His secret. If, due to the severity of circumstances, believers show some temporary weakness, God does not leave them to fend for themselves. He sends His special succour to restore their faith.

122.text:
"Remember when two groups among you believers were about to cower" opens the verse by naming the two bands whose courage was slipping on the way to the fight, and the sources read the cowering as the fear that came over them when the men who had turned back broke away from the army. "then Allah reassured them" names the help that held them, and the sources read the reassurance as the steadiness that was placed in their hearts so that they stayed in the field and did not leave the ranks. "So in Allah let the believers put their trust" closes the verse with the duty that answers the whole account, and the sources read the trust as the leaning of the heart on God after a person has gathered whatever means are in his hands, since the two things are held together in the teaching of the book. The verse before it had named the morning when the believers were posted, and this verse names what happened in the hearts of two bands of them during that day, while the verse after it names the victory that God had already given them at Badr when they were few. The sources also carry the names of the two bands and the words of the men who turned away, so that the mercy of the verse is seen against the state of the day, and the reader learns that the heart that stands steady in the hour of fear was kept by the hand of its Lord and not by the numbers in the field.

**The two groups that were about to cower.**

(When two parties from among you were about to lose heart) was revealed about us, [the two Muslim tribes of] Bani Harithah and Bani Salamah. (When two parties of you almost) two tribes of believers, the Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, hid the fact that they almost (fell away) shrank away from fighting against the enemy on the Day of Uhud, (and Allah was their Protecting Friend) He preserved them and prevented them from doing so. When idh substitutes for the previous idh two parties of you the Banū Salima and the Banū Hāritha the two flanks of the army were about to lose heart about to shrink from the battle and retreat after ‘Abd Allāh b. Remember, O Prophet, what happened to two groups of the believers from Banī Salamah and Banī Ḥārithah, when they became weak and almost withdrew when the hypocrites drew back; but Allah aided them, making them firm in fighting, and turning them away from what they had been on the edge of doing. Next comes verses 122 beginning with the words (When two of your groups tended to lose heart while Allah was their guardian). These 'two groups lost the courage to fight when they saw the hypocrite, Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his men breaking away. He Ibn Ubayy said ‘Why should we get ourselves and our children killed?’ and he also said to Abū Jābir al-Salamī — who had said to him ‘I implore you by God for your Prophet’s sake and yours’ — ‘If we knew how to fight we would follow you!

**Then Allah reassured them.**

’ But God then made them the Banū Salima and the Banū Hāritha steadfast and they did not abandon the field; and God was their Protector their Helper and let the believers rely on God let them place their trust in Him and none other. And Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower When two parties from among you were about to lose heart, but Allah was their Wali (Supporter and Protector). Then, the very Qur'anic statement, (while Allah was their guardian) is a testimony to their perfect faith. "No doubt, the verse contains a complaint against us, but at the same time it bears a good news for us in the words: ; (while Allah was their guardian). parties of you were about to lose heart; and God was their protector and let the believers rely on God. Remember, O Prophet, what happened to two groups of the believers from Banī Salamah and Banī Ḥārithah, when they became weak and almost withdrew when the hypocrites drew back; but Allah aided them, making them firm in fighting, and turning them away from what they had been on the edge of doing.

**In Allah let the believers put their trust.**

"And it is in Allah alone that the believers must place their trust. So, let those who have faith look to Allah alone for support, no matter what may happen to them. And in Allah should the believers put their trust And Allah has already made you victorious at Badr, when you were a weak little force. parties of you were about to lose heart; and God was their protector and let the believers rely on God. (but Allah was their Wali (Supporter and Protector)[3:122]."

**The means that are collected and the trust that follows.**

A Muslim would, given his ability and means, collect all sorts of necessary material support, yet when it comes to trust and tawakkul that he would place in none but Allah. On the contrary, one should collect what is obviously needed to the best of his ability, use it, and then, let Allah take care of the outcome. Not that they have to ignore material needs of the combat; of course, they should have whatever they can get together subject to their means, but the crucial thing is that they must place their total trust in Allah, and Allah alone. The companions were weary then and said to each other, "Did we compel the Messenger of Allah to go out?

**The succour that came on the day of Uhud.**

These verses were revealed after the Battle of Uhud which took place in the third year after hijrah. When three hundred hypocritical Muslims, led by ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy, deserted, some of the Madinan Muslims were disheartened at this, so the Prophet reminded them that they had come forth to defend themselves, relying on God rather than only on themselves. If, due to the severity of circumstances, believers show some temporary weakness, God does not leave them to fend for themselves. He sends His special succour to restore their faith. This special succour of God was sent to the whole group of believers at a time when, by exploiting the weakness of the Muslims, the enemies had overcome them, and had every opportunity to crush the Muslim forces completely. This astonishing event in military history took place because of the special divine succour, which diverted the enemy towards ‘Makkah’ rather than ‘Madīnah’ (the Muslim area). Ubayy the hypocrite and his companions began to retreat.

123.text:
"Indeed, Allah made you victorious at Badr when you were vastly outnumbered" opens the verse with the day that is set before the community as the proof of what their Lord has done for them, and the sources read the outnumbering as the smallness of their number and their gear on that day at the wells of Badr. "So be mindful of Allah" names the duty that the memory is meant to produce, and the sources read the mindfulness as the keeping of the commands and the standing inside the obedience of the Lord. "perhaps you will be grateful" closes the verse with the aim of the mindfulness, and the sources read the gratitude as the state that the favour is meant to grow in the heart that remembers who gave it. The verses before it had named the two bands whose hearts were held steady, and this verse names the earlier victory that the help of God had already given them, so that the faith of the community is grounded in what they have seen and not only in what they hope for, since the community that remembers a day of help is a community that keeps its ground on the day of trial.

**The victory of Badr when they were few.**

(And Allah has already made you victorious at Badr,)[3:123] meaning, during the battle of Badr, which occurred on a Friday, the seventeenth of Ramadan, in the second year of Hijrah. (Allah had already given you the victory at Badr) on the day of the Battle of Badr, (when ye were contemptible) few in number: 313 men. Allah gave you victory over the idolaters in the Battle of Badr despite your small numbers and resources. When they were defeated the following was revealed as a way of reminding them of God’s favour God already gave you victory at Badr a location between Makkah and Medina when you were contemptible few in number and weapons. God surely helped you at Badr while you were abased. The expression translated as 'when you were weak' means that 'you were, at that time, few in numbers and materials'.

**So be mindful of Allah.**

The verse ends with the statement: ‌ (So, fear Allah, that you may be grateful). (So have Taqwa of Allah that you may be grateful.)[3:123], means, fulfill the obligations of His obedience. Therefore, be Mindful so that you may be thankful for the blessings He has given you. (So observe your duty to Allah) fear Allah regarding the matter of war and do not disobey the leader who is in charge of you (in order that ye may be thankful) in order that you are thankful for his help and blessing. So fear God in order that you might be thankful for His blessings.

**The day of Badr and the place where it was fought.**

Badr is located about eighty miles south-west of Madīnah and used to be a halting-place while travelling between Makkah and Madīnah, before the modern Tariq al-Hijrah was commissioned into service which by passes it. At that time, Badr was known for its abundance of water, something very important in the desert zones of Arabia. The first armed encounter between believers and disbelievers came to pass at this spot on Friday, Ramadan al-Mubarak, Hijrah year 2 which fell on March 11, 624 A.D. (And Allah has already made you victorious at Badr,)[3:123] meaning, during the battle of Badr, which occurred on a Friday, the seventeenth of Ramadan, in the second year of Hijrah. The day of Badr is known as Yawm Al-Furqan [the Day of the Clarification], by which Allah gave victory and dominance to Islam and its people and disgraced and destroyed Shirk, even though the Muslims were few. The caravan that Abu Sufyan led (before Badr) returned safely to Makkah, prompting the remaining Makkan leaders and the children of those who were killed at Badr to demand from Abu Sufyan to, "Spend this money on fighting Muhammad!

**The place called Badr.**

Badr is located about eighty miles south-west of Madīnah and used to be a halting-place while travelling between Makkah and Madīnah, before the modern Tariq al-Hijrah was commissioned into service which by passes it. At that time, Badr was known for its abundance of water, something very important in the desert zones of Arabia. The day of Badr is known as Yawm Al-Furqan [the Day of the Clarification], by which Allah gave victory and dominance to Islam and its people and disgraced and destroyed Shirk, even though the Muslims were few. The first armed encounter between believers and disbelievers came to pass at this spot on Friday, Ramadan al-Mubarak, Hijrah year 2 which fell on March 11, 624 A.D. On a superficial view, this battle appears to be a local tribal war, but the truth is that it has charted a revolutionary course in the history of the world, therefore, the Holy Qur'an calls it Yawm al-Furgan (a day of distinction). According to Professor Philip Hitti, this was Islam's first clear victory. Allah willing, we will mention the details of this battle later on, if Allah wills.

**The help that came to the believers.**

This special succour of God was sent to the whole group of believers at a time when, by exploiting the weakness of the Muslims, the enemies had overcome them, and had every opportunity to crush the Muslim forces completely. If, due to the severity of circumstances, believers show some temporary weakness, God does not leave them to fend for themselves. But the enemy army, in spite of being victorious, retreated from the battlefield. It was the defeated who pursued the victorious. Allah gave you victory over the idolaters in the Battle of Badr despite your small numbers and resources.

124.text:
"Remember, O Prophet" opens the verse with the call to hold out a word that was spoken on the day of the fight, and the sources read the remembering as the bringing of that promise before the men who heard it. "when you said to the believers" names the ones who were addressed, and the sources read them as the men who had come out with the messenger and whose hearts were in need of a word. "Is it not enough that your Lord will send down a reinforcement of three thousand angels for your aid" names the question that carries the promise, and the sources read the sending down as the help that comes from above the means that the men could count, with the three thousand named as the number that was set before them. The verses before it had named the two bands whose hearts were held steady and the victory that God had given at Badr, and this verse shows how the hearts of the community were carried on the day when the numbers were against them, while the verse after it names the firmness and the mindfulness that the promise was tied to, so that the help of God is read with the state of the hearts that receive it. The sources also follow what the coming down of the angels was meant to do, and they read the whole account as the comfort of a people who had no strength of their own to lean on, since the number of the men in the field was one thing and the number of the angels that had been told to them was another.

**The promise of the three thousand angels.**

(Is it not sufficient for you) regarding your enemy (that your Lord should support) that your Lord should help you (you with three thousand angels sent down?) from heaven to help you. (And when thou didst say unto the believers) on the Day of Uhud: When idh an adverbial qualifier of nasarakum ‘He gave you victory’ in the previous verse you were saying to the believers promising them as reassurance for them ‘Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you that He should succour you with three thousand angels sent down? read munzalīn or munazzalīn ‘sent down’. were saying to the believers Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent downḍ Yea if you are patient and fear and they come against you instantly your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels accoutred. Remember, O Prophet, when you roused the believers during the battle of Badr, reassuring them after they heard that reinforcements were on their way for the idolaters, by asking whether it was not enough for them that Allah should help them with three thousand angels sent down from Him to reinforce them in the battle.

**What the angels were sent to do.**

This Ayah means, "Allah sent down angels and told you about their descent to encourage you and to comfort and reassure your hearts. The tranquility sent by the Real to the heart of MuṣṬafā was from God without intermediary while the strengthening of the hearts of the believers was through the intermediary of the Messenger . If not for [the doubt that] remained in them he would not have replied to them telling [them] of the help [that would] be sent in the angel malak. Why tell of the angel when the affair is entirely in the hand of the King malikḍ. The word "in succession" means they follow each other and thus indicates that thousands more will follow them.

**The day of Uhud and the weakness of the believers.**

These verses were revealed after the Battle of Uhud which took place in the third year after hijrah. The enemy forces numbered three thousand, while the Muslims who rose in defence were initially only one thousand in number. When three hundred hypocritical Muslims, led by ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy, deserted, some of the Madinan Muslims were disheartened at this, so the Prophet reminded them that they had come forth to defend themselves, relying on God rather than only on themselves. This special succour of God was sent to the whole group of believers at a time when, by exploiting the weakness of the Muslims, the enemies had overcome them, and had every opportunity to crush the Muslim forces completely. The expression translated as 'when you were weak' means that 'you were, at that time, few in numbers and materials'. According to strong and authentic narrations, the number of Muslims was 313. The first armed encounter between believers and disbelievers came to pass at this spot on Friday, Ramadan al-Mubarak, Hijrah year 2 which fell on March 11, 624 A.D.

**What the verse means by the angels that follow.**

This Ayah means, "Allah sent down angels and told you about their descent to encourage you and to comfort and reassure your hearts. The word "in succession" means they follow each other and thus indicates that thousands more will follow them. (and they will come rushing) means, they (angels) will rush to you instantaneously. Al-'Awfi said that Ibn 'Abbas said that the Ayah means, "All at once". It is also said that it means, before their anger subsides (against the disbelievers). "But, if you hold on to patience and have Taqwa, and the enemy comes rushing at you; your Lord will help you with five thousand angels having marks (of distinction). And Allah certainly supported you at Badr when you were weak.

125.text:
"Most certainly, if you believers are firm and mindful of Allah and the enemy launches a sudden attack on you" opens the verse with the two states that the help was tied to, and the sources read the firmness as the patience that keeps a man at his post and the mindfulness as the fear of God that keeps him inside the commands of his Lord, with the sudden attack named as the rush of the enemy before the lines can be set. "Allah will reinforce you with five thousand angels designated for battle" closes the verse with the promise that answers the attack, and the sources read the five thousand as the number that grows on the earlier three thousand, with the angels named as marked for the fight and sent to make the hearts of the believers stand. The verses before it had named the three thousand that were promised to a people who had asked whether it was enough, and this verse shows what the help becomes when the two states are kept, while the verses after it name the purpose of the whole reinforcement and the victory that comes from God alone. The sources also carry the account of what the angels did on the field and the other way that the help of God reaches a community, when a part of the enemy is brought to the answer instead of being destroyed, and the weakness of the community becomes the ground on which the power of its Lord is shown.

**The patience and the mindfulness that the help is tied to.**

(But if you hold on to patience and have Taqwa,)[3:125] means, if you observe patience while fighting the enemy, all the while fearing Me and obeying My command. it is sufficient to you, (but if you persevere) in war with your Prophet, (and keep from evil) and keep from contravening and disobeying Him, the people of Makkah (attack you suddenly) from the direction of Makkah, (your Lord will help you) against your enemy (with five thousand angels sweeping on) 5,000 marked angels; it is also said this means: 5,000 angels wearing turbans of wool. "But, if you hold on to patience and have Taqwa, and the enemy comes rushing at you; your Lord will help you with five thousand angels having marks (of distinction). Indeed, that is enough, and there is good news for you of more aid from Allah if you are courageous in fighting and are Mindful: if the reinforcements of your enemies come rushing at you, then your Lord will help you with five thousand angels, with clear marks on them and their horses. Success depends more on patience and being God-fearing (taqwa) than on material resources. were saying to the believers Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent downḍ Yea if you are patient and fear and they come against you instantly your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels accoutred.

**The five thousand angels marked for the fight.**

In the present verse of Surah 'Al- Imran, the promise begins with three thousand, then goes up to five. The verse of Surah al-Anfal carries the promise of one thousand angels. In sūrat al-Anfāl it is stated with a thousand Q. 89 because at first He reinforced them with this thousand then it became three thousand then five thousand as God says if you are patient in encountering the enemy and fear God in not contravening His command and they the idolaters come against you instantly your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels accoutred’ read musawimmīn or musawammīn that is to say distinctively marked for the battle. "But, if you hold on to patience and have Taqwa, and the enemy comes rushing at you; your Lord will help you with five thousand angels having marks (of distinction). The fact is that Muslims noticed the thousand-strong force of the enemy in the battle of Badr, as stated in Surah al-Anfal, and compared it with their total count of three hundred and thirteen, so they invoked the help of Allah Almighty against such heavy odds. When Allah Almighty has endowed His angels with such power that just one of them could over-turn an entire habitation, very much like what happened with the land of the people of Lut which was overturned single-handedly by the angel Jibra'il why was it necessary to send out an army of angels?

**What the angels did on the field of battle.**

Indeed they were patient and God fulfilled His promise to them so that the angels fought together with them riding upon piebald horses wearing yellow or white turbans let loose down to their shoulders. According to some hadith narrations, when an angel decided to attack a disbeliever, the head of the disbeliever slid of his body all by itself.1 It has also been reported that some noble Companions heard the voice of Jibra'il saying, 'Charge, Haizum!'2 Some of them saw some angels (Muslim). Evidences prove that the angels of Allah did a few things to impress upon Muslims that the angels too are participating in fighting as a sort of assurance that His support through the angels is there. For instance, they may simply assure the believers that angels are standing ready to help them - by appearing before them, by their voice signs or by some other method - as was witnessed in the battle of Badr where all these methods were used.
