The news of the defeat of the idolators [at Badr] reached Kurz and he did not reinforce them, and thus, Allah did not reinforce the Muslims with the five (thousands of angels)."

**The strength that is placed in the hearts.**

Here, the address is to the angels and they have been asked to see that Muslims do not get anxious and that their hearts stay firm. The tranquility sent by the Real to the heart of MuṣṬafā was from God without intermediary while the strengthening of the hearts of the believers was through the intermediary of the Messenger . If not for [the doubt that] remained in them he would not have replied to them telling [them] of the help [that would] be sent in the angel malak. Why tell of the angel when the affair is entirely in the hand of the King malikḍ. This Ayah means, "Allah sent down angels and told you about their descent to encourage you and to comfort and reassure your hearts.

**The two ways in which the help of God reaches a community.**

Those who fear and trust God can receive His divine succour in two ways: first, by His causing a section of the enemy to be brought to repentance and submission, thus reducing their number; and second, by His bringing about their outright defeat. The first kind of God’s succour comes by way of dawah work. God opens to the truth the hearts of those opponents, who have some receptivity in them, and thus they join the believers. In this way they weaken the enemy forces and strengthen the believers’ ranks. By the second method, God gives strength and courage to the believers and enables them to emerge victorious. Believers should never be upset at any lack of manpower or resources. When small in number, they should have the conviction that God will amply compensate for this by sending angels down to help them. When confronted with inadequate resources, they should trust God to create such situations as will compensate for this deficiency.

126.text:
"Allah ordained this reinforcement only as good news for you and reassurance for your hearts" opens the verse with the purpose of the help that was named, and the sources read the good news as the word that a people needs when the ground under them is shaking and the reassurance as the rest that is placed in the breast. "And victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty, All-Wise" closes the verse with the turn to the One who gives the win, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that an army of men or an army of angels is not what wins a field, since the power and the wisdom belong to the Lord who set the whole account in order. The verse before it had named the firmness and the mindfulness and the five thousand angels, and this verse shows what the promise was for, so that no man keeps the help itself as a thing to lean on apart from the One who sent it. The sources also draw the practice of God with His friends out of the verse, since the help that is sent is what strengthens the hearts and turns them from every other support.

**The good news and the rest of the hearts.**

What God ordained that is of reinforcement was only as a good tiding to you of victory and that your hearts might be at peace that they might be at rest and not be terrified by the large number of the enemy as compared to your small number. (Allah ordained this) Allah mentioned this help (only as a message of good cheer for you) that you shall triumph, (and that thereby your hearts might be at rest. Victory) by means of the help of angels (cometh only from Allah, the Mighty) in His vengeance against those who do not believe in Him, (the Wise) in giving triumph and sovereignty to whomever He will; it is also said (the Wise) means: the Wise in that which befell you on the Day of Uhud. What God ordained was only as a good tiding to you and that your hearts might be at peace. Allah did not tell you of this reinforcement with angels, except as news to please and reassure your hearts. Instead, the purpose was to give the believers the good news of victory to comfort them and to strengthen their hearts.

**Victory comes only from Allah.**

Victory comes only from God the Mighty the Wise He gives it to whomever He will and victory comes not because of a large army. For in fact, victory does not just come through material means, but comes only from Allah the Mighty, Who no one has any authority over, Wise in His decree and sacred laws. And there is no victory except from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or expose them to infamy, so that they retire frustrated Not for you is the decision; whether He turns in mercy to (pardon) them or punishes them; verily, they are the wrongdoers And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. You should know that victory only comes from Allah and that if He willed, He would have defeated your enemy without you having to fight them.

**The Almighty and the All-Wise.**

This Ayah means, "Allah is the Almighty Whose power can never be undermined, and He has the perfect wisdom in His decrees and in all His decisions. If Allah Almighty had willed that countries be conquered through armies of angels, the very name of disbelief and disbelievers would have been effaced from the face of the earth, not to say much about governments and empires. But, in this system of the material world, Allah Almighty has not just willed it so. This Ayah means, "Allah sent down angels and told you about their descent to encourage you and to comfort and reassure your hearts.

**The hearts that are severed from every other support.**

Then He severed their hearts and innermost selves from anything other than Him entirely saying Victory comes only from God. God follows His practice sunna with His friends is such a way that when their intentions niyyāt become weak their spiritual desire irāda low or their hearts are on the verge of listlessness fatra He shows them kindnesses alṬāf and special gifts karāmāt. By these the ties of their deeper knowledge ʿirfān are strengthened and the realities of their cer tainty yaqīn are confirmed. He sent down this address according to this practice sunna.

**The patience that counts for more than numbers.**

Success depends more on patience and being God-fearing (taqwa) than on material resources. Believers should never be upset at any lack of manpower or resources. When small in number, they should have the conviction that God will amply compensate for this by sending angels down to help them. When confronted with inadequate resources, they should trust God to create such situations as will compensate for this deficiency. Those who fear and trust God can receive His divine succour in two ways: first, by His causing a section of the enemy to be brought to repentance and submission, thus reducing their number; and second, by His bringing about their outright defeat.

127.text:
"to destroy a group of the disbelievers and humble the rest" opens the verse with the aim that is attached to the help that was sent, and the sources read the destroying as the loss that falls on one part of the enemy and the humbling as the state of the others, who are brought down from the pride they carried into the field. "causing them to withdraw in disappointment" closes the verse with the end of the day for them, and the sources read the withdrawal as the return of the men with nothing but their rage and with the thing they had come out for left in the hands of the believers. The verses before it had named the good news that was given to the hearts and the victory that comes from God alone, and this verse names what that victory did to the two parts of the enemy, so that the help is measured by what it accomplished and not by the number of the angels that came down. The sources also join this end to the mercy that is still open to those who turn, since the passage after it names the pardon that may reach them in place of the ruin. The day is read from both sides, as the loss of the men who came out in pride and as the mercy that waits for the ones who will still listen.

**The group that was cut off.**

(That He may cut off a part) He says: if He sends His help, it is only in order to kill a group (of those who disbelieve) the unbelievers of Makkah, (or overwhelm them) defeat them (so that they retire, frustrated) not having gained the upper hand or booty. Your victory in the Battle of Badr was because Allah willed that a group of the disbelievers be destroyed, and another be humiliated, frustrating them through defeat so that they withdrew. And that He might cut off li-yaqta‘ is semantically connected to the clause containing nasarakum ‘He gave you victory’ that is to say that He might destroy a party of the disbelievers by slaying them or making them fall captive or suppress them humiliate them through defeat so that they fall back return frustrated not having secured what they desired. And that He might cut off a party of the disbelievers or suppress them so that they fall back frustrated. (of those who disbelieve, or expose them to infamy,) by disgracing them and forcing them to return with only their rage, having failed in their aim to harm you.

**The disbelievers who were sent back.**

And there is no victory except from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or expose them to infamy, so that they retire frustrated Not for you is the decision; whether He turns in mercy to (pardon) them or punishes them; verily, they are the wrongdoers And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. (of those who disbelieve, or expose them to infamy,) by disgracing them and forcing them to return with only their rage, having failed in their aim to harm you. And that He might cut off a party of the disbelievers or suppress them so that they fall back frustrated. Even if the believer is struck by a catastrophic defeat nakba there is no doubt that God will cause His enemy to suffer trial and punishment. Your victory in the Battle of Badr was because Allah willed that a group of the disbelievers be destroyed, and another be humiliated, frustrating them through defeat so that they withdrew. (That He may cut off a part) He says: if He sends His help, it is only in order to kill a group (of those who disbelieve) the unbelievers of Makkah, (or overwhelm them) defeat them (so that they retire, frustrated) not having gained the upper hand or booty. (Not for you is the decision; whether He turns in mercy to (pardons) them or punishes them; verily, they are the wrongdoers.) Muslim also collected this Hadith. According to yet another story from the Sahih al-Bukhari, the Holy Prophet has been reported to have invoked evil fate for some disbelievers, whereupon came the revelation of this verse in which the Holy Prophet has been counseled to remain patient and forbearing.1.

**The victory that was not the work of the angels.**

The Holy Qur'an has, itself, given the answer in the verse ‌. It means that the purpose behind the sending of angels was not really to help score a victory on the battlefield. This is very clear from the words ‌ (only that it be a good news) and (that your hearts may be at rest) in the text. Far more clear are the words of Surah a1-Anfal about this event (So, make those who believe firm - 8:12). When Allah Almighty has endowed His angels with such power that just one of them could over-turn an entire habitation, very much like what happened with the land of the people of Lut which was overturned single-handedly by the angel Jibra'il why was it necessary to send out an army of angels? And there is no victory except from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or expose them to infamy, so that they retire frustrated Not for you is the decision; whether He turns in mercy to (pardon) them or punishes them; verily, they are the wrongdoers And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth.

**The mercy that may still reach them.**

(whether He pardons them) concerning the acts of disbelief that they commit, thus delivering them from misguidance to the guidance. (Not for you is the decision; whether He turns in mercy to (pardons) them or punishes them; verily, they are the wrongdoers.) Muslim also collected this Hadith. And there is no victory except from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or expose them to infamy, so that they retire frustrated Not for you is the decision; whether He turns in mercy to (pardon) them or punishes them; verily, they are the wrongdoers And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. God does not let enemies gloat over the misfortunes of His friends.

128.text:
"You O Prophet have no say in the matter" opens the verse with the word that takes the decision out of the hands of the messenger, and the sources read the sentence as the answer given when he prayed against the men who had wounded him, so that the servant is taught that the turning of hearts and the sending of punishment belong to his Lord alone. "It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them" names the two doors that stand open, and the sources read the mercy as the pardon that may reach the men who did the deed and the punishment as the judgment that may fall, with the choice held by the One who owns the creatures. "for indeed they are wrongdoers" closes the verse with the state of the people who are named, and the sources read the word as the description of those who had fought the messenger and broken what they had been given. The verses before it had named the destruction of a part of the enemy and the withdrawal of the rest, and this verse turns from the field to the heart of the messenger, so that the man who carried the message is set at rest about the ones who refused it. The sources carry the account of his face on the day of Uhud and the words he spoke while the blood ran, and they read the verse as the training of a prophet in the hand of his Lord. The verse also fixes the line between the servant and his Master in the heaviest hour of the fight, so that the man who is told that he has no say in the matter is the same man who is told to carry the message to the end of his life. The verse stands in the middle of the account of Uhud, and the sources read it against the wound of the messenger and the words he spoke over the men who had done it, so that the reader learns how the desire of the servant is schooled by the will of his Master.

**The matter that is not in the hands of the messenger.**

(It is no concern at all of thee (Muhammad) repentance and punishment are not in your hands whereby you pray against those who were defeated on the Day of Uhud, the archers and others (whether He relent towards them) He says: if Allah chooses to relent towards them and forgive them (or punish them) because of their leaving their positions; (for they are evil-doers) for leaving their positions. Yet Allah told him that the matter of destruction and punishment lies only with Him alone and that the Prophet has no decision in it. it is no concern at all of yours whether He relents to them or chastises them; for they are indeed evildoers. The deity is the One to whom belongs the command and the prohibition. Because there is no counterpart to Him in divinity [the Prophet] has nothing to do with the command and the prohibition. It is said that in what He taught him and told him He divested [the Prophet] of everything else and every share or claim inasmuch as He stated that the command was in no way his. Those continuing in disbelief are wrongdoers and deserve a punishment. (verily, they are the wrongdoers), and thus, they deserve such a fate.(3:128 end) It is also said that this was revealed about two tribes, the 'Asabah and Dhakwan, against whom the Prophet ﷺ prayed when they killed some of his Companions. Curse so and so , he prayed against the hypocrites. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, cursed so and so from amongst the hypocrites at the dawn prayer.

**The prayer that was made over the wounded face.**

When on the Day of Uhud the Prophet received a head wound and his front tooth was broken and he said ‘How does a people who have drenched the face of their Prophet in blood expect to prosper?’ the following was revealed It is no concern at all of yours nay it is God’s concern so be patient whether meaning until such time as He relents to them through their acceptance of Islam or chastises them; for they are indeed evildoers by virtue of their disbelief. On the day of Uhud, one of the molar teeth of the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, was broken and his face bled. The Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, said while blood was running down his face: 'How can a people ever succeed when they stain the face of their Prophet with blood while he is calling them to their Lord?' And Allah, exalted is He, revealed (It is no concern at all of thee (Muhammad) whether He relent toward them or punish them; for they are evil-doers) . How can a people ever succeed who break his molar and bash in his head when he is calling them to their Lord? His face injured, he is reported to have uttered: 'How shall such people prosper, people who do this to their prophet, although that prophet is calling them towards God?'. According to yet another story from the Sahih al-Bukhari, the Holy Prophet has been reported to have invoked evil fate for some disbelievers, whereupon came the revelation of this verse in which the Holy Prophet has been counseled to remain patient and forbearing.1.

**The mercy that may still be shown to them.**

So, be patient until Allah decides between you: either allowing them to repent to Him, asking for forgiveness, so that they are saved; or permitting them to continue in their disbelief, so that they are punished. Yet Allah told him that the matter of destruction and punishment lies only with Him alone and that the Prophet has no decision in it. (whether He pardons them) concerning the acts of disbelief that they commit, thus delivering them from misguidance to the guidance. But Allah, glorious and majestic is He, revealed (It is no concern at all of thee (Muhammad) whether He relent toward them or punish them; for they are evil-doers) . (It is no concern at all of thee (Muhammad) repentance and punishment are not in your hands whereby you pray against those who were defeated on the Day of Uhud, the archers and others (whether He relent towards them) He says: if Allah chooses to relent towards them and forgive them (or punish them) because of their leaving their positions; (for they are evil-doers) for leaving their positions.

**The patience that is asked of the believers.**

Believers should never be upset at any lack of manpower or resources. When small in number, they should have the conviction that God will amply compensate for this by sending angels down to help them. When confronted with inadequate resources, they should trust God to create such situations as will compensate for this deficiency. By the second method, God gives strength and courage to the believers and enables them to emerge victorious. So, be patient until Allah decides between you: either allowing them to repent to Him, asking for forgiveness, so that they are saved; or permitting them to continue in their disbelief, so that they are punished.

**The station of the prophet and the command of his Lord.**

If no part of the command is permit ted for the leader of the first and the last how can there be any part of the command for the one whose rank is lower in stationḍ It is said that He takes for Himself alone the secret of His servants in His decree ḥukm saying I am the One who relents to whom I will among My servants and I punish whom I will. It is said that He raised [the Prophet] up at one time to a station in which He said and you threw not when you threw but God threw [8:17]. [The Prophet] threw a handful of earth and hit all the faces [of the enemy]. But in another time He said to him No part of the command is yours [3:128] and then added in explanation To God belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth [3:129]. What happens in the end is hidden from you O Muḥammad and you are not aware of My secret regarding them. From the verse ‌ (You have no authority in the matter) , the text returns to the main event of Uhud after a brief mention of the event of Badr in between.

**The angels that were sent to make the hearts firm.**

For instance, they may simply assure the believers that angels are standing ready to help them - by appearing before them, by their voice signs or by some other method - as was witnessed in the battle of Badr where all these methods were used. According to some hadith narrations, when an angel decided to attack a disbeliever, the head of the disbeliever slid of his body all by itself.1 It has also been reported that some noble Companions heard the voice of Jibra'il saying, 'Charge, Haizum!'2 Some of them saw some angels (Muslim). Here, the address is to the angels and they have been asked to see that Muslims do not get anxious and that their hearts stay firm. If Allah Almighty had willed that countries be conquered through armies of angels, the very name of disbelief and disbelievers would have been effaced from the face of the earth, not to say much about governments and empires. You should know that victory only comes from Allah and that if He willed, He would have defeated your enemy without you having to fight them.

129.text:
"To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" opens the verse with the statement of the owner of the two worlds, and the sources read it as the creation and the ordering of everything belonging to Him, so that no creature stands outside His hand. "He forgives whoever He wills" names the first of the two acts, and the sources read the pardon as the mercy that reaches the servant who turns, with the choice held by the One who owns him. "and punishes whoever He wills" names the second, and the sources read the punishment as the justice that falls on the deed, with the two acts set in the verse side by side so that hope and fear are held in one hand. "And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful" closes the verse with the two names that carry the gate of return, and the sources read them as the forgiveness that is given to those who repent and the mercy that comes to the one who dies in that state. The verses before it had named the matter that is not in the hands of the messenger, and this verse names the One to whom the whole matter belongs, while the verses after it turn to the community with the command and the warning.

**What belongs to Allah in the heavens and the earth.**

(...And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the Earth.)[3:129], everything is indeed the property of Allah and all are servants in His Hand. (Not upon you is their guidance, but Allah guides whom He wills.)[2:272], and,. (Verily, you guide not whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills)[28: 56]. (Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings. To God belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants; He forgives whom He wills forgiveness for and chastises whom He wills chastisement for.

**He forgives whoever He wills and punishes whoever He wills.**

(He forgiveth whom He will) whoever deserves to be forgiven, (and punisheth whom He will) whoever deserves to be punished. He forgives the disobedience of whomever He wills of His servants through His Mercy, and punishes whom He wills through His Justice. To God belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants; He forgives whom He wills forgiveness for and chastises whom He wills chastisement for. (He forgives whom He wills, and punishes whom He wills.) for His is the decision and none can resist His decision.

**The command and the decree that belong to Him alone.**

The deity is the One to whom belongs the command and the prohibition. Because there is no counterpart to Him in divinity [the Prophet] has nothing to do with the command and the prohibition. It is said that in what He taught him and told him He divested [the Prophet] of everything else and every share or claim inasmuch as He stated that the command was in no way his. Therefore the right to possess is His right to pos sess mulk the command is His command amr and the decree is His decree ḥukm. But in another time He said to him No part of the command is yours [3:128] and then added in explanation To God belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth [3:129]. It is said that He raised [the Prophet] up at one time to a station in which He said and you threw not when you threw but God threw [8:17]. [The Prophet] threw a handful of earth and hit all the faces [of the enemy].

**The forgiveness that is given to the one who repents.**

(He forgiveth whom He will) whoever deserves to be forgiven, (and punisheth whom He will) whoever deserves to be punished. (Allah is Forgiving) of those who repent, (Merciful) towards him who dies in a state of repentance. And God is Forgiving of His friends Merciful to those who obey Him. He forgives the disobedience of whomever He wills of His servants through His Mercy, and punishes whom He wills through His Justice.

130.text:
"O believers, Do not consume interest" opens the verse with the command that cuts off the practice the community had carried from the days before, and the sources read the interest as the gain that is taken on a loan with nothing given in return. "multiplying it many times over" names the shape the practice took among them, and the sources read the doubling as the increase that is piled upon the debt year after year, and they notice that the words describe the state of the people at the time and name the wrong that sits inside the practice. "And be mindful of Allah" turns the command to the root of the matter, and the sources read the mindfulness as the fear that keeps a person away from the gain that has been forbidden. "so you may prosper" closes the verse with the end that is set before them, and the sources read the success as the state of the one who is saved from the punishment and given the good that the verse after it names. The verses before it had named the Lord who forgives and punishes as He wills, and this verse shows one deed that draws the punishment and one state that keeps a person clear of it. The command is set inside a passage about the two companies, so that the wealth a man gathers by the forbidden road is weighed against the mercy that the verses after it place before the community. The sources also treat the doubling as a description of what the people were doing at the time and not as the outer edge of the rule, since the gain itself is what was cut off.

**The usury that the command refuses.**

Allah prohibits His believing servants from dealing in Riba and from requiring interest on their capital, just as they used to do during the time of Jahiliyyah. O you who believe do not exact usury twofold and severalfold read mudā‘afatan or mud‘afatan by increasing the amount to be repaid when the loan period comes to an end and delaying the request of the loan. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, stay away from usury: increasing and compounding the wealth that you lend to people as the people of the time of ignorance before Islam did; and be mindful of Allah: following what He instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, so that you may reach the good you desire in this world and in the Afterlife. O you who believe do not exact usury doubled and redoubled. The detailed rules regarding 'riba' and the philosophy underlying its prohibition have been discussed thoroughly in Surah al-Baqarah verses 275-278 (Volume 1 of this commentary).

**The doubling and the multiplying of the debt.**

" If the debtor asks for deferment of the loan, the creditor would require interest and this would occur year after year until the little capital becomes multiplied many times. (Devour not usury, doubling) the silver coin (and quadrupling) the appointed period for repayment. Moreover, these words also suggest that even the interest charged is simple and not compound, yet once a person is engaged in the business of interest he does not stop at charging interest in one transaction only. Rather, he reinvests the income of interest in another loan transaction, and keeps investing the interest proceeds in similar transactions again and again, and thus the ultimate result is that the original interest charged through the first transaction is doubled and multiplied. These words are used only to explain the factual position prevalent at that time, and to indicate its unjust and evil nature. However, it may be pointed out here that words of (doubled and multiplied) used in this verse do not mean that the prohibition of 'riba' is restricted only to a transaction where the interest is doubled or multiplied. In fact, these words are not used in a restrictive sense, because it is evident from Surah al-Baqarah that 'riba' or interest is prohibited in any case, even though its rate is not so high as to make it doubled or multiplied.

**The mindfulness that keeps a person away from it.**

(Observe your duty to Allah) fear Allah regarding the consumption of usury, (that ye may be successful) so that you be saved from Allah's wrath and punishment. And fear God by abandoning such usury so that you may prosper that you may triumph. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, stay away from usury: increasing and compounding the wealth that you lend to people as the people of the time of ignorance before Islam did; and be mindful of Allah: following what He instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, so that you may reach the good you desire in this world and in the Afterlife. And fear the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers. [God] has prohibited usury for His servants; this includes loaning one amount and asking twice as much in return. (He who gives time to a debtor or forgives him, then Allah will save him from the heat of Jahannam (Hell-fire). Behold! The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. Verily, there is no dose of anything better to Allah than a dose of rage that the servant controls, and whenever the servant of Allah controls it, he will be internally filled with faith.)

**The success that the verse sets before them.**

(Observe your duty to Allah) fear Allah regarding the consumption of usury, (that ye may be successful) so that you be saved from Allah's wrath and punishment. And fear God by abandoning such usury so that you may prosper that you may triumph. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, stay away from usury: increasing and compounding the wealth that you lend to people as the people of the time of ignorance before Islam did; and be mindful of Allah: following what He instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, so that you may reach the good you desire in this world and in the Afterlife. But He has asked you for a loan which He will repay seven hundredfold even up to an infinite repay ment.This alludes to the magnanimity karam that is not inherent in humans but rather is an attribute of the Real . (Those who spend their wealth (in Allah's cause) by night and day, in secret and in public)[2:274] These believers are never distracted from obeying Allah, spending on what pleases Him, being kind to His servants and their relatives, and other acts of righteousness.

**The love of money and the wealth that is given away.**

Engaging in usury is the ultimate in money worship. A usurer thinks day in and day out as to how to double and quadruple his money. If the inspiration to tread the former path is the love of money, the inspiration towards the latter is the love of God and His Messenger. Hastening towards it means giving away more and more of one’s wealth for the cause of God. The way to worldly success is to increase one’s riches, while the way to success in the Hereafter is to decrease one’s riches. But what he ought to pursue relentlessly is not the acquisition of material things but his entry into Paradise in the Hereafter. He ought to be ever eager to attain God’s mercy and blessing, but not by increasing his worldly wealth in order to guarantee himself a life of grandeur in this world. (I swear regarding three matters: no charity shall ever decrease the wealth; whenever one forgives people, then Allah will magnify his honor; and he who is humble for Allah, then Allah will raise his rank.) (And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but afterwards seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.)[4: 110] and there are several examples similar to this Ayah. (And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but afterwards seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.)[4: 110] and there are several examples similar to this Ayah.

131.text:
"Guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers" opens the verse with the warning that follows the command on interest, and the sources read the guarding as the keeping away from the deeds that lead to the fire and the doing of what God has asked. The fire is named as prepared for the people who refuse, and the sources carry the accounts that show where it stands and how the servants are saved from it, so that the warning is read with the mercy that is placed beside it in the verses that follow. The verse before it had named the interest that is forbidden and the mindfulness that keeps a person clear, and this verse names the end that waits for the one who keeps the practice. The sources also notice that the warning is addressed to the believers, so that no one leans on the name of faith while carrying the deeds of the people who have no faith, and they read the fire as a place that stands where its Lord has set it, and the mercy of the Lord as a door that stays open for the servant who turns before the day of the account comes.

**The fire that is prepared for the disbelievers.**

(And ward off (from yourselves) the Fire) fear the Fire regarding the consumption of usury which was (prepared) created (for disbelievers) in Allah and in the prohibition of usury. And fear the Fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers lest you be chastised with it. Protect yourselves from the fire of Hell that Allah has prepared for the disbelievers through doing good and staying away from what is prohibited. Allah also threatens them with the Fire and warns them against it, saying,.

Protect yourselves from the fire of Hell that Allah has prepared for the disbelievers through doing good and staying away from what is prohibited. (And ward off (from yourselves) the Fire) fear the Fire regarding the consumption of usury which was (prepared) created (for disbelievers) in Allah and in the prohibition of usury. And fear the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers. [God] has prohibited usury for His servants; this includes loaning one amount and asking twice as much in return. The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. (Similarly, the Fire is where Allah wants it to be.) This Hadith has two possible meanings. Such is the case with Hell-fire, for it is where Allah wants it to be. The Fire, on the other hand, is in the lowest of lows. Therefore, Paradise being as wide as the heavens and Earth does not contradict the fact that the Fire exists wherever Allah wills it to be. (Paradise as wide as the heavens and the Earth)[3:133]; "Where is the Fire then?

**The believer and the time he may spend in the Fire.**

These words indicate that the believer will not be chastised by [the fire]. If he is chastised by it for a time he will not abide in it. Protect yourselves from the fire of Hell that Allah has prepared for the disbelievers through doing good and staying away from what is prohibited. And fear the Fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers lest you be chastised with it. And fear the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers:

**The riba that the command prohibited.**

The detailed rules regarding 'riba' and the philosophy underlying its prohibition have been discussed thoroughly in Surah al-Baqarah verses 275-278 (Volume 1 of this commentary). However, it may be pointed out here that words of (doubled and multiplied) used in this verse do not mean that the prohibition of 'riba' is restricted only to a transaction where the interest is doubled or multiplied. In fact, these words are not used in a restrictive sense, because it is evident from Surah al-Baqarah that 'riba' or interest is prohibited in any case, even though its rate is not so high as to make it doubled or multiplied. Moreover, these words also suggest that even the interest charged is simple and not compound, yet once a person is engaged in the business of interest he does not stop at charging interest in one transaction only. Rather, he reinvests the income of interest in another loan transaction, and keeps investing the interest proceeds in similar transactions again and again, and thus the ultimate result is that the original interest charged through the first transaction is doubled and multiplied. These words are used only to explain the factual position prevalent at that time, and to indicate its unjust and evil nature. (He who gives time to a debtor or forgives him, then Allah will save him from the heat of Jahannam (Hell-fire). Behold! The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. Verily, there is no dose of anything better to Allah than a dose of rage that the servant controls, and whenever the servant of Allah controls it, he will be internally filled with faith.)

132.text:
"Obey Allah and the Messenger" opens the verse with the two names that hold the command together, and the sources read the joining of the two as the sign that the obedience of the messenger is the obedience of the One who sent him, since the messenger explains what the book carries and shows how it is to be done. "so you may be shown mercy" closes the verse with the end, and the sources read the mercy as the gift that is placed before the community when its faith is drawn out in the deed and not left in the word. The verses before it had named the fire that is prepared for the people who refuse, and this verse names the road that leads away from it, while the verse after it names the forgiveness and the garden that are set before those who run. The sources also dwell on the rank that the obedience of the messenger is given, and they read the address as the guard that keeps a community from the splitting that comes when each man follows his own reading of the book. The command stands here after a passage about wealth and usury, and the sources notice that the obedience is asked in the same breath as the mercy, so that the deed and the hope are held together, and the messenger is named beside his Lord as the one who shows how the book is to be carried into the life of the day.

**The obedience that is given to Allah and the Messenger.**

The first verse, in a brief statement, presents a cardinal command of Faith in the following words: ‌ ‌ 132 (And obey Allah and the Messenger so that you may be blessed). (And obey Allah and the messenger) concerning the prohibition of usury and its avoidance, (that ye may find mercy) in order that mercy encompasses you such that you are saved and not punished. Obey Allah and His Messenger by following what He instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, so that you may gain His mercy in this world and in the Afterlife. And obey God and the Messenger so that you may find mercy. [God] tied obedience to the Messenger to obedience to Himself. Here, in order that one becomes deserving of Divine mercy, the obedience to Allah Almighty has been declared necessary and binding, and along with it, the obedience of the Messenger has been made equally necessary and binding.

**The rank that is given to the Messenger.**

This was to elevate [the Prophet's] rank and to make things easier for the com munity by handing them over to the company of an individual who was one of them. Allah Almighty has made it clear in these verses that the obedience to Allah and His Messenger does not become genuine and effective through lip-service alone. The first part of the Faith is to affirm and declare the existence of God (Allah), His Oneness, and that man is there to worship and obey Him. It is more reassuring to be with one's own kind. As such, the obedience of the Messenger is really nothing but the obedience of Allah Almighty, but, given its external appearance and detailed description, it is somewhat different from that. For instance, it was said: which means that the purpose behind sending the Messenger is that he should explain for people the meanings and objectives of the verses revealed to him. The pattern of combining the command to obey Allah Almighty, immediately followed by the command to obey the Messenger appears in the Qur'an again and again. In short, the repeated stress on the obedience of the Messenger alongwith the obedience of Allah Almighty, as well as, specific instructions to follow the dictates of the Messenger at various places are there to counter the dangerous ignorance of a person who may venture to separate the details of Qur'anic injunctions described by the Holy Prophet and available in the treasure-house of his ahadith, making it look like something foreign to the obedience of Allah, and consequently may hasten to reject them.

**The mercy that is promised to those who obey.**

(And obey Allah and the messenger) concerning the prohibition of usury and its avoidance, (that ye may find mercy) in order that mercy encompasses you such that you are saved and not punished. Obey Allah and His Messenger by following what He instructs and staying away from what He has prohibited, so that you may gain His mercy in this world and in the Afterlife. Here, in order that one becomes deserving of Divine mercy, the obedience to Allah Almighty has been declared necessary and binding, and along with it, the obedience of the Messenger has been made equally necessary and binding. This was to elevate [the Prophet's] rank and to make things easier for the com munity by handing them over to the company of an individual who was one of them.

**The wealth that is spent in the way of God.**

(Those who spend (in Allah's cause) in prosperity and in adversity)[3:134], in hard times and easy times, while active (or enthusiastic) and otherwise, healthy or ill, and in all conditions, just as Allah said in another Ayah,. (Those who spend their wealth (in Allah's cause) by night and day, in secret and in public)[2:274] These believers are never distracted from obeying Allah, spending on what pleases Him, being kind to His servants and their relatives, and other acts of righteousness. (He who gives time to a debtor or forgives him, then Allah will save him from the heat of Jahannam (Hell-fire). Behold! The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. Verily, there is no dose of anything better to Allah than a dose of rage that the servant controls, and whenever the servant of Allah controls it, he will be internally filled with faith.) (I swear regarding three matters: no charity shall ever decrease the wealth; whenever one forgives people, then Allah will magnify his honor; and he who is humble for Allah, then Allah will raise his rank.) (And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but afterwards seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.)[4: 110] and there are several examples similar to this Ayah. Hastening towards it means giving away more and more of one’s wealth for the cause of God. The way to worldly success is to increase one’s riches, while the way to success in the Hereafter is to decrease one’s riches. If the inspiration to tread the former path is the love of money, the inspiration towards the latter is the love of God and His Messenger. Honour and success are of no importance when compared to Paradise, the pleasure and enjoyment of which are immeasurable.

133.text:
"And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth" opens the verse with the call to run, and the sources read the hastening as the eagerness that does not sit and wait for the season of mercy to pass, with the forgiveness named as what the run is aimed at and the garden as the breadth that no land on earth can measure. "prepared for those mindful of Allah" closes the verse by naming the people the garden was made ready for, and the sources read the mindfulness as the fear of God that keeps a person inside the commands and the rooting out of the love of wealth that the verses before have named. The verses before it had named the obedience of Allah and the messenger and the mercy that follows it, and this verse names the road and the reward, while the verses after it describe the people who are named here, with the spending in ease and in hardship at the head of the list. The sources also weigh the two roads a person may run on, since the wealth that a man gathers is set against the forgiveness that his Lord offers, and the verse asks the hearer to choose the race he will enter, since the run towards the garden and the run after the profit of this world cannot be made with the same heart. The verse is the doorway of the passage that follows, and the sources read the two qualities named in it, the haste and the mindfulness, as the two feet on which a person walks towards the mercy of his Lord, and they set the breadth of the garden against the narrowness of the gains that the verses before it have named.

**The hastening towards forgiveness from the Lord.**

The second command is: 'Race one another towards Forgiveness from your Lord and towards Paradise.' Here, Forgiveness stands for the means of obtaining forgiveness, that is, good deeds which bring forth forgiveness. The outcome of all these sayings is that Forgiveness covers all good deeds which become the means of obtaining Divine forgiveness. The second point worth considering is that Allah Almighty has mentioned 'Forgiveness' first and the 'Paradise' after it. Since Divine forgiveness is the primary factor in one's entry into the Paradise, the text takes this importance into consideration and does not present forgiveness in the absolute sense. (And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord) hasten to repent of usury and from all transgressions and reach for forgiveness from your Lord, (and for a Paradise) by means of righteous works and avoidance of usury (as wide as are the heavens and the earth) if they were to be joined to each other, (prepared) created (for those who ward off (evil) ward off disbelief, idolatry, indecencies, and the consumption of usury;. And vie with one another hastening read wa-sāri‘ū or simply sāri‘ū to forgiveness from your Lord and to a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth that is as broad as both of them together if put side by side breadth denotes ampleness that has been prepared for those who fear God in being obedient and abandoning acts of disobedience. Rush to do good actions, and draw near to Allah through doing as He instructs, so that you achieve the great forgiveness of Allah and enter a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, which Allah has prepared for the Mindful. And vie with one another hastening to forgiveness from your Lord and to a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth that has been prepared for those who fear. The meaning here is vie with one another hastening to act in ways that will bring about forgiveness for you.

**The Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth.**

(as wide as the heavens and the earth) draws the attention to the spaciousness of Paradise. (When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for Al-Firdaws which is the highest and best part of Paradise. From it originate the rivers of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Beneficent (Allah).) First comes the resolution of an apparent contradiction which may be felt when one notices that the present verse carries a command to race one another towards Forgiveness and Paradise, while through another verse: If the word is taken here in this sense, the verse would mean that Paradise is not an ordinary commodity; the entire heavens and the earth are its price. And vie with one another hastening to forgiveness from your Lord and to a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth that has been prepared for those who fear.

**The mindful of Allah for whom the garden was prepared.**

And vie with one another hastening to forgiveness from your Lord and to a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth that has been prepared for those who fear. Nothing but repentance brings about forgiveness because the one who disobeys is the one who is in need of it. What will take him to Paradise is only Forgiveness of His Lord, and His grace. Since Divine forgiveness is the primary factor in one's entry into the Paradise, the text takes this importance into consideration and does not present forgiveness in the absolute sense. Hastening towards it means giving away more and more of one’s wealth for the cause of God. (Those who spend their wealth (in Allah's cause) by night and day, in secret and in public)[2:274] These believers are never distracted from obeying Allah, spending on what pleases Him, being kind to His servants and their relatives, and other acts of righteousness. Who expend in prosperity and adversity and restrain their rage and pardon their fellow men; and God loves those who are virtuous.

**The spending in prosperity and in adversity.**

(Those who spend (in Allah's cause) in prosperity and in adversity)[3:134], in hard times and easy times, while active (or enthusiastic) and otherwise, healthy or ill, and in all conditions, just as Allah said in another Ayah,. (Those who spend their wealth (in Allah's cause) by night and day, in secret and in public)[2:274] These believers are never distracted from obeying Allah, spending on what pleases Him, being kind to His servants and their relatives, and other acts of righteousness. (He who gives time to a debtor or forgives him, then Allah will save him from the heat of Jahannam (Hell-fire). Behold! The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. Verily, there is no dose of anything better to Allah than a dose of rage that the servant controls, and whenever the servant of Allah controls it, he will be internally filled with faith.) Rush to do good actions, and draw near to Allah through doing as He instructs, so that you achieve the great forgiveness of Allah and enter a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, which Allah has prepared for the Mindful. The way to worldly success is to increase one’s riches, while the way to success in the Hereafter is to decrease one’s riches.

**The love of money and the fear of loss.**

If the inspiration to tread the former path is the love of money, the inspiration towards the latter is the love of God and His Messenger. Engaging in usury is the ultimate in money worship. A usurer thinks day in and day out as to how to double and quadruple his money. But what he ought to pursue relentlessly is not the acquisition of material things but his entry into Paradise in the Hereafter. He ought to be ever eager to attain God’s mercy and blessing, but not by increasing his worldly wealth in order to guarantee himself a life of grandeur in this world. Where those desirous of riches have the fear of worldly loss, those of a spiritual bent of mind fear loss in the Hereafter. Honour and success are of no importance when compared to Paradise, the pleasure and enjoyment of which are immeasurable. (Those who spend their wealth (in Allah's cause) by night and day, in secret and in public)[2:274] These believers are never distracted from obeying Allah, spending on what pleases Him, being kind to His servants and their relatives, and other acts of righteousness. But when He mentioned forgiveness he did not mention height or width so some people have said that forgiveness is from the [divine] attributes of the essence ṣifāt al-dhāt and is part of the meaning of mercy raḥma.

134.text:
"They are those who donate in prosperity and adversity" opens the verse by naming the people the passage has been describing, and the sources read the spending as the gift that keeps going out in the days of ease and in the days of need, so that the hand is open whether the wealth is flowing or thin. "control their anger" names the second mark, and the sources read the restraining as the holding back of the rage when the man has the power to let it out, with the pardon named next as what follows the holding. "and pardon others" names the third, and the sources read the pardon as the passing over of the wrong that a man has suffered at the hands of another. "And Allah loves the good-doers" closes the verse with the statement of the love that rests on the people who live in this way, and the sources read the word as the highest praise that a servant can be given. The verses before it had named the race towards the forgiveness of the Lord, and this verse draws the portrait of the people who run that race, while the verse after it names the mark of the people who fall and rise again. The verse is the portrait of the community that the whole passage has been building, and the sources read the three marks in it as one character, since the open hand, the held tongue and the pardoned wrong all come from the same root in the heart. The people who carry them are the people who run towards the forgiveness that the verse before has named, and the love of God is set on them as the seal of the whole description.

**Those who spend in prosperity and adversity.**

(Those who spend (in Allah's cause) in prosperity and in adversity)[3:134], in hard times and easy times, while active (or enthusiastic) and otherwise, healthy or ill, and in all conditions, just as Allah said in another Ayah,. (Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity) He says: those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is times of comfort and in times of hardship, (those who control their wrath) those who check their anger, keeping their hot-temperedness to themselves (and are forgiving towards mankind) towards slaves; (Allah loveth the good) He loves those who are kind towards slaves and freemen. Who expend in obedience to God in prosperity and adversity in times of ease and difficulty and restrain their rage and desist from following it up even though they are able to and pardon their fellow-men those who wrong them waiving their punishment; and God loves those who are virtuous through such actions that is to say He will reward them. The Mindful are those who spend their wealth for the sake of Allah, in ease and hardship, who control their anger when they could seek revenge, and who forgive those who wrong them. It is important to note at this point that the Holy Qur'an uses the word which means that they spend in the way of Allah under all conditions, of prosperity and of adversity. On the other hand, the point made here is that those who keep on spending within the limitations of their capacity to spend, especially when their circumstances are straightened, would discover to their delight that, by doing so, the blessed style of giving and the wonderful habit of sharing with others less fortunate has come to stay and that it will not go extinct. This is why the Lord of the Worlds praises and lauds his spending and says, "Those who spend in prosperity and adversity.

**Those who restrain their rage.**

Who expend in obedience to God in prosperity and adversity in times of ease and difficulty and restrain their rage and desist from following it up even though they are able to and pardon their fellow-men those who wrong them waiving their punishment; and God loves those who are virtuous through such actions that is to say He will reward them. They tolerate suffering, or rather, they welcome it with patience and forbear ance, for they bear witness that God knows and sees. (who repress anger) meaning, they do not satisfy their rage upon people.

**Those who pardon people.**

Here He alludes to the fact that those who pardon people are those who pass over and efface people's sins, but they do not limit themselves to that. This is why God commanded, "Take to pardoning," that is, take the excellent and beautiful things from among the character traits, and pardon those who wrong you, join with those who cut off from you, and act with beauty toward those who act with ugliness toward you. The Mindful are those who spend their wealth for the sake of Allah, in ease and hardship, who control their anger when they could seek revenge, and who forgive those who wrong them. (He who gives time to a debtor or forgives him, then Allah will save him from the heat of Jahannam (Hell-fire). Behold! The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. Verily, there is no dose of anything better to Allah than a dose of rage that the servant controls, and whenever the servant of Allah controls it, he will be internally filled with faith.)

**And Allah loves the doers of good.**

This is the attribute of the beautiful-doers, and God is their Friend, for He says, "And God loves the beautiful-doers. Since this sentence implicitly instructs people to be good to others and thus be loved by Allah, so Hadrat Ali (Zainul abidin) ibn Sayyidna Husain once he heard it, said: 'All right, go. Rather, they refrain from harming them and await their rewards with Allah, the Exalted and Most Honored.

**The character of the favoured servants of Allah.**

So, the verse clearly settles that the favoured servants of Allah are unique in their character who never forget Allah, neither in luxury nor in distress. By having identified the traits and marks of God-fearing Muslims, and having stated that they are the ones deserving of ultimate success and of elevated stations in Paradise, the righteous have been given a good news (of receiving the same reward, if they follow them) and the evil-doers are exhorted and persuaded to mend themselves and follow the God-fearing. This is to indicate that the rights of Allah, despite their supreme status above all rights, are not meant to benefit Allah in any way. The verse: ‌ (the path of those whom You have blessed - 1:6) from Surah al-Fatihah clearly indicates that the straight and correct path of Faith has to be learnt from these very favoured servants of Allah. First are those who spend nothing, whether in prosperity or adversity, whether in the vast ness of blessings or in the days of famine and hardship. " Second are those who spend in vastness of blessings but not in narrowness and hardship.

135.text:
"They are those who" opens the verse by tying the people to the portrait that the verse before it has drawn, and the sources read the sentence as the naming of the same company with one more mark added to them. "upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves" names the fall that the mark is built on, and the sources read the evil deed as the sin that is done in the open and the wronging of the self as the lesser fault that a person commits against his own soul. "remember Allah and seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in sin" names the three things that follow the fall, and the sources read them as the memory of God that wakes the heart, the asking for pardon that follows, and the refusal to stay in the road the fault was taken on. "and who forgives sins except Allah" closes the verse with the question that leaves the servant no door but the one, and the sources read it as the statement that the pardon belongs to God alone. The verses before it had named the people who spend and pardon, and this verse names the people who fall and are lifted, while the verse after it names the reward that waits for them. The sources read the whole verse as the mercy that keeps the servant from despair after a fall, since the book does not describe a company without fault but a company that turns whenever the fault is committed, and the mark of the people of faith is not that they never slip but that they do not stay where they fell, since the door of the pardon stands open for the one who comes back to it with a sorry heart.

**Those who remember Allah when they do wrong.**

(And those who, when they do an evil thing) a transgression (or wrong themselves) by staring at [women], touching or kissing (remember Allah) fear Allah (and implore forgiveness for their sins) repent of their sins (�-who forgiveth sins save Allah only?) the sins of he who repents (-and will not knowingly) i.e. knowing that it is a transgression against Allah (repeat (the wrong) they did). And who when they commit an indecency a despicable sin such as adultery or wrong themselves with less than that such as a kiss remember God that is to say His threat of punishment and pray forgiveness for their sins — and who that is none shall forgive sins but God? — and who do not persist persevere in what they did but have desisted from it knowing that what they did was sinful. They are the ones; if they were to commit a major sin, or wrong themselves by committing a lesser sin, they remember Allah, and His warning to the wrongdoers and promise to the Mindful; so they ask their Lord for forgiveness, regretting what they did. And who when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves remem ber God and pray forgiveness for their sins-and who shall forgive sins but Godḍ-and who do not persist in what they did knowing. Therefore, if they commit an error they follow it with repentance and ask forgiveness.

**The evil deed and the wronging of oneself.**

(And those who, when they do an evil thing) a transgression (or wrong themselves) by staring at [women], touching or kissing (remember Allah) fear Allah (and implore forgiveness for their sins) repent of their sins (�-who forgiveth sins save Allah only?) the sins of he who repents (-and will not knowingly) i.e. knowing that it is a transgression against Allah (repeat (the wrong) they did). The transgres sions mukhālafāt that occur in the minds of the most respected people are like the actions of others. It is said that they commit an indecency by relying on their [own] actions or they wrong themselves by regarding their [own] states so they seek forgiveness for their sins by declaring themselves free from what they do and do not do knowing that there are no means to Him except through Him. They know that they have done wrong and that Allah forgives all disobedience. And who when they commit an indecency a despicable sin such as adultery or wrong themselves with less than that such as a kiss remember God that is to say His threat of punishment and pray forgiveness for their sins — and who that is none shall forgive sins but God? — and who do not persist persevere in what they did but have desisted from it knowing that what they did was sinful.

**Those who turn to Allah after they fall.**

Should they ever fall in sin under the compulsions of human weakness, they immediately turn to Allah, repent, seek His forgiveness and resolve to abstain from that sin in future. If a sin has been committed, one should immediately turn to Allah, renew the zeal to obey Him and start remembering Him as He should be remembered. They too fall into error, but that is only temporary. May Allah Almighty bestow upon us the good fortune to become possessed with these supreme morals identified by the Holy Qur'an. They immediately realize their mistake and return to God, spontaneously invoking His forgiveness and seeking His mercy. They ask Allah not to take them to account for it, because Allah alone can forgive, and they do not continue in their disobedience.

**Who forgives sins except Allah.**

(and none can forgive sins but Allah), means that none except Allah forgives sins. And who when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves remem ber God and pray forgiveness for their sins-and who shall forgive sins but Godḍ-and who do not persist in what they did knowing. They ask Allah not to take them to account for it, because Allah alone can forgive, and they do not continue in their disobedience. Another point of guidance here tells us that forgiveness of sins depends on two things: To regret past sins, seek pardon for these and to pray for forgiveness. Therefore, if they commit an error they follow it with repentance and ask forgiveness.

**The man from the Helpers and the people of Thaqif.**

The following was then revealed about a man from the Helpers because he stared at, touched and kissed the wife of a man from Thaqif, saying: The Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, tied two men, one from the Helpers and one from Thaqif, with the bond of brotherhood and they were inseparable. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, went out one day to one of his military expeditions and the man from Thaqif accompanied him, leaving his wife and business under the care of the Helper who used to look after the family of the man from Thaqif. He hugged and kissed her but then he regretted his action. I have betrayed my brother!' His friend said: 'O so-and-so come let us go to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, and ask him about your sin, haply Allah will ease your situation and relent on you'. And so he went back with him until they reached Medina one day, at the time of 'Asr prayer and Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought down the news of the acceptance of his repentance. (And those who, when they do an evil thing or wrong themselves, remember Allah) [3:135]. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said: This was revealed about Nabhan, the seller of dates. Upon his retreat, his friend's wife exclaimed: 'Glory be to Allah!

**The remembering of Allah that keeps a person from sin.**

The verse tells us that involvement in sin is caused by one's negligence in remembering Allah. If a sin has been committed, one should immediately turn to Allah, renew the zeal to obey Him and start remembering Him as He should be remembered. They are the ones; if they were to commit a major sin, or wrong themselves by committing a lesser sin, they remember Allah, and His warning to the wrongdoers and promise to the Mindful; so they ask their Lord for forgiveness, regretting what they did. Therefore, if they commit an error they follow it with repentance and ask forgiveness. (I swear regarding three matters: no charity shall ever decrease the wealth; whenever one forgives people, then Allah will magnify his honor; and he who is humble for Allah, then Allah will raise his rank.) Whatever has been stated verbally in the Quran is borne out by the events of Islamic history. But advice is heeded only by those who are keen to have it. They know that they have done wrong and that Allah forgives all disobedience.

136.text:
"Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens under which rivers flow" opens the verse with the wage that is set for the people the two verses before have described, and the sources read the forgiveness as the covering of the faults that the people repented of and the gardens as the place that is given after the account is closed. "staying there forever" names the length of the stay, and the sources read it as the dwelling that is never cut and the life that is never taken away. "How excellent is the reward for those who work righteousness" closes the verse with the praise that is put on the wage itself, and the sources read the word as the wonder that is invited from the reader at what the workers are given. The verses before it had named the people who turn back to their Lord after the fall, and this verse names what is kept for them, while the verses after it turn to the days of the nations that have passed and the lesson that is written in their ruins.

**The forgiveness that is given from their Lord.**

(The reward of such will be forgiveness) of their sins (from their Lord, and Gardens beneath) beneath its trees and habitations (which rivers) of wine, water, honey and milk (flow, wherein they will abide for ever) in Paradise, never to die or leave it, (a bountiful reward for workers!) the reward of those who repent is Paradise and all that which was mentioned. Those — their requital is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens beneath which rivers flow abiding therein khālidīna fīhā an implied situation that is it is foreordained that they will abide in it once they enter it; excellent is the wage this wage of those workers of obedience! The Mindful people who are like this, and have these praiseworthy qualities, are rewarded with Allah’s forgiveness and His overlooking what they have done. Those-their requital is forgiveness from their Lord in returning them to witnessing the Lordship and the best possible outcome and fate that was already theirs.

**The gardens and the rivers that flow under them.**

Those — their requital is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens beneath which rivers flow abiding therein khālidīna fīhā an implied situation that is it is foreordained that they will abide in it once they enter it; excellent is the wage this wage of those workers of obedience! (The reward of such will be forgiveness) of their sins (from their Lord, and Gardens beneath) beneath its trees and habitations (which rivers) of wine, water, honey and milk (flow, wherein they will abide for ever) in Paradise, never to die or leave it, (a bountiful reward for workers!) the reward of those who repent is Paradise and all that which was mentioned. (When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for Al-Firdaws which is the highest and best part of Paradise. From it originate the rivers of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Beneficent (Allah).) And gardens beneath which rivers flow in the future in paradise and in the here and now in the happiness of whispered conversations and the fullness of intimacy. In the Afterlife, they will have gardens with rivers flowing below palaces, where they will live eternally.

**How excellent is the reward of those who work.**

Those — their requital is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens beneath which rivers flow abiding therein khālidīna fīhā an implied situation that is it is foreordained that they will abide in it once they enter it; excellent is the wage this wage of those workers of obedience! How blessed is the reward for those who act according to Allah’s laws! (The reward of such will be forgiveness) of their sins (from their Lord, and Gardens beneath) beneath its trees and habitations (which rivers) of wine, water, honey and milk (flow, wherein they will abide for ever) in Paradise, never to die or leave it, (a bountiful reward for workers!) the reward of those who repent is Paradise and all that which was mentioned.

**The rights of Allah and the rights of people.**

Upto this point, the text describes qualities of character that relate to the fulfillment of human rights. Following this, come qualities that relate to the rights of Allah where it has been said that true Muslims do not disobey Allah. One whom God has purified by the light of solicitude is protected from entanglement in the delusions of people. The Mindful people who are like this, and have these praiseworthy qualities, are rewarded with Allah’s forgiveness and His overlooking what they have done. This character of true Muslims appears in the text in the following words:

137.text:
"Similar situations came to pass before you" opens the verse with the word that sets the trials of the community beside the trials of the peoples who came before, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the alternation of days is a practice of God that has run through every nation. "so travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers" turns the statement into a command to look with the eye, and the sources read the travel as the journey that takes a person to the ruined houses of the peoples who refused the messengers, so that the lesson enters by way of sight and not only by way of hearing, and the ruin of the nations is named as a book that any traveller can read on the ground. The verses before it had named the reward of the workers and the faults that are pardoned, and this verse lifts the reader from his own day to the days that are written in the earth, while the verse after it names the book that explains the truth to the whole of humanity and warns the mindful.

**The ways of life that passed away before you.**

Many similar ways (and mishaps of life) were faced [by nations (believers and disbelievers) that have passed away] before you, so travel through the earth, and see what was the end of those who denied This is a plain statement for mankind, a guidance and instruction for the Muttaqin So do not become weak, nor be sad, and you will be triumphant if you are indeed believers If a wound has touched you, be sure a similar wound has touched the others. (137... Many similar ways (and mishaps of life) were faced before you), for the previous nations who followed their Prophets before you, they too suffered losses. (Systems) with reward and forgiveness for those who repent and punishment and destruction for those who do not repent (have passed away before you) have passed in bygone nations. Ways of life have passed away before you; so travel in the land and behold how was the end of those who denied. Similar incidents have therefore come to pass in times before them. The following was revealed regarding the defeat at Uhud Ways of life have passed away before you all manner of unbelief has preceded where they have been given respite but are then seized with punishment; so travel in the land O believers and behold how was the end of those who denied the messengers that is how their affair ended in destruction.

**Travel the land and see the end of the deniers.**

(Do but travel in the land and see) and reflect upon (the nature of the consequence) how the ultimate end was (for those who did deny) the messengers and did not repent of their disbelief. (so travel through the earth, and see what was the end of those who denied). Ways of life have passed away before you; so travel in the land and behold how was the end of those who denied. So, travel the earth and learn from seeing what the fate of those who disbelieved in Allah and His messengers was: their houses are now empty and their power has disappeared. The following was revealed regarding the defeat at Uhud Ways of life have passed away before you all manner of unbelief has preceded where they have been given respite but are then seized with punishment; so travel in the land O believers and behold how was the end of those who denied the messengers that is how their affair ended in destruction. Consider how We acted with those who showed friendship and how We took revenge on those who showed enmity.

**The day of Uhud and the comfort given to the believers.**

When the believers were tested by what happened to them on the day of Uḥud, Allah comforted them by saying that what afflicted them was part of the divinely ordained laws of life, i.e. the believers suffering trials at the hands of the disbelievers and overcoming them in the end after their trial. The following was revealed regarding the defeat at Uhud Ways of life have passed away before you all manner of unbelief has preceded where they have been given respite but are then seized with punishment; so travel in the land O believers and behold how was the end of those who denied the messengers that is how their affair ended in destruction. Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who performed Jihad and knows (tests) those who are patient You did indeed wish for death before you met it. (Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who will perform Jihad and (also) knows (tests) those who are the patient?)[3:142] meaning, you will not earn Paradise until you are tested and thus Allah knows who among you are the ones who struggle and fight in His cause and are patient in the face of the enemy. Those who fear God lead their lives as if God is watching over them, that is, as if all their actions are performed so as to be more and more pleasing in the eyes of God. However, the good end was theirs, and the ultimate defeat was for the disbelievers.

138.text:
"This is an insight to humanity" opens the verse by naming the book itself as the light that is set before every person, and the sources read the insight as the plain statement that shows what is true and what is not, with the whole of humanity named as the people it is given to. "a guide and a lesson to the God-fearing" narrows the company that takes the good from it, and the sources read the guidance as the leading away from error and the lesson as the warning that keeps a person out of what has been forbidden, with the mindful named as the people who benefit from both. The verse before it had called the reader to travel and see the fate of the deniers, and this verse names the book that explains what the eye sees, while the verses after it turn to the community with the word that they should not lose heart. The sources place the two companies in the verse, the whole of humanity that is given the statement and the mindful who take the good from it, so that the gift is read as universal and the benefit as the portion of those who listen.

**The book that explains the truth to mankind.**

(138.. This is a plain statement for mankind), meaning, the Qur'an explains the true reality of things and narrates how the previous nations suffered by the hands of their enemies.
