139.text:
"Do not falter or grieve" opens the verse with the two things that the community was slipping into after the day of the fight, and the sources read the faltering as the weakening in front of the enemy and the grief as the sorrow over what was lost on the field. "for you will have the upper hand" names the promise that is set against the two, and the sources read the upper hand as the victory that is kept for the company that keeps to its faith, whatever the day of the battle has done to it. "if you are true believers" closes the verse with the condition that puts the promise on the state of the heart, and the sources read the word as the reminder that the rank of a people rests on its faith and not on the number of its men. The verses before it had named the book that guides the mindful, and this verse speaks straight to the community in its hour of loss, while the verse after it names the alternation of the days that explains what happened on the field. The sources carry the account of the day itself, with the horsemen who came against the hill and the marksmen who held it, so that the word against grief is read against the noise of a real defeat.

**Do not falter and do not grieve.**

And do not lose heart and do not grieve, and you are the upper-most if you are believers. (Faint not) do not weaken in front of your enemies (nor grieve) about that which you missed of booty on the Day of Uhud, for Allah will reward you in the Hereafter, just as you should not grieve about the killings and wounds inflicted on you, (for ye will overcome them) the ultimate result will be yours through triumph and domination (if ye are (indeed) believers) that triumph and domination is from Allah. Faint not shrink not from fighting the disbelievers neither grieve for what befell you at Uhud for you shall prevail through victory over them if you are truly believers. the response to this last conditional clause is the sum meaning of what has preceded it. Do not become weak, O believers, and do not be sad about what happened to you on the day of Uḥud. Faint not neither grieve for you shall prevail if you are believers. [This] means when you support or launch an attack by means of [the help of] God you should not be afraid of anything other than God. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, were defeated at the Battle of Uhud. Once again, Muslims are being consoled through these verses about what happened to them at the Battle of Uhud.

**You will be the uppermost if you are believers.**

That is not appropriate for you, because you are superior because of your faith, and the uppermost with Allah’s help and the hope of victory, if you have faith in Allah and in His promise to those who are Mindful. (nor be sad, and you will be triumphant if you are indeed believers), for surely, the ultimate victory and triumph will be yours, O believers.) Faint not neither grieve for you shall prevail if you are believers. [This] means when you support or launch an attack by means of [the help of] God you should not be afraid of anything other than God. His words if you are believers that is it is not right that the believer should be overshadowed by fear of anything other than God. They are being told that, under the customary practice of Allah, the disbelievers are the ultimate losers; it does not matter if Muslims have not scored a victory at this time because of their strategic mistake, but should they stick to the demands of their Faith, that is, perseverance and fear of Allah, it will be the disbelievers who shall be the ultimate losers. God has promised the believers success in this world and Paradise in the next. Otherwise, Allah will raise their grades according to the losses they suffered.

**The battle of Uhud and the marksmen who held the hill.**

The Battle of Uhud has been fully described earlier in this Surah through which we already know that the initial success of the Muslim army turned into a defeat in this Jihad because of some of their own shortcomings, although they had already scored an earlier victory (at Badr). A group of Muslim marksmen took the initiative, climbed the hill and targeted the horses of the idolaters until they defeated them, hence His saying (for ye will overcome them) . The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, were defeated at the Battle of Uhud. As they were in this situation, Khalid ibn al-Walid came forward leading a group of horsemen from the idolaters intending to climb over the hill to gain position of height over the Muslims. When he saw what was happening, the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, said: 'O Allah! We have no strength or might except through You.

140.text:
"If you have suffered injuries at Uhud" opens the verse by naming the wound that the community took on the field, and the sources read the sentence as the address that meets the men in the middle of their pain. "they suffered similarly at Badr" sets the other day beside it, and the sources read the sentence as the reminder that the enemy had already tasted a like loss at the hands of the same community. "We alternate these days of victory and defeat among people so that Allah may reveal the true believers" names the practice that rules the whole account, and the sources read the turning of the days as the custom of God in this world, where the win passes from hand to hand so that no people is carried away by its own strength, and the revealing of the sincere is named in the same sentence as the first purpose, and the sources read the revealing as the test that shows what the heart carries. "choose martyrs from among you" names the second, and the sources read it as the honour that is set inside the loss. "and Allah does not like the wrongdoers" closes the verse with the judgment that is placed over the whole account. The verses before it had told the community not to grieve, and this verse gives the reason why the grief must be put down, while the verses after it name the proving and the purifying that the days work in the people of faith. The sources also carry the day of Uhud with its wounded and its dead, and they set the loss beside the loss that the enemy had already taken at Badr, so that the two days are weighed in one hand.

**The wound that was suffered on the day of Uhud.**

It has been said that if Muslims were wounded or hurt in that particular battle, so also were those fighting against them. If you receive a wound, they have received a similar wound. If a wound touches you befalls you at Uhud a like wound qarh or qurh which is the exhaustion that results from a wound and the like already at Badr has touched the other people the disbelievers. If a wound touches you a like wound already has touched the other people. (If ye have received a blow) if you were harmed on the Day of Uhud, (the (disbelieving) people) the people of Makkah (have received) on the Day of Badr (a blow) harm (the like thereof) like the harm you received on the Day of Uhud: O believers, if you suffered injuries and losses on the day of Uḥud, then the disbelievers also suffered injuries and losses just as you did.

**They have received a similar wound.**

It has been said that if Muslims were wounded or hurt in that particular battle, so also were those fighting against them. If you receive a wound, they have received a similar wound. If a wound touches you a like wound already has touched the other people. (If ye have received a blow) if you were harmed on the Day of Uhud, (the (disbelieving) people) the people of Makkah (have received) on the Day of Badr (a blow) harm (the like thereof) like the harm you received on the Day of Uhud: O believers, if you suffered injuries and losses on the day of Uḥud, then the disbelievers also suffered injuries and losses just as you did. Then, in this very battle, many a men from the enemy ranks were killed and wounded initially.

**We alternate these days among people.**

(These are (only) the vicissitudes) the days of the life of this world (which We cause to follow one another for mankind) sometimes the believers have the upper hand over the unbelievers and sometimes it is the unbelievers who have the upper hand over the believers, (to the end that Allah may know) that He may see (those who believe) at the time of jihad (and may choose witnesses from among you) He honours whom He wills among you with martyrdom; (and Allah loveth not wrong-doers) He loves not the idolaters, their religion or their domination. Such days We deal out in turn We dispense them among mankind one day for one group the next day for another that they might be admonished and that God may know through knowledge manifested outwardly those who believe who are sincere in their faith from others; and that He may take witnesses from among you honouring them with martyrdom and God loves not the evildoers the disbelievers that is He will chastise them and the blessings He bestows upon them are only a means of drawing out their punishment. Allah distributes such days between people, whether they have faith or disbelieve, giving victory and defeat as He wills, for reasons of great wisdom. Such days We deal out in turn among mankind and that God may know those who believe; and that He may take witnesses from among you and God loves not the evildoers. And so are the days, that We give to men by turns, that Allah may know (test) those who believe, and that He may take martyrs from among you. In this mortal world, the customary practice of Allah Almighty is to cause the days of hardship and ease, pain and comfort, suffering and peace occur among people by turns. Days come in turns al-ayām nuwabun and circumstances change wa-l-ḥālāt duwalun and nothing is hidden from the Real.

**That Allah may reveal the true believers.**

Among these reasons is to make it clear, those who truly have faith as opposed to those who are hypocrites, and to honour whomever He wills with martyrdom in His cause. And Allah likes not the wrongdoers And that Allah may test those who believe and destroy the disbelievers. (and that Allah may know (test) those who believe,) meaning, "So that We find out who would be patient while fighting the enemies," according to Ibn 'Abbas. Such days We deal out in turn among mankind and that God may know those who believe; and that He may take witnesses from among you and God loves not the evildoers. (These are (only) the vicissitudes) the days of the life of this world (which We cause to follow one another for mankind) sometimes the believers have the upper hand over the unbelievers and sometimes it is the unbelievers who have the upper hand over the believers, (to the end that Allah may know) that He may see (those who believe) at the time of jihad (and may choose witnesses from among you) He honours whom He wills among you with martyrdom; (and Allah loveth not wrong-doers) He loves not the idolaters, their religion or their domination. Allah dislikes those who wrong themselves by giving up striving in his path.

**The witnesses who are taken from among the community.**

Such days We deal out in turn among mankind and that God may know those who believe; and that He may take witnesses from among you and God loves not the evildoers. Besides this, He will confer upon those who have suffered rejection in this world, the foremost honour of being chosen as witnesses in His court. And so are the days, that We give to men by turns, that Allah may know (test) those who believe, and that He may take martyrs from among you. And it will be on the basis of their evidence that the eternal fate of all human beings will be decided. Persevering in God’s cause while facing all odds and difficulties along the way is a form of struggle, or jihad, while standing by one’s pledges and never taking an emotional step are a form of patience, or sabr. If seventy Muslim men were martyred with many wounded, is it not that they had condemned an identical number of their enemies to Hell, and wounded many, a year ago?

141.text:
"and distinguish the true believers and destroy the disbelievers" opens the verse with the two works that the days of trial carry out, and the sources read the distinguishing as the separating of the sincere from the false inside the ranks, so that the company that comes through the test is known for what it is. The destroying of the other company is named in the same breath, and the sources read it as the work of the truth against the people who fight it, since a power that takes the upper hand only to commit aggression carries its own ruin inside it. The verses before it had named the revealing of the true believers and the taking of the witnesses, and this verse completes the reason why the days are turned this way and that, while the verse after it asks the community whether it thought the garden could be entered without the test.

**The believers who are proved.**

And that God may prove the believers purifying them of sins through what befalls them and efface that is destroy the disbelievers. (And that Allah may prove) may forgive (those who believe) for that which befalls them in jihad, (and may blight the disbelievers) and may destroy the unbelievers in war. And that God may prove the believers and efface the disbelievers. The tests of the unseen are a kind of smelting for the servant. Through various stages He purifies him from faults so that he becomes like pure gold without any dross. In this way one becomes clear of defects and purified for God. A part of this wisdom of changing fortunes is the purification of those who have faith from their sins, separating them from the hypocrites, and destroying and removing those who reject the truth. But one will not receive this status merely on the strength of verbal claims to have embraced the faith; each individual will have necessarily to prove his genuineness in terms of the patience he has exercised on earth and his struggle for the cause of God.

**The disbelievers who are effaced.**

And that God may prove the believers purifying them of sins through what befalls them and efface that is destroy the disbelievers. And that God may prove the believers and efface the disbelievers. And efface the disbelievers in the wadis of dispersion tafriqa. (And that Allah may prove) may forgive (those who believe) for that which befalls them in jihad, (and may blight the disbelievers) and may destroy the unbelievers in war. (and destroy the disbelievers), for it is their conduct that if they gain the upper hand, they transgress and commit aggression. And Allah likes not the wrongdoers And that Allah may test those who believe and destroy the disbelievers. However, the good end was theirs, and the ultimate defeat was for the disbelievers.

**The purification that the test works.**

Through various stages He purifies him from faults so that he becomes like pure gold without any dross. A part of this wisdom of changing fortunes is the purification of those who have faith from their sins, separating them from the hypocrites, and destroying and removing those who reject the truth. And that God may prove the believers purifying them of sins through what befalls them and efface that is destroy the disbelievers. The tests of the unseen are a kind of smelting for the servant. In this way one becomes clear of defects and purified for God. As for the scum it passes away as dross [13:17].

**The patience that the struggle asks for.**

Persevering in God’s cause while facing all odds and difficulties along the way is a form of struggle, or jihad, while standing by one’s pledges and never taking an emotional step are a form of patience, or sabr. Whichever group struggles while remaining patient and peaceful will be successful in this world of God as well as in the Hereafter. And it will be on the basis of their evidence that the eternal fate of all human beings will be decided. Difficulties and obstacles will be placed by others in the path of the believer in both cases, that is, whether he wants to base his personal life on faith and belief or stand before others as a witness of the religion of God. If, for some reason, a falsely-motivated power succeeds in getting a short-lived upper hand, the group motivated by the truth should not lose heart and come to think that, from this point onwards, they are always doomed to nothing but defeat.

142.text:
"Do you think you will enter Paradise without Allah proving which of you truly struggled for His cause and patiently endured" opens the verse with the question that cuts off the easy hope, and the sources read it as the address to people who were counting on the name of faith while shrinking from the cost of it. The proving is named as the work of God among the ranks, and the sources read the test as the trial that draws out what a person carries when the road becomes steep, with the struggle named as the labour in the cause of God and the patience named as the staying power that keeps a man at his post, since a claim of faith is not weighed until the day of the battle puts it on the scale, and the book asks the community to look at the day of Uhud as the place where the claim and the truth of it were set side by side. The verses before it had named the purification that the trial works, and this verse names the price that the trial asks, while the verses after it show the wish for the meeting that was spoken before the day arrived.

**The question that is put to the believers.**

The Ayah asks, do you think that you will enter Paradise without being tested with warfare and hardships? (142. Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who will perform Jihad and (also) knows (tests) those who are the patient?) (Or deemed ye) do you think, O group of believers (that you would enter Paradise) without fighting (while yet Allah knoweth not) has not seen (those of you who really strive) in the way of Allah on the Day of Uhud, (nor knoweth those (of you) who are steadfast?) has not see those who are steadfast in the fight against their enemies on the Day of Uhud. Or nay did you suppose you should enter Paradise without God knowing through knowledge manifested outwardly who among you have struggled and who are patient in times of hardship? (Alif Lam Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say: "We believe," and will not be tested?)[29:1,2], This is why He said here,. (Do not wish to encounter the enemy, and ask Allah for your well-being. However, if you do encounter them, then observe patience and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.)

**The struggle and the patience that Allah looks for.**

(Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who will perform Jihad and (also) knows (tests) those who are the patient?)[3:142] meaning, you will not earn Paradise until you are tested and thus Allah knows who among you are the ones who struggle and fight in His cause and are patient in the face of the enemy. (142. Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who will perform Jihad and (also) knows (tests) those who are the patient?) Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who performed Jihad and knows (tests) those who are patient You did indeed wish for death before you met it. Or nay did you suppose you should enter Paradise without God knowing through knowledge manifested outwardly who among you have struggled and who are patient in times of hardship? If his actions correspond to his verbal claim of faith, he is true, and if not, he is false.

**The difficulties that meet the believers.**

When an individual resolves to follow the path of God, he is confronted with many kinds of problems and difficulties created by others. Sometimes these problems produce in him a state of uncertainty; sometimes they make him think of opting for a policy of expediency; sometimes they arouse negative feelings within him; sometimes he is tempted to embrace such a version of God’s religion as has great public appeal. He faces difficulties, but he is not discouraged; he perseveres in sending out the call of truth. Whatever reaction man shows on such occasions serves as an indicator of whether he is false or true in his acceptance of faith. (Or deemed ye) do you think, O group of believers (that you would enter Paradise) without fighting (while yet Allah knoweth not) has not seen (those of you who really strive) in the way of Allah on the Day of Uhud, (nor knoweth those (of you) who are steadfast?) has not see those who are steadfast in the fight against their enemies on the Day of Uhud. This test is a momentous one; but it is as a result of his passing this test that God selects him to be a witness in His divine court.

**The patience that the day of battle asks.**

(Do not wish to encounter the enemy, and ask Allah for your well-being. However, if you do encounter them, then observe patience and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.) (Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who will perform Jihad and (also) knows (tests) those who are the patient?)[3:142] meaning, you will not earn Paradise until you are tested and thus Allah knows who among you are the ones who struggle and fight in His cause and are patient in the face of the enemy. If, for some reason, a falsely-motivated power succeeds in getting a short-lived upper hand, the group motivated by the truth should not lose heart and come to think that, from this point onwards, they are always doomed to nothing but defeat. It has been said that if Muslims were wounded or hurt in that particular battle, so also were those fighting against them. Sometimes these problems produce in him a state of uncertainty; sometimes they make him think of opting for a policy of expediency; sometimes they arouse negative feelings within him; sometimes he is tempted to embrace such a version of God’s religion as has great public appeal.

143.text:
"You certainly wished for the opportunity for martyrdom before encountering it" opens the verse by naming the eagerness that the community had carried before the day came, and the sources read the wish as the longing for death in the way of God that the men had spoken of while the field was still far off. "now you have seen it with your own eyes" closes the verse with the sight that answers the wish, and the sources read the seeing as the day of Uhud itself, where the fighting stood before them and the men met what they had asked for. The verses before it had asked whether the garden could be entered without the struggle, and this verse shows the community standing inside the answer, with the wish of the tongue now a thing they have looked at with the eye. The sources also carry the account of the day with its swords and its dust, so that the verse is read as the gentle rebuke of a people who had asked for a thing before they knew what it would cost.

**The wish for death before the day came.**

(And verily ye used to wish for death) in war (before ye met it (in the field) on the Day of Uhud. You were longing for tamannawna one of the two letters tā’ has been omitted from the original tatamannawna death before you met it when you said ‘Would that we had a day like the Day of Badr in order to attain what its martyrs attained. O believers, you wished to meet the disbelievers so that you could gain martyrdom for the sake of Allah, like your brothers did on the day of Badr, before you saw the severity and ways of death. You were longing for death before you met it. Before today, you wished that you could meet the enemy and were eager to fight them.

**Now you have seen it with your own eyes.**

(Now ye have seen it) you have seen fighting and war on the Day of Uhud, (with your eyes!) you saw the swords of the unbelievers, ran away from them and did not remain unshaken with your Prophet! ’ Now you have seen it that is the cause of it war looking on that is with your eyes open and contemplating the conditions so why did you retreat? The pangs of longing come after being patient in enduring difficulties yet When tears flow down cheeks The one who is crying is distinguished from the one who is only pretending.

**The problems and difficulties that meet the one who follows the truth.**

When an individual resolves to follow the path of God, he is confronted with many kinds of problems and difficulties created by others. Sometimes these problems produce in him a state of uncertainty; sometimes they make him think of opting for a policy of expediency; sometimes they arouse negative feelings within him; sometimes he is tempted to embrace such a version of God’s religion as has great public appeal. He faces difficulties, but he is not discouraged; he perseveres in sending out the call of truth. Let us imagine a servant of God who comes forward as a preacher of truth before the people. Even when he has to pay the price with his life and property, his stand is not shaken. This test is a momentous one; but it is as a result of his passing this test that God selects him to be a witness in His divine court.

**The causes of the defeat and the heart that does not fall.**

Instead of taking this negative attitude, they should rather go about finding out the causes of that defeat, and once they have discovered those, they should take corrective measures and eliminate all possibilities of repeating those mistakes. If, for some reason, a falsely-motivated power succeeds in getting a short-lived upper hand, the group motivated by the truth should not lose heart and come to think that, from this point onwards, they are always doomed to nothing but defeat. Do you think that you will enter Paradise before Allah knows (tests) those of you who performed Jihad and knows (tests) those who are patient You did indeed wish for death before you met it. "Muhammad is no more than a messenger" opens the verse with the word that puts the messenger in his place among the servants of God, and the sources read the sentence as the answer to the cry that had gone up on the field when the rumor of his death ran through the ranks. "Those who do so will not harm Allah whatsoever, and Allah will reward those who are grateful" closes the verse with the two ends of the road, the loss that falls on the man who turns and the wage that is kept for the man who stays. Here, it has been hinted that they made a mistake when they abandoned the duty assigned to them by the Holy Prophet in order to collect spoils. 149.text:
"O believers! If you yield to the disbelievers" opens the verse with the address to the community and the danger that stands at its door, and the sources read the yielding as the listening to the enemies of the faith when they invite the believers back to the road they came from. "they will drag you back to disbelief" names the end of that listening, and the sources read the turning back as the return to the old religion, with the enemy named as the one who pulls the man away from his footing and not merely as an adviser. "and you will become losers" closes the verse with the end of the road, and the sources read the loss as the ruin that takes the man in this world with his faith and in the world to come with his portion. The verses before it had named the companies that prayed for the help of their Lord, and this verse warns the community against the voices that came to it after the setback on the field, while the verses after it name the Guardian who is better than every helper the enemy can offer. The sources also carry the words of the hypocrites among them, who came with the offer of the old faith when the news of the battle had spread, so that the verse is read as the answer to a real invitation that was made to the community in its hour of weakness. The sources also weigh the two offers that stood before the believers on that day, the promise of the old faith that asked nothing of them and the word of God that asked everything, and they read the verse as the warning that a community which leans on the strength of its enemies will lose the ground it stands on.

**The setback of the battle of Uhud.**

When Muslims faced a temporary setback during the battle of Uhud and rumours went around that the Prophet has been martyred, the hypocrites found an occasion for mischief under the shadows of a battle nearly lost. They said to Muslims: 'Now, that the Prophet is no more with us, why should we not go back to our old faith and thus get rid of all conflicts between us?' This shows how ugly the conduct of hypocrites was and how avowed an enemy they were to Muslims. The temporary defeat of the Muslims at the battle of Uhud gave an opportunity to the opponents of Islam to prove their stand that the credo of the Prophet and his companions was not a divine matter. It was just the boyish enthusiasm of certain people and now they were suffering for it. Hudhayfa [Ibn al-Yaman] and 'Ammar [Ibn Yasir]! This Ayah means, Allah gave them the upper hand to try and test you, O believers,.

**Those who would make you turn back on your heels.**

The Qur'anic expression, 'they will make you turn back on your heels', means that the real objective of anti-Islam people is to disengage Muslims from their Faith through engineered suspicion either overtly or covertly, the later method being designed and implemented in a manner which serves to gradually decrease the love and honour of Islam from their hearts resulting in a reversal of their position. 150.text:
"But no! Allah is your Guardian" opens the verse with the word that cuts across the offer of the enemy, and the sources read the guardian as the one who keeps the community and sets its affairs on the right road. "and He is the best Helper" closes the verse with the rank that is given to the help of God over every other help, and the sources read the sentence as the teaching that the aid of a creature comes with a price while the aid of the Lord comes with kindness. The verses before it had warned the community against the voices that called it back, and this verse puts the answer in its mouth, while the verses after it name the fear that is cast into the hearts of the people who set partners beside their Lord. The sources also draw the comparison between the two helpers, and they read the help of any other as a favour that the helper lays over the neck of the helped, while the help of God is a kindness that asks for no return. The verse is set at the head of a passage that teaches the community where its strength lies after the setback of the field, and the sources read the whole of it as the turning of the eye from the creature to the Creator.

**Allah is your Protector and Helper.**

(But Allah is your Protector) He preserves you and will make you triumphant against them, (and He is the best of helpers) He is the strongest of helpers. Nay but God is your Protector your Helper and He is the best of helpers so obey only Him and not them. These disbelievers will not help you if you obey them; rather, Allah is your helper against your enemies. Nay but God is your protector and He is the best of helpers. [This] means that if you obey the adversaries they will pull you into their states and cast you into their darknesses. Nay God is your protector your helper the One who aids you Your Master and the One who sets your affairs aright. The statement, '...Allah is your Lord and He is the best of helpers' tells Muslims to place their trust in Allah and rely on His help alone.

**The best of helpers above every other help.**

And He is the best of helpers because He aids you against your lower selves and protects you from their evil. Anyone other than Him adds to your afflictions when they help you because they aid your lower selves against you. And He is the best of helpers because anyone other than Him holds a favor over you in helping you while He rewards you for your asking for His help. It is said that when you ask someone for help you need to give him something of value and then he may or may not help you. But when you ask [God] for help He gives you every kindness and takes no pleasure in not helping you. So, obey Him, for He, may He be glorified, is the best of helpers, and you will not need anyone apart from Him. (But Allah is your Protector) He preserves you and will make you triumphant against them, (and He is the best of helpers) He is the strongest of helpers.

**The trust that Muslims place in Allah.**

The statement, '...Allah is your Lord and He is the best of helpers' tells Muslims to place their trust in Allah and rely on His help alone. Even if their antagonists come up with plans of help, Muslims should not go by these against the injunctions of Allah and the Messenger. They said to Muslims: 'Now, that the Prophet is no more with us, why should we not go back to our old faith and thus get rid of all conflicts between us?' This shows how ugly the conduct of hypocrites was and how avowed an enemy they were to Muslims. This shows how ugly the conduct of hypocrites was and how avowed an enemy they were to Muslims. [This] means that if you obey the adversaries they will pull you into their states and cast you into their darknesses.
