When Muslims faced a temporary setback during the battle of Uhud and rumours went around that the Prophet has been martyred, the hypocrites found an occasion for mischief under the shadows of a battle nearly lost. In the previous verses, it will be recalled, the instruction was to follow the men of Allah; here, the instruction is not to act upon the advice of hypocrites and anti-Islam people. Indeed, the instruction is to continue taking guard against them. The temporary defeat of the Muslims at the battle of Uhud gave an opportunity to the opponents of Islam to prove their stand that the credo of the Prophet and his companions was not a divine matter. However, such happenings, even if the results of the Muslims’ own errors, are, at all events, ‘test papers’ from God. Such happenings serve as a two-sided trial for the believer. He passes the test only if he perseveres at all times, is not influenced by the adverse remarks of others and is not discouraged by temporary setbacks.

151.text:
"We will cast horror into the hearts of the disbelievers for associating false gods with Allah" opens the verse with the help that the Guardian sends ahead of the fight, and the sources read the horror as the fear that falls on the enemy and takes the steadiness out of his ranks, so that the believers face men whose hearts are already shaken. "a practice He has never authorized" names the ground on which that horror stands, and the sources read the false gods as the partners that were joined to the worship of God with no warrant from Him whatsoever. "The Fire will be their home" and "what an evil place for the wrongdoers to stay" close the verse with the dwelling that is kept for that company, and the sources read the fire as the end of the road that begins with the setting of a partner beside the Lord. The verses before it had named the Guardian and the best Helper, and this verse shows the hand of that Guardian at work against the people who fight His messengers, while the verses after it turn back to the day of the fight and the promise that was kept on the field before it was lost by the error of the community. The sources also carry the account of the enemy column that set out for Madīnah and turned back on the road with its heart full of dread, so that the verse is read as a promise that was already being kept in the days that followed the battle.

**The fear that is cast into the hearts of the enemy.**

(We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they joined others in worship with Allah, for which He sent no authority; their abode will be the Fire and how evil is the abode of the wrongdoers). Allah next conveys the good news that He will put fear of the Muslims, and feelings of subordination to the Muslims in the hearts of their disbelieving enemies, because of their Kufr and Shirk. (We shall cast terror) fear of you such that they run from you (into the hearts of those who disbelieve) the unbelievers of Makkah (because they ascribe unto Allah partners, for which no warrant hath been revealed) either in a Scripture nor taught by a messenger. We will cast terror read ru‘b or ru‘ub into the hearts of the disbelievers after departing from Uhud they resolved to return in order to exterminate the Muslims but they were terrified and did not return; for what they have associated because of their associating with God that for which He has revealed no warrant that is no argument in support of its worship namely idols; their abode shall be the Fire; evil is the abode the resting place of the evildoers the disbelievers. Allah will put great fear in the hearts of the disbelievers, so that they are not able to stand firm to fight you. We will cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers; for that they have associated with God that for which He sent down no authority; their abode shall be the fire; evil is the abode of the evildoers. God designated our Prophet to cast terror ruʿb from Him into the hearts of His enemies. [The Prophet] said:

**The associating of partners with Allah with no authority.**

We will cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers; for that they have associated with God that for which He sent down no authority; their abode shall be the fire; evil is the abode of the evildoers. The word, sultan, rendered here as 'authority' includes all revealed or rational bases of their position. This is because of worshipping false gods next to Allah, and following their own desires, when no proof has been sent down to them to do so. However, such happenings, even if the results of the Muslims’ own errors, are, at all events, ‘test papers’ from God. A happening like that of Uhud must take place in this world in order to find out who are the ones who truly trust in God and who are the ones who are to fall by the wayside.

**The Fire that is their dwelling place.**

(Their habitation) their dwelling-place (is the Fire, and hapless the abode of the wrong-doers) the dwelling-place of the unbelievers is the Fire. We will cast terror read ru‘b or ru‘ub into the hearts of the disbelievers after departing from Uhud they resolved to return in order to exterminate the Muslims but they were terrified and did not return; for what they have associated because of their associating with God that for which He has revealed no warrant that is no argument in support of its worship namely idols; their abode shall be the Fire; evil is the abode the resting place of the evildoers the disbelievers. Fear hayba and force qahr would hardly be right in hearts were it not from Him and used with those who follow falsehood make false claims and misrepresent [the truth].

**The company that turned back on the road to Makkah.**

The promise of casting awe and fear into the hearts of the disbelievers in this verse was made in the back-ground of the battle of Uhud when the disbelievers of Arabia marched back to Makkah without any obvious reason and inspite of defeat overtaking Muslims (Baydawi). However, after having covered a certain distance on their way to Makkah, they awoke to their folly. When they thought of marching back to Madīnah, Allah Almighty filled their hearts with such awe and fear that they could not muster the courage to do so. After Uhud, Abu Sufyan and the idolaters headed toward Makkah. But after they traversed a certain distance, they felt regret, saying: But when they decided to do so, Allah, exalted is He, cast terror in their hearts which made them decide against what they had resolved to do. We massacred them such that none of them remained except those who fled from the battlefield and then we left them alone.

**The five things that were given to the Prophet.**

(I was given five things that no other Prophet before me was given. I was aided with fear the distance of one month, the earth was made a Masjid and clean place for me, I was allowed war booty, I was given the Intercession, and Prophets used to be sent to their people, but I was sent to all mankind particularly.) God designated our Prophet to cast terror ruʿb from Him into the hearts of His enemies. [The Prophet] said: If you see that they defeated us, do not rush to help us.' The disbelievers gave flight when we met them, and we saw their women fleeing up the mountain while lifting up their clothes revealing their anklets and their legs. Then a person shouted, 'Muhammad has been killed.' So we pulled back, and the disbelievers followed us, after we had killed those who carried their flag, and none of them dared to come close the flag, until then.'" Muhammad bin Ishaq said next, "The flag of the disbelievers was left on the ground until 'Amrah bint 'Alqamah Al-Harithiyyah picked it up and gave it to the Quraysh who held it." But, this whole deal came into the knowledge of the Holy Prophet in Madīnah through revelation.

152.text:
"Indeed, Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you initially swept them away by His Will" opens the verse with the day on which the word of God was kept, and the sources read the sentence as the reminder that the beginning of the battle belonged to the community, when the enemy was driven back by the help of its Lord and not by the weight of its arms. "then your courage weakened and you disputed about the command and disobeyed" names the turn, and the sources read the weakening as the moment when the archers left the post that the messenger had fixed for them and the dispute as the argument that rose over whether the post should still be kept. "after Allah had brought victory within your reach" names the gift that was in their hands when they turned away from it, and the sources read the sight of the victory as the proof of what was thrown away for the sake of the goods of the day. "Some of you were after worldly gain while others desired a heavenly reward" names the two desires that split the ranks, and "He denied you victory over them as a test" names the hand that let the enemy come back. "yet He has pardoned you" and "And Allah is Gracious to the believers" close the verse with the mercy that was given after the fault. The verses before it had named the fear that was cast into the enemy, and this verse explains how the day turned in the middle of the fight, while the verse after it shows the community running in panic with the call of the messenger sounding behind it. The sources carry the words of the archers who were told to keep their place whatever they saw on the field, and they read the whole account as the teaching that the promise of God is tied to the command of His messenger.

**The promise that was kept at the opening of the fight.**

Allah kept the promise He gave you of victory over your enemies on the day of Uḥud, when you were engaging them in battle, by Allah’s permission, until you became weaker in your resolve to do as the Messenger had commanded you, and you disagreed about whether to stay at your posts or leave them in order to obtain the gains of war. (Allah verily made good His promise unto you) on the Day of Uhud (when ye routed them) when you killed them at the beginning of the fight (by His leave) by His command and help, (until (the moment) when your courage failed you) to fight against the enemy, (and ye disagreed about the order) you disagreed about the question of war (and ye disobeyed) the Prophet by leaving your positions, (after He had shown you that for which ye long) victory and booty. God has been true to His promise towards you of giving you victory when you slew them by His leave by His will until you lost heart until you shrank from battle and quarrelled disagreed over the command that is the command of the Prophet s that you remain at the foot of the mountain for the arrow attack some of you saying ‘Let us depart for our comrades have been given victory’ others saying ‘We should not disobey the command of the Prophet s’; and you disobeyed his command and abandoned your station in search of the booty after He God had shown you what you longed for of assistance the response to the clause containing idhā is indicated by what precedes it that is to say ‘when you lost heart He denied you His assistance’.

**The archers who left the post for the spoils.**

(Some of you) some of the archers (desired the world) with their jihad and fighting. This refers to those who abandoned their positions and rushed to gather the booty, (and some of you desired the Hereafter) with their jihad and fighting. This refers to 'Abdullah Ibn Jubayr and his fellow believers who remained at their positions until they were killed. You disobeyed the Messenger’s command to stay at your positions no matter what may happen. This occurred after Allah showed you the victory over your enemies that you wanted so much. Among you are those who desire the goods of this world, and it was those who left their positions; and among you are those who desire the reward of the Afterlife, and it was those who stayed at their positions, obeying the Messenger’s command. As stated in the verses, the noble Companions were split in two groups at that time; some sought the mundane while others sought the Hereafter. They, as the first observers of the operation of the Law, knew it beyond doubt that their due share in the spoils was under no condition subject to being more or less.

**The two desires that split the ranks.**

Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the next world. Some of you desired this world abandoning his station for the sake of the booty; and some of you desired the Hereafter holding to it until he was slain such as ‘Abd Allāh b. Among you are those who desire the goods of this world, and it was those who left their positions; and among you are those who desire the reward of the Afterlife, and it was those who stayed at their positions, obeying the Messenger’s command. The worth of someone is his desire, and the want of someone is his leader. Wanting this world is all trickery and delusion, wanting the afterworld is all occupation with the work of wage-earners, and wanting the Patron is all celebration and joy. And, did their participation entitle them to some larger share?

**The turning away that was a test.**

Then Allah turned you away from them and gave them power over you so as to test you, and to make clear who were the believers who were patient with trials and who were those who abandoned their positions and became weak. (Therefore He made you flee from them) defeated and made them triumph over you, (that He might try you) that He might test you with the archers' disobedience. But, equally worth noticing here are the graces of Allah Almighty showered on the noble Companions side by side with the element of warning. To begin with, by saying (so that He may test you) it was made clear that this temporary setback did not come as punishment, rather, it was to test them. Then He made you flee from them, that He might test you. (Allah verily made good His promise unto you) on the Day of Uhud (when ye routed them) when you killed them at the beginning of the fight (by His leave) by His command and help, (until (the moment) when your courage failed you) to fight against the enemy, (and ye disagreed about the order) you disagreed about the question of war (and ye disobeyed) the Prophet by leaving your positions, (after He had shown you that for which ye long) victory and booty. But, Allah Almighty has His ways with people; He very much likes to see the hearts of the Companions of His Messenger clean and untouched even by the remotest idea of any tilt towards material possession.

**The kindness of Allah to the believers.**

Allah has indeed forgiven you for what you committed when you went against the Messenger’s command, and Allah’s grace for the believers is great: guiding them to faith, forgiving their disobedience, and rewarding them for the difficulties they go through. (Yet now He hath forgiven you) He did not exterminate you. (Allah is a Lord of Kindness to believers) in that He did not exterminate them, i.e. the archers. But surely, He forgave you, and Allah is Most Gracious to the believers (And remember) when you ran away without even casting a side glance at anyone, and the Messenger was in your rear calling you back. Then, comes the statement, which very clearly proclaims:

**The disagreements that broke the unity of the community.**

Yet unity cannot come about in a society solely on the basis of uniformity of opinion. Only when a community thinks on this level can it remain united and powerful. When people start breaking up into factions, just because of disagreements, the resulting weakness will most certainly lead to defeat. But in the case of the Muslims, their weakness and defeat are traceable solely to their disunity arising from dissension. It takes united action also, even in the face of divisive opinions, to ensure total cohesiveness within a community. When believers show steadfastness at crucial moments, God sends His special succour, that is, He strikes terror into the hearts of those who deny the truth. They are ultimately defeated at the hands of true believers.

153.text:
"Remember when you were running far away in panic, not looking at anyone" opens the verse with the picture of the community climbing the hill with its back to the field, and the sources read the flight as the men leaving the ground of the fight and paying no heed to the one who was calling them back. "while the Messenger was calling to you from behind" names the call that followed them up the slope, and the sources read the sentence as the voice of the messenger from the rear, and the sources carry the words of the man who called out to them by name when the rumor of the death had taken their hearts. "So Allah rewarded your disobedience with distress upon distress, Now, do not grieve over the victory you were denied or the injury you suffered" names the wage of the day, and the sources read the first distress as the pain of the defeat itself and the second as the grief that came when the messenger could not be found. The same sentence names the lesson that the pain was sent to teach, and the sources read the sentence as the discipline that was meant to set the heart of the community on what is kept with God rather than on what was taken from its hand. "And Allah is All-Aware of what you do" closes the verse with the knowledge that sees every deed and every heart. The verses before it had named the pardon that followed the fault of the archers, and this verse names the hour of the flight and the call that sounded behind it, while the verses after it lift the eye of the community to the grief that is a mercy and to the firmness that follows the lesson. The sources also note that the first call and the second came in the middle of the confusion, and they read the whole verse as the account of a day on which the community learned the price of leaving its post.

**The exit from the battlefield and the hill of Uhud.**

Then Allah mentioned how they turned their back on the Prophet ﷺ because of their fear of the enemy, saying: (When ye climbed) the hill after being defeated (and paid no heed to anyone) paid no heed to the Prophet and did not wait for him, (while the messenger) Muhammad, (in your rear, was calling you (to fight) he was behind you, O group of believers, saying: Remember, O believers, when you ran away on the day of Uḥud, when failure came upon you because you went against the command of the Messenger. None of you looked at anyone else, and the Messenger called you from behind, between you and the idolaters, saying, ‘Come to me, servants of Allah! In the first verse here, the Holy Qur'an describes the exit of the Companions from the battlefield, their inability to come back even when called by the Holy Prophet in person, the consequent grief that afflicted him because of their conduct and, later on, the incidence of the Companions feeling sorry for the sorrow they brought on their master. When you were ascending not turning around for anyone and the Messenger was calling you from your rear so he rewarded you with grief for grief so that you might not grieve for what escaped you neither for what befell you; and God is aware of what you do. Remember when you were ascending fleeing in the distance not turning around not stopping for anyone and the Messenger was calling you from your rear saying ‘Come to me servants of God this way servants of God!’ so He rewarded you He requited you with grief through defeat for grief ghamman bi-ghamm; the bā’ bi- ‘with’ is said to mean ‘alā ‘for’ because of the grief that you caused the Prophet when you disobeyed his command that is with grief doubled being in addition to the grief of the booty forfeited so that li-kaylā is semantically connected either to ‘afā ‘He has pardoned’ or athābakum ‘He rewarded you’; the lā of kay-lā is thus extra you might not grieve for what escaped you of booty neither for what befell you of being slain and of defeat; and God is aware of what you do.

**The Messenger who called from behind.**

None of you looked at anyone else, and the Messenger called you from behind, between you and the idolaters, saying, ‘Come to me, servants of Allah! According to hadith narrations, when Sayyidna Ka'b ibn Malik called out to them, Muslims heard his call and reassembled. The author of Ruh al-Ma'ani resolves this by saying that the first call came from the Messenger of Allah himself which could not be heard by the Companions and they kept going the way they were going. That was the time when Sayyidna Ka'b ibn Malik called. When he called, there was obviously no refutation of the news with the call. Finally, when Sayyidna Ka'b ibn Malik called out, his call included a refutation of this news mentioning the fact that the Messenger of Allah was alive. So, the companions (of 'Abdullah bin Jubayr) said, 'The booty, the booty!' 'Abdullah bin Jubayr said, 'Allah's Messenger commanded me not to allow you to abandon your position.' They refused to listen, and when they left their position, Muslims were defeated and seventy of them were killed.

**The distress upon distress that was given.**

’ Allah repaid you for this with pain and distress, followed by pain and distress: first because of the victory and gains of war you lost; and then with the rumour that the Prophet had been killed that spread among you. (Therefore He rewarded you grief for grief) in addition to the grief wrought upon you by Khalid Ibn al-Walid, He also inflicted on you the grief of death and defeat, (that (He might teach) you not to sorrow either for that which ye missed) of booty (or for that which befell you) and that you do not sorrow for that which befell you of deaths and injuries. There did Allah give you one distress after another by way of requital, to teach you not to grieve for that which had escaped you, nor for what struck you. Mujahid and Qatadah said, "The first distress was when they heard that Muhammad was killed and the second when they suffered casualties and injury. As far as the displeasure of Allah and the sorrow of His Messenger are concerned, these can be explained by saying - if they had stayed unagitated and firm, they could have recognized the calling voice.

**The grief that was sent to teach the community.**

Later you came to know that the Prophet had not been killed, so that you would not grieve about the victory and gains of war that you lost, or the deaths and wounds that you received, as a way of making misfortune and pain easier on you. (Therefore He rewarded you grief for grief) in addition to the grief wrought upon you by Khalid Ibn al-Walid, He also inflicted on you the grief of death and defeat, (that (He might teach) you not to sorrow either for that which ye missed) of booty (or for that which befell you) and that you do not sorrow for that which befell you of deaths and injuries. In the first verse here, the Holy Qur'an describes the exit of the Companions from the battlefield, their inability to come back even when called by the Holy Prophet in person, the consequent grief that afflicted him because of their conduct and, later on, the incidence of the Companions feeling sorry for the sorrow they brought on their master. The first verse here mentions the sorrows of the sahabah, the noble Companions of the Holy Prophet . He forgave the error you committed, because, and Allah knows best, the idolators were many and well supplied, while Muslims had few men and few supplies. (after He showed you what you love), that is, victory over the disbelievers,.

**The knowledge of Allah that sees every deed.**

(Allah is Informed of what ye do) in jihad as well as in defeat. But surely, He forgave you, and Allah is Most Gracious to the believers (And remember) when you ran away without even casting a side glance at anyone, and the Messenger was in your rear calling you back. In the first verse here, the Holy Qur'an describes the exit of the Companions from the battlefield, their inability to come back even when called by the Holy Prophet in person, the consequent grief that afflicted him because of their conduct and, later on, the incidence of the Companions feeling sorry for the sorrow they brought on their master. Finally, when Sayyidna Ka'b ibn Malik called out, his call included a refutation of this news mentioning the fact that the Messenger of Allah was alive.

154.text:
"Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you" opens the verse with the gift that came down on the night of the battle, and the sources read the serenity as the peace that settled on the hearts of the faithful after the fear of the field, with the drowsiness named as the sign that the peace had entered the body as well as the soul. "while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah, the thoughts of pre-Islamic ignorance, They ask, Do we have a say in the matter? Say, O Prophet, All matters are destined by Allah" names the other company and the speech that rose from it, and the sources read the disturbance as the unrest of the people whose hearts were not settled, with the question named as the fruit of the old way of weighing the power of God by the strength of men. "They conceal in their hearts what they do not reveal to you. They say to themselves, If we had any say in the matter, none of us would have come to die here. Say, O Prophet, Even if you were to remain in your homes, those among you who were destined to be killed would have met the same fate. Through this, Allah tests what is within you and purifies what is in your hearts" names the hidden speech and the answer that closes it, and it teaches that a house cannot stand between a man and the term that is written for him. "And Allah knows best what is hidden in the heart" closes the verse with the knowledge that sees what no eye sees. The verses before it had named the grief that taught the community, and this verse names the sleep that came after it, while the verse after it turns to the men who fled from the field and the pardon that met them when they came back, so that the two companies of the night stand side by side in the account.

**The serenity that came down after the distress.**

(Then, after grief, He sent down security for you) from the enemy. Then He sent down upon you after grief security — a slumber nu‘āsan ‘slumber’ substitutes for amanatan ‘security’ overcoming yaghshā or taghshā a party of you namely the believers. A group among you, who trusted in the promise of Allah, became overcome by sleep because of the peace and serenity in their hearts. Allah reminds His servants of His favor when He sent down on them tranquillity and slumber that overcame them while they were carrying their weapons and feeling distress and grief. Then He sent down upon you after grief security-a slumber overcom ing a party of you and a party whose own souls distressed them thinking wrongly of God thoughts of the age of ignorance saying Have we any part whatever in the affairḍ Say: Even on the most earth-shaking of occasions, when people find it impossible to sleep, the believers are able to revitalize themselves with the soothing effect of sleep.

**The drowsiness that overcame a party of them.**

(As slumber did it overcome a party of you) such that those among you who had sincerity and certitude slept, (while (the other) party, who were anxious on their own account) who were overcome with anxiousness about themselves. A group among you, who trusted in the promise of Allah, became overcome by sleep because of the peace and serenity in their hearts. Slumber overtook a party of you, while another party was thinking about themselves and thought wrongly of Allah – the thought of ignorance. This was demonstrated on the occasion of Uhud when, despite the severest of conditions, they were able to have a good night’s sleep. Rested and refreshed, they then pursued the enemy forces as far as Hamraul-Asad, some eight miles from Madīnah. Severely wounded and defeated, they would not have been able to take any further action, had calm not descended upon them.

**The party that was disturbed by evil thoughts.**

This refers to Mu'attib Ibn Qushayr, the hypocrite, and his fellows who were not overcome by sleep, (thought wrongly of Allah) that He would not come to the help of His Messenger and his Companions, (the thought of ignorance) as they did think of Him in the time of ignorance [before the advent of Islam]. Another group were not blessed with security or sleep, and they were the hypocrites, who only worried about their own safety, and felt upset and scared. They thought badly of Allah, thinking that He would not help His Prophet or support His servants, like those of the time of ignorance before Islam did, who did not understand Allah’s reality. This group thought that the idolators achieved ultimate victory, when their forces took the upper hand in battle, and that Islam and its people would perish. This is typical of people of doubt and hesitation, in the event of a hardship, they fall into such evil thoughts. This is the state in which the believers live, whereas those who have not made God their guardian and protector in the full sense of these words, inevitably fear for their own lives. Bereft of any concern for religion, they are engrossed in their own selves.

**The words of the hypocrites about the affair of the day.**

These hypocrites said, due to their ignorance of Allah, that they did not have a say in whether they went out to fight; and if they had, they would not have done so. (The cause) triumph and domination (belongeth wholly to Allah) they are in the Hand of Allah. Tell them, O Prophet, in reply, that everything that happens is up to Allah, and that He decreed that they would go out to fight. Say to them ‘The affair belongs entirely read accusative kullahu to denote an emphasis or nominative kulluhu as a subject of a new sentence the predicate of which is what follows to God’ that is to say the decree is His He does what He wills. As if in a dream, I heard the words of Mu'attib bin Qushayr, 'If we had anything to do with the affair, none of us would have been killed here.' I memorized these words of his, which Allah mentioned later on,. They conceal within their hearts what they do not disclose what they do not manifest to you saying yaqūlūna ‘saying’ is an explication of the preceding statement ‘Had we had any part in the affair we would not have been slain here’ that is to say ‘Had the choice been ours we would not have set out and thus been slain; but we were forced to set out’.

**Even if they had stayed in their homes.**

(Even though ye had been in your houses) in Medina, (those appointed to be slain would have gone forth to the places where they were to lie) where they were to be killed at Uhud. "Even if you had remained in your homes, those for whom death was decreed would certainly have gone forth to the place of their death," but that Allah might test what is in your breasts; and to purify that which was in your hearts (sins), and Allah is All-Knower of what is in the breasts Those of you who turned back on the day the two hosts met, Shaytan only caused them to err because of some of what they had earned. Say to them ‘Even if you had been in your houses with some among you whom God had appointed that they be slain those of you for whom it had been appointed decreed that they be slain would have sallied forth would have gone forth to the places where they were to lie’ the battleground where they were to fall and they would have been slain; and their staying put at home would not have saved them for God’s decree will be inevitably. These hypocrites hide in themselves doubt and bad opinion which they do not show to you, saying that if they had a say in whether they had gone to fight, then people would not have been killed in this place. Even if you had been in your houses those for whom it had been appointed that they be slain would have sallied forth to the places where they were to lie that God might try what was in your breasts and that He might prove what was in your hearts; and God knows what is in the breasts. (They hide within themselves (a thought) which they reveal not unto you) for fear that they would be killed, (saying: Had we had any part in the cause we should not have been slain here. Say) to the hypocrites, O Muhammad:

**The test that purifies what is in the hearts.**

((All this has been) in order that Allah might try) test (what is in your breasts) what is in the breast of the hypocrites (and prove) bring to the fore (what is in your hearts) of hypocrisy. (Allah is Aware of what is hidden in the breasts (of men) He knows what is in people's hearts of good and evil, i.e. the hearts of hypocrites; it is also said that it refers to the hearts of the archers. (that Allah might test what is in your breasts; and to purify that which was in your hearts,) means, so that He tests you with whatever befell you, to distinguish good from evil and the deeds and statements of the believers from those of the hypocrites,. And He did what He did at Uhud that God might try that He might test what was in your breasts your hearts of sincerity or hypocrisy and that He might prove that He might distinguish what was in your hearts; and God knows what is in the breasts what is in the hearts. Nothing can be hidden from Him and He tries people only to make matters manifest for them.

155.text:
"Indeed, those believers who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds" opens the verse with the account of the men who turned on the day of the battle, and the sources read the slipping as the work of the enemy of God who used the faults of the community to push it away from its post. The sources also read the misdeeds as the disobedience of the archers and the taste for the spoils that moved them, so that the slip is traced to a cause inside the ranks and not to a strength in the enemy. "But Allah has pardoned them" names the mercy that followed the fault, and the sources read the pardon as the covering of what happened on the field, with the clemency named next as the patience of God who did not hurry the punishment. "Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing" closes the verse with the two names that carry the whole account. The verses before it had named the party that was disturbed by evil thoughts, and this verse names the men who were led aside in the middle of the fight, while the verses after it warn the community against the speech of the people who weigh life and death by the number of the homes they sit in. The sources also note that the slip of the company was not left without an answer, since the mercy of God met the men who had turned and set them back on the road that the community was walking.

**Those who turned back on the day the two hosts met.**

Allah then mentioned those who fled on the Day of Uhud, saying (Lo! those of you who turned back) defeated, meaning: 'Uthman Ibn 'Affan and his fellow believers (on the day when the two hosts) the hosts of Muhammad and Abu Sufyan (met, Satan alone it was who caused them to backslide) Satan enticed them to believe that Muhammad was killed and thus fled to a place about six parasangs (farasikh) from the scene. Those of you who were defeated, O Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, on the day the army of the idolaters and the army of the Muslims met at Uḥud, it was Satan who made you slip, because of what you had earned from doing wrong. Truly those of you who turned away from the battle the day the two hosts the Muslim host and that of the disbelievers encountered each other at Uhud the Muslims with the exception of twelve men — truly Satan made them slip with his evil insinuations through some of what they had earned of sins namely when they disobeyed the Prophet’s command; but God pardoned them; God is Forgiving to believers Forbearing hastening not against the disobedient with punishment. Truly those of you who turned away the day the two hosts encountered each other-truly Satan made them slip through some of what they had earned; but God pardoned them; God is Forgiving Forbearing. (Those of you who turned back on the day the two hosts met, Shaytan only caused them to err because of some of what they had earned. But Allah, indeed, has forgiven them). They were six people in all, (because of some of that which they have earned) because of leaving their positions.

**Satan who made them slip.**

The answer is that the particular past mistake was the obvious reason which gave Satan the incentive to make them slip once again, an effort in which the Satan incidentally succeeded. Truly those of you who turned away the day the two hosts encountered each other-truly Satan made them slip through some of what they had earned; but God pardoned them; God is Forgiving Forbearing. Satan thus made inroads by using the dissension already evident among them. In Ruh al-Ma'ani, a report from Zajjaj says that the Satan made them recall some of their sins in the presence of which they hesitated to appear before their Lord. But there was much more to it; there were wise arrangements made by the Creator behind this slip and its outcome.

**The archers and the post they left.**

When the fifty archers posted at the Mount Uhud pass saw that the Muslims had won the battle, a large number of them insisted on going in pursuit of booty. The battle began well for the Muslims, but turned to near defeat because of the disobedience of a band of fifty archers who had been given the task of guarding a certain pass. The majority from among the fifty Companions who were commanded by the Holy Prophet to guard a hill-top strategic point, with clear instruction not to leave their duty-post, no matter what happens at the battle front underneath, moved away from their assigned place. Granted that the reason for their abandonment of the post of duty was an erroneous independent judgment, as they thought their side had won the battle. The order to guard their post, according to their view, had been carried out, therefore, they thought, they could go down and join in with the rest of Muslims. Moreover, this retreat from the battlefield took place while the Messenger of Allah was with them unmoved from the front line and calling them back from behind them.

**The forgiveness that met them after the slip.**

(Now Allah hath forgiven them) since He did not exterminate them. (Clement) for He did not hasten their punishment. Allah has forgiven them, and will not take them to account for it, out of His favour and mercy. Allah forgives those who repent to Him, and is Forbearing, not quick to punish. But, something more worthy of consideration is what Allah Almighty has done in their case inspite of all their mistakes. However, when they admitted their error, they were forgiven by God, and after the initial setback, God’s succour came to them too.

**Those who turned back and were forgiven.**

Such happenings, whatever their apparent reason, are wrought by God, in order that His true believers may turn to Him in repentance and become worthy of further blessings from Him. The Almighty struck terror into the hearts of their enemies, which resulted in their retreat, although they were just a few miles from Madīnah. Had God’s succour not come, there was nothing to stop them from forcing their entry into Madīnah and uprooting the nascent tree of Islam. This verse alludes to the states of those whose spiritual desire irāda has become meager and their intentions niyyāt weak. Allah reminds His servants of His favor when He sent down on them tranquillity and slumber that overcame them while they were carrying their weapons and feeling distress and grief. "Even if you had remained in your homes, those for whom death was decreed would certainly have gone forth to the place of their death," but that Allah might test what is in your breasts; and to purify that which was in your hearts (sins), and Allah is All-Knower of what is in the breasts Those of you who turned back on the day the two hosts met, Shaytan only caused them to err because of some of what they had earned. Allah then mentioned those who fled on the Day of Uhud, saying (Lo! those of you who turned back) defeated, meaning: 'Uthman Ibn 'Affan and his fellow believers (on the day when the two hosts) the hosts of Muhammad and Abu Sufyan (met, Satan alone it was who caused them to backslide) Satan enticed them to believe that Muhammad was killed and thus fled to a place about six parasangs (farasikh) from the scene.

156.text:
"O believers, Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle" opens the verse with the warning that is put on the community by way of a likeness, and the sources read the sentence as the instruction to keep away from the way of the people who measure death by the road a man travels and by the ground he stands on. "If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed" names the word of those people, and the sources read the sentence as the speech of the hypocrites over the graves of the men who fell, as if a house in the city could have kept a term that God had written. "Allah makes such thinking a cause of agony in their hearts" names the first answer, and the sources read the agony as the regret that is planted in the chest of the man who thinks that he can hold his brother back from what is decreed. "It is Allah who gives life and causes death" names the second answer, and the sources read the sentence as the plain statement that the whole affair belongs to the hand of God and not to the plans of men. "And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do" closes the verse, and the sources read the sentence as the warning that the hidden doubts and the open deeds are all in the sight of the One who keeps the account. The verses before it had named the community that was pardoned for the slip of the day, and this verse keeps the community from the way of thinking that makes a man sit down from the struggle, while the verses after it raise the death in the way of God above the goods that a man gathers in his life. The sources also weigh the two ways of reading the same day, the way of the man who sees only the sword that struck his brother and the way of the man who sees the hand that wrote the term, and they read the verse as the teaching that keeps the heart of the believer steady in the middle of the loss.

**The instruction not to be like the disbelievers.**

Be not like those who disbelieve and who say to their brethren when they travel through the earth or go out to fight: (O you who believe! Be not like those who disbelieve (hypocrites) and who say to their brethren), about their dead brethren,. Then Allah said to the Companions of Muhammad: (O ye who believe!) in Muhammad and the Qur'an. O you who believe be not as the disbelievers who say of their brothers when they travel in the land or are on raiding campaigns 'Had they been with us they would not have died and would not have been slain' - so that God may make that anguish in their hearts. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, do not be like those among the hypocrites who disbelieve, who do not have faith in destiny and Allah’s decree, and who say of their relatives if they travel to earn a living or go out to fight and they die or are killed: (Be not) in war (as those who disbelieved) in secret, i.e. 'Abdullah Ibn Ubayy and his followers who returned to Medina (and said of their brethren) the hypocrites (who went abroad in the land) who journeyed with the Companions of Muhammad (or were fighting in the field) or went with their Prophet in a fighting expedition: Allah forbids His believing servants from the disbelievers' false creed, seen in their statement about those who died in battle and during travel; "Had they abandoned these trips, they would not have met their demise. Prohibiting the Ideas of the Disbeleivers about Death and Predestination.

**If they had stayed with us they would not have died.**

(If they had been (here) with us) in Medina (they would not have died) on their journey (or been killed) during the fighting expedition; (that Allah may make it) make that doubt (anguish) grief (in their hearts. Allah giveth life) on the journey (and causeth death) settlement; (and Allah is Seer of what ye do) of what you say. O you who believe be not as the disbelievers who say of their brothers when they travel in the land or are on raiding campaigns 'Had they been with us they would not have died and would not have been slain' - so that God may make that anguish in their hearts. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Prophet, do not be like those among the hypocrites who disbelieve, who do not have faith in destiny and Allah’s decree, and who say of their relatives if they travel to earn a living or go out to fight and they die or are killed: (when they travel through the earth) for the purpose of trading and otherwise,. (or go out to fight), participating in battles,.

**The regret that is made to grow in their hearts.**

(so that Allah may make it a cause of regret in their hearts.) means, Allah creates this evil thought in their hearts so that their sadness and the grief they feel for their loss would increase. Allah makes this belief in their hearts increase their regret. Whoever makes a habit of worrying about what is past and planning for his future and each new moment - the least of his punishment will be the constriction of his heart through disconcerting worries and the disappearance of the quality of life from his heart because of his forgetfulness and his saying 'if only such and such' or 'maybe such and such'. The result of this kind of thinking is estrangement and grief the constriction of the heart and separation. When a non-believer suffers a setback, he grieves over it, thinking that had he adopted this or that course, he could have been saved.

**It is Allah who gives life and causes death.**

For God gives life and He gives death and so no staying put can prevent death and God sees what you do ta‘malūna or ya‘malūna ‘they do’ and He will requite you for it. Allah alone gives life and death as He wills: staying behind would not stop His decree, and going would not bring it more quickly. (It is Allah that gives life and causes death.) for the creation is under Allah's power, and the decision is His Alone. No one lives or dies except by Allah's leave, and no one's life is increased or decreased except by His decree. All that happens in this world is by the will of God. However, everything takes place under the veil of cause and effect. Incidents appear to have a cause behind them but, actually, they occur at the will of God. One who claims to be a believer, yet regards life and death, success and failure as the results of human strategies, is not true to his claim. But when a believer confronts the same situation, he resigns himself to it by accepting it as the will of God.

**The causes that veil the hand of the Almighty.**

Man’s faith is put to the test through apparent causes, which make it difficult to see the hidden hand of God in all things. The saying of the hypocrites in verse 156 here is an extension of what was cited in verse 154 earlier: ‌ :"If we had any say in the matter, we would have not been killed here. " Since there were chances that sincere Muslims may be affected by such doubt-creating devices used by hypocrites, Muslims were asked through these verses to remain unconcerned with such sayings and doings and adhere to the belief that the span of life and the time of death are ordained by Allah alone. Those, on the other hand, who hold worldly resources important devote their whole lives to providing for the things of this world. But the only things of true value are those which will be theirs in the Hereafter—that is, God’s forgiveness and Paradise. The non-believer is the one who is lost in trying to understand the causes and effects, while the believer is one who penetrates their veil to discover the actual reality. When a man has the conviction that everything happens by God’s will, then all other human causes appear insignificant and not worthy of further consideration. Paradise is something which can be attained only at the cost of one’s life. Man’s existence on earth is the exact price he has to pay to enter Paradise. If he fails to make this sacrifice, he cannot be certain of his fate in the Hereafter.

**Allah sees what you do and keeps the account.**

And Allah is All-Seer of what you do And if you are killed or die in the way of Allah, forgiveness and mercy from Allah are far better than all that they amass And whether you die or are killed, verily, unto Allah you shall be gathered. (And if you are killed or die in the way of Allah, forgiveness and mercy from Allah are far better than all that they amass.)[3:157], indicating that death and martyrdom in Allah's cause are a means of earning Allah's mercy, forgiveness and pleasure. None of what you do is hidden from Him and you will be rewarded according to what you do. O you who believe be not as the disbelievers that is as the hypocrites who say of their brothers that is regarding their affair when they travel in the land and then die or are on raiding campaigns ghuzzan ‘a raiding party’ is the plural of ghāzin and are then slain ‘Had they been with us they would not have died and would not have been slain’ in other words do not say as they say — so that God may make that saying of theirs as a conclusion of their affair anguish in their hearts. (And Allah is All-Seer of what you do,) for His knowledge and vision encompasses all His creation and none of their affairs ever escapes Him. This, indeed, is better than remaining in this life with its short lived delights. Furthermore, whoever dies or is killed will return to Allah, the Exalted and Most Honored, and He will reward him if he has done good deeds, or will punish him for his evil deeds.

The verses before it had warned the community against the speech of the men who counted the dead by the roads they had taken, and this verse answers that speech with the worth of the death in the cause of God, while the verse after it names the meeting with Allah that waits for every soul whether it dies in its bed or falls on the field, and so the two verses answer the speech of the men who counted the dead by the roads they had taken.
