158.text:
"Whether you die or are martyred" opens the verse by gathering the two ends of every life into one sentence, and the sources read the sentence as the removal of the difference between the man who falls on the field and the man who is taken in his bed, since the term is the same in both cases and the hand that writes it is the same. "all of you will be gathered before Allah" closes the verse with the meeting that no soul can escape, and the sources read the gathering as the court at which the account of every man is read, with the honour of the death in the way of God named as the reward of the man who returns to his Lord from the field. The verses before it had set the mercy of God above the goods of the world, and this verse names the return that waits for the whole company, while the verse after it turns to the messenger with the mercy by which he was made gentle with the people who had failed on the day of the battle.

**Whether you die or are slain.**

And if you die or are slain it is to God you shall be mustered. And if you die or are slain it is to God you shall be mustered: And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you die read in both ways muttum or mittum or are slain in the holy struggle or otherwise it is to God and to none other than Him that you shall be mustered in the Hereafter and He will requite you. If you die – however you may die – or you are killed in Allah’s path, you will all return to Allah alone, and He will reward you according to what you have done. (What though ye be slain) on a journey or in settlement (or die) in a fighting expedition, (when unto Allah you are gathered?) after you die. "If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed," so that Allah may make it a cause of regret in their hearts.

**The forgiveness and the mercy that are better.**

And if you are slain in God's way or die forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they amass. If you die – however you may die – or you are killed in Allah’s path, you will all return to Allah alone, and He will reward you according to what you have done. To sacrifice the spirit rūḥ in God is better than life with anything other than God. (And if you are killed or die in the way of Allah, forgiveness and mercy from Allah are far better than all that they amass.)[3:157], indicating that death and martyrdom in Allah's cause are a means of earning Allah's mercy, forgiveness and pleasure.

**Those who return to their Lord after the field.**

Furthermore, whoever dies or is killed will return to Allah, the Exalted and Most Honored, and He will reward him if he has done good deeds, or will punish him for his evil deeds. Returning to God is better for one who knows God than staying behind with anything other than God. If you die – however you may die – or you are killed in Allah’s path, you will all return to Allah alone, and He will reward you according to what you have done. But the only things of true value are those which will be theirs in the Hereafter—that is, God’s forgiveness and Paradise. Whatever the servant prefers over God is not something that is blessed.

159.text:
"It is out of Allah's mercy that you O Prophet have been lenient with them" opens the verse with the gentleness that is traced to its source, and the sources read the sentence as the reminder that the softness of the messenger with the men who had failed on the field was a gift from his Lord and not a softness that came from the man himself. "Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you" names the danger that the gentleness turned away, and the sources read the departing as the scattering of the companions from around the man who had been sent to them. "So pardon them, ask Allah's forgiveness for them, and consult with them in conducting matters" names the three commands that follow the gentleness, and the sources read the pardon as the wiping away of the fault, the prayer as the asking of the pardon that comes from God for the fault that stands between them and their Lord, and the consultation as the taking of the counsel of the companions in the affairs of the community. "Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah" names the step that follows the counsel, and the sources read the sentence as the teaching that the man who has done his part must leave the outcome in the hand of his Lord. "Surely Allah loves those who trust in Him" closes the verse with the love that rests on the people who lean on their Lord. The verses before it had named the mercy that followed the fault of the archers, and this verse shows the messenger dealing with the men who had failed, while the verses after it name the help of God that makes the whole community stand or fall. The sources also carry the occasions on which the messenger took the counsel of his companions, at Badr and at Uhud and at the trench, and they read the command of the consultation as a law for every leader who comes after him, so that the verse stands as the pattern of the community that keeps together after a wound.

**The mercy by which the Prophet was lenient with them.**

(And by the mercy of Allah, you dealt with them gently) means, "With Allah's mercy you became this kind. (And by the mercy of Allah, you dealt with them gently)[3:159]. meaning, who would have made you this kind, if it was not Allah's mercy for you and them. Due to Allah’s great mercy, your character, O Prophet, was made to be gentle with your Companions. It was by the mercy of God that you O Muhammad were lenient with them that is that you showed indulgence toward them when they disobeyed you; had you been harsh ill-natured and fierce of heart brutish and coarse towards them they would have dispersed split away from about you. (It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wert lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern) harsh in speech (and fierce of heart) coarse with them (they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them) pardon your Companions for that which may ensue from them (and ask forgiveness for them) from that transgression which ensues from them (and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs) in matter of war. Then, by placing the word, ‌ 'rahmah' (mercy) in an indefinite form, hint has been made towards the great and extensive spread of Allah's mercy which, in turn, makes it very obvious that this mercy is not restricted to the noble Compan-ions only, but extends in full to the Holy Prophet himself for Allah has made him identified with such perfect attributes. However, Allah gathered them and made you kind and soft with them, so that their hearts congregate around you." 'Abdullah bin 'Amr said that he read the description of the Messenger of Allah in previous Books, "He is not severe, harsh, obscene in the marketplace or dealing evil for evil. Allah addresses His Messenger and reminds him and the believers of the favor that He has made his heart and words soft for his Ummah, those who follow his command and refrain from what he prohibits.

**The heart that kept the companions around him.**

Hadst thou been harsh and hard of heart, they would have scattered from around thee. Then He says, "Hadst thou been harsh and hard of heart, they would have scattered from around thee. It was by the mercy of God that you O Muhammad were lenient with them that is that you showed indulgence toward them when they disobeyed you; had you been harsh ill-natured and fierce of heart brutish and coarse towards them they would have dispersed split away from about you. (And had you been severe and harsh-hearted, they would have broken away from about you;) Had this been the Prophet's behavior, "They would have scattered from around you. In this verse, Allah Almighty has said: 'Had you been rough and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you.' This indicates that harshness, in conduct or language, is sheer poison for a da'wah worker or a leader conveying Allah's message to people.

**The pardon and the prayer for their forgiveness.**

So pardon them pass over what they have done and ask forgiveness for them for their sins until I forgive them and consult them find out their opinions in the matter that is your affair in the battle and otherwise in order to win their hearts over and so that you may be emulated in this respect; and indeed the Prophet s would frequently consult them. So, pardon them their shortcomings with you and ask Allah to forgive them for what is between them and Allah; and ask their opinion in whatever needs to be agreed upon. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Hasan said that the Ayah means, "It is not for a Prophet to breach the trust. Soon, after that, the verse says: 'And seek forgiveness for them'. Not only that he should remain patient in what is painful, the Messenger is being asked not to forget seeking their good with utmost sincerity. Had these been not there in him, the mission of educating human beings with which he is charged would have never been accomplished as desired.

**The consultation that the Messenger was asked to hold.**

matter' which means that the Holy Prophet is to seek their advice in matters of concern so that they are fully satisfied and emotionally at peace, as the Messenger of Allah, by following this instruction, will be giving an external form to his intention of doing what is good for them. As far as the meaning of the word amr, in the Qur'anic verses: ‌ ‌ (And consult them in the matter -3:159) and ‌ ‌ (And a matter of theirs is (settled) by a consultation between themselves -42:38) is concerned, it can be said that there is the possibility to assign both the first as well as the second. Similarly, the verse from Surah a1-Shura cited above - - means that in every important matter (which) needs deliberation, whether it belongs to the field of authority and government or to some-thing important other than these, the customary practice of true Muslims is that they work through mutual consultation. If it is said that the word has been used here in the first sense while the second meaning is inclusive therein, that would not be something far-fetched since affairs relating to command and authority are all very important. Concerning the battle of Uhud, the Messenger asked the Companions if they should fortify themselves in Al-Madīnah or go out to meet the enemy, and the majority of them requested that they go out to meet the enemy, and he did. The Messenger of Allah used to ask his Companions for advice about various matters, to comfort their hearts, and so they actively implement the decision they reach. We would never say what the Children of Israel said to Musa, 'So go, you and your Lord, and fight you two, we are sitting right here.' Rather, we say march forth and we shall march forth with you; and before you, and to your right and left shall we fight. The Prophet also asked them if they should attack the idolators on the Day of Hudaybiyyah, and Abu Bakr disagreed, saying, "We did not come here to fight anyone. He also took their advice on the day of Khandaq (the Trench) about conducting a peace treaty with some of the tribes of Al-Ahzab (the Confederates), in return for giving them one-third of the fruits of Al-Madīnah. " The Prophet also asked them for their opinion about where they should set up camp at Badr.

**The decision and the trust that is put in Allah.**

(Then when you have taken a decision, put your trust in Allah,) means, if you conduct the required consultation and you then make a decision, trust in Allah over your decision,. (And when thou art resolved) to do something, (then put your trust in Allah) to give you triumph and domination. And when you are resolved to carry out what you wish after counsel rely on God put your trust in Him and not in any counsel; for God loves those who rely on Him. Then if you decide on something after agreeing together, then go ahead with it, and trust in Allah. Then when you have taken a decision, put your trust in Allah, certainly, Allah loves those who put their trust (in Him)If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? However, if one sits idle dreaming about distant means and irrelevant concerns, or if one relies solely on means and plans as effective agents and ignores the Prime Causer of means and the Planner-par-Excellence of all affairs and plans, then this would certainly be against tawakkul, the placing of trust in Allah. After having asked the Holy Prophet to consult with his Companions the verse concludes with the instruction on final decision-making. And in Allah (Alone) let believers put their trust It is not for any Prophet to illegally take a part of the booty, and whosoever deceives his companions over the booty, he shall bring forth on the Day of Resurrection that which he took. O master, if you were to give the unmixed wine of tawḤīd to your companions, with out the admixture of their own shares, they would flee and no longer come around you. " At another time he said, "I have a moment with God em braced by no proximate angel, nor any sent prophet.

160.text:
"If Allah helps you, none can defeat you" opens the verse with the help that decides the whole affair, and the sources read the sentence as the reminder of the day of Badr, when the community stood against a force that was greater than itself and the aid of its Lord brought it through. "But if He denies you help, then who else can help you" names the other side of the same truth, and the sources read the sentence as the question that leaves no room for any helper beside God, since the creature that is asked for aid may turn away and the Lord who gives it never does. "So in Allah let the believers put their trust" closes the verse with the command that follows from the two sentences before it, and the sources read the trust as the resting of the whole heart on the One whose help cannot be bought and cannot be withheld. The verses before it had named the gentleness of the messenger and the counsel he was asked to take, and this verse names the help that stands behind the whole community, while the verses after it turn to the goods of the field and the account that is kept for the man who takes what is not his. The sources also read the trust as an act of the inward life and not only of the tongue, since the man who leans on God finds in that leaning the security that no other support can give. The verse is set in the middle of the passage that rebuilt the community after the day of the wound, and the sources read it as the word that gave the men back their footing, when the enemy that had beaten them on the field was still standing in the road before Madīnah. The turn of the verse from the help of God to the trust that is placed in Him is read by the sources as the teaching that the two belong together, since the aid is asked for and the outcome is left in the hand of the One who gives it.

**The help that makes a people stand.**

(If Allah is your helper) as on the Day of Badr (none can overcome you) none of your enemy shall overcome you, (and if He withdraw His help from you) as on the Day of Uhud, (who is there who can help you) He will make that no one overcomes your enemy? If God helps you if He gives you assistance against your enemy as on the Day of Badr then none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you if He refrains from assisting you as on the Day of Uhud then who is there who can help you after Him? that is after His forsaking you? If Allah supports you with His help and aid, then no one can overcome you, even if everyone in the earth came together against you; yet if He does not help or protect you, then no one can help you after Him. If God helps you then none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you then who is there who can help you after Himḍ Therefore on God let the believers rely. It is said that when the matter was that of [His] help He said then none can overcome you. (If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? And in Allah (Alone) let believers put their trust), is similar to His statement that we mentioned earlier,.

**The help that comes from Allah alone.**

If Allah supports you with His help and aid, then no one can overcome you, even if everyone in the earth came together against you; yet if He does not help or protect you, then no one can help you after Him. (If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? And in Allah (Alone) let believers put their trust), is similar to His statement that we mentioned earlier,. (If Allah is your helper) as on the Day of Badr (none can overcome you) none of your enemy shall overcome you, (and if He withdraw His help from you) as on the Day of Uhud, (who is there who can help you) He will make that no one overcomes your enemy? In the matter of being forsaken He did not say then there is no helper for you but rather said more indirectly'then who is there who can help you after Himḍ Here there is a subtlety regarding the finer properties of the [divine] address. If God helps you if He gives you assistance against your enemy as on the Day of Badr then none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you if He refrains from assisting you as on the Day of Uhud then who is there who can help you after Him? that is after His forsaking you? If God helps you then none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you then who is there who can help you after Himḍ Therefore on God let the believers rely.

**The success that is granted to the believers.**

He helps the believers by granting success to the bodily forms bi-l-tawfīqi lil-ashbāḥ and then by granting [spiritual] realization to the spirits thuma bi-l-taḥqīqi lil-arwāḥ. Therefore on God let believers rely in finding security through sincere supplication and laying the robe of pardon over the defects of sin. [This is done] by devoutly seeking refuge and by rejecting any strength or power [other than God]. So let those who have faith depend on Him and on no one else. (If Allah is your helper) as on the Day of Badr (none can overcome you) none of your enemy shall overcome you, (and if He withdraw His help from you) as on the Day of Uhud, (who is there who can help you) He will make that no one overcomes your enemy? The protective friend ship walāya of God will remain purified from the confused clamoring of human qualities and the cravings and desires of the lower selves which are the remaining effects of [what] veils and hinders [people] from nearness. Those whom He helps He holds back from pursuing what is objectionable and those to whom He gives free rein and leaves to their own bad choices He forsakes. It is said that while [He will] help [you] against the enemy the worst enemy you have is the lower self within you. [His] help against [your] lower self comes when its claims of strength are routed by the guardians of His mercy and the armies of cravings junūd al-shahawāt scatter upon the attacks of the arriving hosts wufūd al-munāzilāt.

**The trust that is placed in Allah alone.**

(In Allah let believers put their trust) the believers should put their trust in Allah that He will give them triumph and domination. Therefore on God and on no one else let the believers rely. So let those who have faith depend on Him and on no one else. Therefore on God let believers rely in finding security through sincere supplication and laying the robe of pardon over the defects of sin. [This is done] by devoutly seeking refuge and by rejecting any strength or power [other than God]. (certainly, Allah loves those who put their trust (in Him). And in Allah (Alone) let believers put their trust It is not for any Prophet to illegally take a part of the booty, and whosoever deceives his companions over the booty, he shall bring forth on the Day of Resurrection that which he took.

**The lower self that is the worst enemy.**

It is said that while [He will] help [you] against the enemy the worst enemy you have is the lower self within you. [His] help against [your] lower self comes when its claims of strength are routed by the guardians of His mercy and the armies of cravings junūd al-shahawāt scatter upon the attacks of the arriving hosts wufūd al-munāzilāt. Those whom He helps He holds back from pursuing what is objectionable and those to whom He gives free rein and leaves to their own bad choices He forsakes. The protective friend ship walāya of God will remain purified from the confused clamoring of human qualities and the cravings and desires of the lower selves which are the remaining effects of [what] veils and hinders [people] from nearness. Therefore on God let believers rely in finding security through sincere supplication and laying the robe of pardon over the defects of sin. [This is done] by devoutly seeking refuge and by rejecting any strength or power [other than God]. If God helps you then none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you then who is there who can help you after Himḍ Therefore on God let the believers rely.

**The verses that follow the call to trust.**

In the first verse here, the recurring sense of grief that gripped the noble Companions after what happened at the battle of Uhud is being removed through elegant counsel. Verses 161-164 declare that the station of Allah's messenger is free of failings, that he exhibits the highest standard of trustworthiness, and that the very presence of his on the face of the earth is a great blessing and a favour shown to the people of the world. Verses 165-167 explain the reason why Muslims faced hardships at Uhud, while refuting the view of the hypocrites alongwith it in verse 168. Towards the end, in verses 169-171, it has been said that those who lay down their lives in the way of Allah achieve the ultimate success, real, permanent and full. Then every person shall be paid in full what he has earned, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly Is then one who follows (seeks) the pleasure of Allah like the one who draws on himself the wrath of Allah? His abode is Hell, and worse indeed is that destination They are in varying grades with Allah, and Allah is All-Seer of what they do Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting unto them His verses (the Qur'an), and purifying them, and instructing them the Book (the Qur'an) and Al-Hikmah [the wisdom and the Sunnah], while before that they had been in manifest error. (And by the mercy of Allah, you dealt with them gently) means, "With Allah's mercy you became this kind.

161.text:
"It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war" opens the verse with the clearing of the messenger from a suspicion that had been whispered in the community, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the men who carry the message of God are kept far above the taking of what belongs to the people. "And whoever does so, it will be held against them on the Day of Judgment" names the end of the man who takes from the spoils in secret, and the sources read the sentence as the disgrace that waits for him when the account is read before the whole creation. "Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged" closes the verse with the scale on which the whole affair is weighed, and the sources read the sentence as the promise that no good deed is lost and no evil is left unrecorded. The verses before it had named the help that comes from God alone, and this verse names the trust that is broken by the man who takes what is not his, while the verses after it set the one who seeks the pleasure of his Lord beside the one who earns His anger. The sources also carry the account of the red cloth that went missing on the day of Badr and the words that were spoken about the messenger, and they read the whole verse as the answer that closed those mouths. The passage sets the misappropriation of the spoils in the same breath as the honesty of the one who carries the message, so that the reader learns that the trust of the community is bound to the trust of the man who leads it. The sources read the verse as the root of the law that keeps the hand of the leader from what belongs to the people and as the comfort of the messenger whose name had been touched by the whisper of the doubters, and they set it beside the account of the day when the whole community is paid in full, so that the honest man and the man who takes in secret are weighed on one scale.

**It is not for a prophet to take the spoils.**

The verse translated as, 'And it is not (conceivable) for a prophet to misappropriate the spoils - 161', has a particular back-ground of its revelation. It is not for a prophet to be fraudulent; whoever defrauds [others] shall bring what he has defrauded on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul shall be paid in full what it has earned and they shall not be wronged. He has made the states of the prophets free of the stain of treacherous actions. No of the prophets of Allah would be dishonest and take anything from the gains of war which Allah had not assigned for him. (It is not for any Prophet) it is not permissible for any prophet (to deceive) to cheat his community regarding booty; it is also possible that the meaning is: it is not permissible for a community to deceive its prophet. (It is not for any Prophet to illegally take a part of the booty,) was revealed in connection with a red robe that was missing from the spoils of war of Badr. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Hasan said that the Ayah means, "It is not for a Prophet to breach the trust. When some red velvet cloth went missing on the Day of Badr and some people began to say ‘Perhaps the Prophet took it’ the following was revealed It is not for a prophet to be fraudulent an yaghulla a variant reading has the passive an yughalla meaning to attribute ghulūl ‘fraud’ to him to be treacherous with regard to the spoils so do not presume this of him; whoever defrauds shall bring what he has defrauded on the Day of Resurrection carrying it around his neck; then every soul the fraudulent and the otherwise shall be paid in full the requital of what it has earned what it has done and they shall not be wronged a single thing.

**The one who takes from the spoils of war.**

Whoever dishonestly takes something from the gains of war will be repaid by being disgraced on the Day of Judgement: carrying whatever he took in front of creation. This is also applied particularly to misappropriation in the spoils as the crime of stealing from the spoils is far more serious as compared to common thefts and filching since spoils belong to the whole Muslim army as a matter of right. It is not for a prophet to be fraudulent; whoever defrauds [others] shall bring what he has defrauded on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul shall be paid in full what it has earned and they shall not be wronged. Thereupon, this verse was revealed which said that ghulul is a great sin to be punished severely on Doomsday and that the very thought of linking this sin to a prophet is an ugly audacity, .for prophets are free of all sins (: ma sum). Even if there comes the thought of making amends at some later stage, it would be very difficult to give back to everyone what was due to be given, or seek their forgiveness for the injustice done. (Whoso deceiveth) as regards any of the booty (will bring his deceit with him) carried on his neck (on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be paid in full what it hath earned) that which it has deceived and also other things; (and they will not be wronged) their good works will not be diminished and their evil deeds will not be increased.

**The disgrace that waits before the whole creation.**

May Allah protect us from this disgrace of the Day we rise again which, according to some narrations, will be so hard on those who face it that they would wish to be sent to the fires of Jahannam in lieu of this terrible disgrace. What else could be more severe for the misappropriator when he, before the eyes of the whole creation on the plains of resurrection and retribution, will find himself disgraced with what he had stolen all stacked on his neck? A narration from Sayyidna Abu Hurairah appearing in Al-Bukhari and Muslim reports that the Holy Prophet said: 'Watch out, lest I see one of you with a camel loaded round his neck (and the announcement being made that this person had stolen a camel from the spoils). Whoever dishonestly takes something from the gains of war will be repaid by being disgraced on the Day of Judgement: carrying whatever he took in front of creation. It is not for a prophet to be fraudulent; whoever defrauds [others] shall bring what he has defrauded on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul shall be paid in full what it has earned and they shall not be wronged. (Whoso deceiveth) as regards any of the booty (will bring his deceit with him) carried on his neck (on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be paid in full what it hath earned) that which it has deceived and also other things; (and they will not be wronged) their good works will not be diminished and their evil deeds will not be increased.

**Every soul paid in full and none wronged.**

Then every soul will be given the total reward of what they earned. No one will be wronged by any addition to their disobedience or by any subtraction from their good actions. Then every person shall be paid in full what he has earned, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly Is then one who follows (seeks) the pleasure of Allah like the one who draws on himself the wrath of Allah? Someone who had secretly withheld a portion of wool from the spoils thought about it after the distribution of the spoils was over. Even if there comes the thought of making amends at some later stage, it would be very difficult to give back to everyone what was due to be given, or seek their forgiveness for the injustice done. Then every person shall be paid in full what he has earned, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly Is then one who follows (seeks) the pleasure of Allah like the one who draws on himself the wrath of Allah?

**The Prophet who was free of every stain.**

He has made the states of the prophets free of the stain of treacherous actions. Those to whom We gave the message to bear to Our servants convey it to those who should receive it. They are not concerned with any affair of a close intimate without Our command and they do not hold back harboring malice in passing on anyone's share when We have commanded it. Rather to each was revealed what they were meant to hear. Do you not see how [the Prophet] said of Abū Ṭālib Go and bury him when the Commander of the Believers ʿAlī said to him Your erring uncle has died ḍ Do you not see how [Muḥammad] accepted al-Waḥshī the killer of ḥamza when he became a Muslimḍ It is said It was not for any prophet to give Our secrets to any but the people to whom they were meant. Then Allah mentioned their surmise about the Prophet ﷺ that he was not going to divide any of the booty among them, and because of this they left their positions, saying: (It is not for any Prophet) it is not permissible for any prophet (to deceive) to cheat his community regarding booty; it is also possible that the meaning is: it is not permissible for a community to deceive its prophet.

**The leader who keeps his heart clean.**

The Prophet forgave the forty Muslims who had disobeyed his orders on the occasion of the battle of Uhud. However, people doubted that the Prophet had really forgiven them. They thought that he had done so only outwardly, for show, and that later he would show his anger. These verses tell us that the Prophet’s inner feelings did not differ from his outward behaviour. This also indicates what a Muslim leader should be like. His heart should be free of malice, jealousy, hatred, etc., even at a time when such a grave mistake is being made by his people as was made by the Prophet’s companions on the occasion of the battle of Uhud. He should not even keep any malice hidden in his heart. How could one, dedicated to leading people along the path of God’s will, ever think of meeting God, if he himself had gone against His will?

162.text:
"Are those who seek Allah's pleasure like those who deserve Allah's wrath" opens the verse with the question that sets the two men apart, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the one who walks after the good pleasure of his Lord can never be the equal of the one who draws the anger of his Lord on his own head. "Hell is their home" names the dwelling of the second company, and the sources read the sentence as the end of the road that the man who trades his faith for a gain is walking. "What an evil destination" closes the verse with the word of judgement on that end, and the sources read the phrase as the wonder that is invited from the reader at the place to which such a man is brought. The verses before it had named the scale on which every soul is paid in full, and this verse sets the two ends of the scale before the eyes, while the verse after it names the varying degrees in which the people stand before their Lord.

**The one who follows the pleasure of Allah.**

Is he who follows God’s beatitude being obedient and not defrauding like him who is laden one who returns with God’s anger because of his disobedience and fraud whose abode is Hell? (Is one who followth the pleasure of Allah) in taking the fifth and shunning deceit (as one who hath earned condemnation from Allah) as one who deserves Allah's wrath due to his deception, (whose habitation) i.e. the dwelling of the deceiver (is the Fire, a hapless journey's end?) where he shall end up. Is he who follows God's beatitude like him who is laden with God's anger whose abode is hellḍ An evil journey's end! Before Allah, someone who has faith and does good actions that please Allah is not the same as someone who disbelieves and does wrong, earning Allah’s anger and Hell as their resting place. The one with whom He is well pleased throughout eternity fī azālihi is not equal to the one with whom He is displeased and has abandoned in his states fī aḥwālihi and left him to rely on his own actions ʿalā aʿmālihi oblivious to the witnessing of His favors li-shuhūdi afḌālihi. To seek God's beatitude [one must] separate oneself mufāraqa from what has been prohibited and embrace muʿānaqa what has been commanded.

**The abode that waits for the people of anger.**

Is he who follows God's beatitude like him who is laden with God's anger whose abode is hellḍ An evil journey's end! This type of person is not similar to one who earns Allah's anger, has no means of escaping it and who will reside in Jahannam on the Day of Resurrection, and what an evil destination it is. (Is one who followth the pleasure of Allah) in taking the fifth and shunning deceit (as one who hath earned condemnation from Allah) as one who deserves Allah's wrath due to his deception, (whose habitation) i.e. the dwelling of the deceiver (is the Fire, a hapless journey's end?) where he shall end up. What an awful resting place and destination Hell is! (Is then one who follows (seeks) the pleasure of Allah like the one who draws on himself the wrath of Allah? His abode is Hell, and worse indeed is that destination!)[3:162],.

**The degrees of the people before Allah.**

His abode is Hell, and worse indeed is that destination They are in varying grades with Allah, and Allah is All-Seer of what they do Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting unto them His verses (the Qur'an), and purifying them, and instructing them the Book (the Qur'an) and Al-Hikmah [the wisdom and the Sunnah], while before that they had been in manifest error. They are of degrees before God: that is they possess degrees in the decree ḥukm of God-happy are those who have been brought close and wretched are those who have been kept at a distance. The one with whom He is well pleased throughout eternity fī azālihi is not equal to the one with whom He is displeased and has abandoned in his states fī aḥwālihi and left him to rely on his own actions ʿalā aʿmālihi oblivious to the witnessing of His favors li-shuhūdi afḌālihi.

**The man who carries the anger of his Lord.**

Is he who follows God's beatitude like him who is laden with God's anger whose abode is hellḍ An evil journey's end! This type of person is not similar to one who earns Allah's anger, has no means of escaping it and who will reside in Jahannam on the Day of Resurrection, and what an evil destination it is. Is he who follows God’s beatitude being obedient and not defrauding like him who is laden one who returns with God’s anger because of his disobedience and fraud whose abode is Hell? Before Allah, someone who has faith and does good actions that please Allah is not the same as someone who disbelieves and does wrong, earning Allah’s anger and Hell as their resting place. (Is then one who follows (seeks) the pleasure of Allah like the one who draws on himself the wrath of Allah? His abode is Hell, and worse indeed is that destination!)[3:162],.

163.text:
"They each have varying degrees in the sight of Allah" opens the verse with the ranks in which the people stand before their Lord, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that the reward of every man is measured to the work he has done and to the state of his heart. "And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do" closes the verse with the knowledge that misses nothing, and the sources read the sentence as the warning that no deed is hidden from the One who keeps the account of every company. The verses before it had set the two ends of the scale in the open, and this verse names the degrees that lie between them, while the chapter turns from here to the mercy that was given to the community after the day of the wound. The sources also draw the two companies apart in the rank they hold, and they read the whole verse as the closing of the passage that began with the gentleness of the messenger and the counsel he was asked to take, so that the degrees of the people are read as the fruit of the two roads that the passage has set side by side.

**The varying degrees in the sight of Allah.**

His abode is Hell, and worse indeed is that destination They are in varying grades with Allah, and Allah is All-Seer of what they do Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting unto them His verses (the Qur'an), and purifying them, and instructing them the Book (the Qur'an) and Al-Hikmah [the wisdom and the Sunnah], while before that they had been in manifest error. (There are degrees (of grace and reprobation) with Allah) He says: those who leave deceit have different ranks with Allah in Paradise; but those who deceive will occupy different levels in hell, (and Allah is Seer of what ye do) whether it is deception or other things. They are of degrees that is individuals of different degrees before God that is belonging to varying stations for those that follow His beatitude a reward and for those that are laden with God’s anger punishment; and God sees what they do and will requite them for it. They are different in the ranks and levels in the Afterlife: those who follow Allah’s pleasure find their places in Paradise, according to how high their rank in it is; and those who follow what displeases Allah find their places in Hell, according to how low their rank in it is. They are of degrees before God: that is they possess degrees in the decree ḥukm of God-happy are those who have been brought close and wretched are those who have been kept at a distance.

**Allah sees what they do.**

Nothing is hidden from Him, and everyone will be rewarded according to what they do. Then every person shall be paid in full what he has earned, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly Is then one who follows (seeks) the pleasure of Allah like the one who draws on himself the wrath of Allah? Then when you have taken a decision, put your trust in Allah, certainly, Allah loves those who put their trust (in Him)If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? They are of degrees that is individuals of different degrees before God that is belonging to varying stations for those that follow His beatitude a reward and for those that are laden with God’s anger punishment; and God sees what they do and will requite them for it.

Is he who follows God's beatitude like him who is laden with God's anger whose abode is hellḍ An evil journey's end! The one with whom He is well pleased throughout eternity fī azālihi is not equal to the one with whom He is displeased and has abandoned in his states fī aḥwālihi and left him to rely on his own actions ʿalā aʿmālihi oblivious to the witnessing of His favors li-shuhūdi afḌālihi. To seek God's beatitude [one must] separate oneself mufāraqa from what has been prohibited and embrace muʿānaqa what has been commanded. **The Prophet who was free of the stain of deceit.**

The word, ghulul is also used in the absolute sense for khiyanah, a breach of trust, (misappropriation, pilferage and stealing). The verse translated as, 'And it is not (conceivable) for a prophet to misappropriate the spoils - 161', has a particular back-ground of its revelation. Some people said that the sheet may have been, perhaps, taken by the Holy Prophet . Thereupon, this verse was revealed which said that ghulul is a great sin to be punished severely on Doomsday and that the very thought of linking this sin to a prophet is an ugly audacity, .for prophets are free of all sins (: ma sum). (There are degrees (of grace and reprobation) with Allah) He says: those who leave deceit have different ranks with Allah in Paradise; but those who deceive will occupy different levels in hell, (and Allah is Seer of what ye do) whether it is deception or other things.

164.text:
"Indeed, Allah has done the believers a great favour by raising a messenger from among them" opens the verse with the gift that is set at the head of the whole passage, and the sources read the favour as the sending of a man of their own company who knew their tongue and their ways, so that the word of God came to them in a shape they could carry. "reciting to them His revelations, purifying them" names the first two works of that messenger, and the sources read the reciting as the reading that put the verses of the book on his tongue and the purifying as the cleansing of the hearts from what the age of ignorance had laid on them. "and teaching them the Book and wisdom" names the third and the fourth, and the sources read the teaching as the instruction in the book itself and the wisdom as the unveiling of the secrets of the religion and the setting of the truth before the eyes of the people. "For indeed they had previously been clearly astray" closes the verse with the state from which the community was lifted, and the sources read the straying as the road that had no guide, so that the coming of the messenger is measured by the darkness that he ended. The verses before it had named the counsel and the trust that followed it, and this verse names the mercy that made those aids work, while the verses after it turn to the day of the wound and the question that was put to the community about it. The sources also carry the wonder that such men were never seen on the earth before, and they read the sending of the messenger as a favour that reached the whole creation. The verse is set in the passage that rebuilt the community after the day of the wound, and the sources read it as the reminder of the gift that the community still carried in its hands while it grieved over the field, since the man who recited the verses to them was still among them and the book that he taught was still in their keeping. The favour is read by the sources as one that no loss on a battlefield can undo, since the treasure of the community is the word of God in its hands and the guidance that keeps it from the road of the straying nations.

**The favour that was shown to the believers.**

Verse 164 speaks of the great favour Allah has shown to the Muslims by sending the Holy Prophet towards them. What is new in the present verse is the statement: 'And Allah has surely conferred favour on the believers'. The words on the believers' in this verse apparently mean that the advent of the Holy Prophet was a favour conferred on the Muslims only while at another place the Holy Prophet has been held as ‌ :'the Mercy for all the worlds' which includes both Muslims and non-Muslims. There is a common reason operating at both places, that is, the beneficial coming of the Holy Prophet is a great blessing and a great favour for the Muslim and the non-Muslim alike, just as the Qur'an is a Book of Guidance for the entire humanity. In order to explain the primary statement in the verse which declares that the Holy Prophet is the greatest possible blessing and favour for the believers or for the whole humanity, it can be said that the statement hardly needed any explanation. only if modern man was not all that blind to the spiritual side of life and, at the same time, was sacrificing every good thing for the sake of naked material gains. Allah then mentions his blessings on them, saying: However, Allah gathered them and made you kind and soft with them, so that their hearts congregate around you." 'Abdullah bin 'Amr said that he read the description of the Messenger of Allah in previous Books, "He is not severe, harsh, obscene in the marketplace or dealing evil for evil.

**The messenger who was raised from among them.**

[The Prophet] taught them their religion and made their proofs clear to them. Therefore, his having graced this world and his being born generous is a great favour shown to the universal kingdom of human beings, though true Muslims are the ones who have reaped the fullest benefit from these blessings. Never had the earth, nor the heavens, seen such men, each one of them, a living miracle of the Messenger of Allah, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. He belonged to them in every way but they were not grateful for his blessings did not respect his right and were not able to see what he guided them to nor refrain from straying in error-this is a description of his enemies who denied and were arrogant.

**The recitation that purifies the hearts.**

Allah blessed the believers and favoured them when He sent them a messenger from among them, who: recited the Qur’ān to them, purified them from worshipping others next to Allah and from shameful character traits, and taught them the Qur’ān and the ways of the Prophet ﷺ. The first task to be performed among the people is to foster in them the ability to read the signs of God spread everywhere within and without their own selves. This end is achieved by the reformer speaking to them in person and giving them the opportunity to spend time in his company. The message can, of course, be put across through general discourses and writing, but this would only be in principle; whereas by resorting to individual communication the message can be conveyed in a more precise and detailed way. Individual meetings thus serve the purpose of the purification of the addressees, or madu‘. His language, his style of speaking, his style of living— all should be familiar to them. No such feelings should be created between him and his addressee that may lead, in one way or another, to the latter becoming distanced from him, or to the addressee and the reformer becoming rivals.

**The teaching of the Book and the wisdom.**

The third task is to introduce to the madu‘ the shariah—the book of guidance on how life should be led in this world. The fourth task is to impart wisdom, that is, to unveil the secrets of religion and to highlight the truths hidden between the lines.
