165.text:
"Why is it when you suffered casualties at Uḥud" opens the verse with the question that was rising in the community after the day of the fight, and the sources read the sentence as the address to men who had lost seventy of their number and could not read the meaning of the loss. "although you had made your enemy suffer twice as much at Badr, you protested" names the day that was set over against the wound, and the sources read the sentence as the reminder that the same hand that gave the victory at Badr had left the field at Uhud, so that the community might learn the difference between its own strength and the strength of its Lord. "How could this be, Say, O Prophet" names the question that was carried to the messenger, and "It is because of your disobedience" names the answer that puts the cause of the day where it belongs, since the archers had left the post that the messenger had fixed for them and the fault of the ranks was the door through which the enemy came back. "Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything" closes the verse with the word that carries both the victory and the defeat in one hand, and the sources read the sentence as the statement that God does what He wills and is not bound by the plans of men. The verses before it had named the favour of the messenger and the book that he taught, and this verse turns to the day on which that community was tested, while the verses after it name the true believers and the hypocrites that the same trial drew apart. The sources also weigh the two sides of that day, since the enemy that had beaten the community at Uhud had itself been beaten twice over at Badr, and the grief of the community is read against the mercy that had come before it.

**The disaster that came upon the community.**

(What is the matter with you?) When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: (When a single disaster smites you), in reference to when the Muslims suffered seventy fatalities during the battle of Uhud,. He then mentioned their misfortune on the Day of Uhud, saying: (When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: "From where does this come to us?" Say, "It is from yourselves".), because you took the ransom. O believers, when disaster struck you at Uḥud, and many of you were killed, and you had beforehand afflicted on your enemies a disaster twice as great in terms of those killed and captured on the day of Badr; why then did you ask where this calamity came from? And why when distress befell you at Uhud when seventy of you were slain and you had afflicted twice the like of it at Badr slaying seventy of them and taking another seventy captive did you say in amazement ‘How is this?’ that is how did this defeat happen to us when we are Muslims and God’s Messenger is among us the last statement annā hādhā ‘how is this?’ constitutes the locus of the interrogative of denial.

**The victory of Badr that was set beside it.**

(What is the matter with you?) When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: (although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great,) during Badr, when the Muslims killed seventy Mushriks and captured seventy others,. (And was it so, when a disaster smote you) on the Day of Uhud, (though you had smitten (them with a disaster) twice (as great) as you inflicted on the people of Makkah, on the Day of Badr, a disaster twice that inflicted on you on the Day of Uhud, (that ye said: How is this?) how can this befall us when we are Muslims. And why when distress befell you at Uhud when seventy of you were slain and you had afflicted twice the like of it at Badr slaying seventy of them and taking another seventy captive did you say in amazement ‘How is this?’ that is how did this defeat happen to us when we are Muslims and God’s Messenger is among us the last statement annā hādhā ‘how is this?’ constitutes the locus of the interrogative of denial. In this verse, Muslims are being reminded that the hardship they were facing that day was only half of what they had already inflicted earlier at the battle of Badr, for seventy Muslims were martyred at Uhud while seventy disbelievers were killed at Badr and seventy others from them were taken prisoners by Muslims. (When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: "From where does this come to us?" Say, "It is from yourselves".), because you took the ransom.

**The disaster that smote the believers at Uhud.**

(And was it so, when a disaster smote you) on the Day of Uhud, (though you had smitten (them with a disaster) twice (as great) as you inflicted on the people of Makkah, on the Day of Badr, a disaster twice that inflicted on you on the Day of Uhud, (that ye said: How is this?) how can this befall us when we are Muslims. (you say: "From where does this come to us") why did this defeat happen to us? The subject of verse 165, translated as, And how is it that, when you suffered a hardship the twice of which you had inflicted upon them...° has appeared in several previous verses. Here, it comes for the sake of emphasis and further clarification because Muslims were very much disturbed as a result of this incident, so much so that some of them could not resist wondering why should they be suffering in that manner while they were in the company of the Holy Prophet doing Jihad. (What is the matter with you?) When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: (When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: "From where does this come to us?" Say, "It is from yourselves".), because you took the ransom.

**It is from your own selves.**

(Say, "It is from yourselves.") Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said, "When Uhud occurred, a year after Badr, Muslims were punished for taking ransom from the disbelievers at Badr [in return for releasing the Mushriks whom they captured in that battle]. (Say, "It is from yourselves.") means, because you, the archers, disobeyed the Messenger's command to not abandon your positions. (It is from yourselves) it is due to the transgression you committed yourselves when you left your positions. Secondly, and primarily too, the purpose of saying, 'This is from your ownselves' at the end of this verse, is to tell Muslims that the hardship they have faced is not because the enemy is stronger or his forces overwhelming, but all that has been caused by some of their own shortcomings, that is, they fell short in obeying the command of the Holy Prophet . O believers, when disaster struck you at Uḥud, and many of you were killed, and you had beforehand afflicted on your enemies a disaster twice as great in terms of those killed and captured on the day of Badr; why then did you ask where this calamity came from? The purpose behind this reminder is that Muslims should think positively in their present state of depression in view of the fact that they had already won a battle, inflicting a loss on the enemy twice as much as they had themselves suffered at their hands.

**The wisdom behind the hardship of Uhud.**

The Wisdom behind the hardships of the Muslims at Uhud. In this verse, Muslims are being reminded that the hardship they were facing that day was only half of what they had already inflicted earlier at the battle of Badr, for seventy Muslims were martyred at Uhud while seventy disbelievers were killed at Badr and seventy others from them were taken prisoners by Muslims. The purpose behind this reminder is that Muslims should think positively in their present state of depression in view of the fact that they had already won a battle, inflicting a loss on the enemy twice as much as they had themselves suffered at their hands. Now, a winner-like this need not surrender to sorrow and grief in the event defeat comes once, or less. Yet such happenings, though tragic in appearance, have a good side to them as well, for in this way Muslims are put to the test. In the face of unfavourable situations, the insincere fall away, while the true believers persevere because of their total trust in God. In this way, it becomes clear who are the trustworthy and who are not. Furthermore, God’s mercy is all the more focussed upon them, when, after incurring loss due to their inadvertent mistakes, the believers turn to God once again in all patience and humility. O believers, when disaster struck you at Uḥud, and many of you were killed, and you had beforehand afflicted on your enemies a disaster twice as great in terms of those killed and captured on the day of Badr; why then did you ask where this calamity came from?

166.text:
"So what you suffered on the day the two armies met was by Allah's Will" opens the verse with the word that sets the loss inside the will of God, and the sources read the sentence as the comfort that took the day of the fight out of the hands of the enemy and put it in the hand of the One who had measured it. "so that He might distinguish the true believers" closes the verse with the purpose that the trial was sent to serve, and the sources read the distinguishing as the sifting of the ranks, where the man whose faith was built on the truth stood and the man whose faith was built on the crowd fell away. The verses before it had named the disobedience that opened the door of the day, and this verse names the leave of God under which the whole of it took place, while the verses after it name the hypocrites who were drawn out into the open by the same hour. The sources also read the trial as a mercy in its own shape, since the wound of Uhud showed the community the difference between the companions of the road and the companions of the market.

**The day on which the two armies met.**

(That which befell you) of deaths and injuries, (on the day when the two armies) the army of Muhammad and that of Abu Sufyan (met, was by permission of Allah) by His will and decree; (that He might know the true believers) that He might see the believers in jihad;. And what afflicted you the day the two hosts encountered at Uhud was by God’s leave by His will and that He might know through knowledge manifested outwardly the true believers. The death, wounds and defeat you suffered on the day of Uḥud, when your army and the army of the idolaters met, was by the permission and decree of Allah, with far-reaching wisdom behind it: to make it clear who truly had faith. (And what you suffered on the day the two armies met, was by the leave of Allah), for when you ran away from your enemy, who killed many of you and injured many others, all this occurred by Allah's will and decree out of His perfect wisdom,. " And Allah has power over all things And what you suffered on the day the two armies met, was by the leave of Allah, in order that He might test the believers And that He might test the hypocrites, it was said to them: And what afflicted you the day the two hosts encountered was by God's leave and that He might know the believers.

**By the leave of Allah and not by chance.**

Immediately later, in verse 166, the words fa bi idhnillahi: indicate that whatever happened there was with the leave and will of Allah Almighty operating behind which are many wise divine arrangements, some of them having been explained earlier. And what afflicted you the day the two hosts encountered at Uhud was by God’s leave by His will and that He might know through knowledge manifested outwardly the true believers. The death, wounds and defeat you suffered on the day of Uḥud, when your army and the army of the idolaters met, was by the permission and decree of Allah, with far-reaching wisdom behind it: to make it clear who truly had faith. And what afflicted you the day the two hosts encountered was by God's leave and that He might know the believers. (And Allah has power over all things.) and He does what He wills and decides what He wills, and there is none who can resist His decision. " And Allah has power over all things And what you suffered on the day the two armies met, was by the leave of Allah, in order that He might test the believers And that He might test the hypocrites, it was said to them:

**That He might distinguish the true believers.**

(in order that He might test the believers.) who were patient, firm and were not shaken,. And what afflicted you the day the two hosts encountered was by God's leave and that He might know the believers. One such wise arrangement is that Allah will 'see' His true believers, and the hypocrites too, that is, the sincerity of Muslims and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become so clear that everybody could see it for himself. Here, the reference to Allah's knowing or seeing means seeing in the perspective of our own sense-experience in the mortal world. Otherwise, as far as Allah is concerned, He knows and sees everything, all the time. In the face of unfavourable situations, the insincere fall away, while the true believers persevere because of their total trust in God. In this way, it becomes clear who are the trustworthy and who are not.

**The wise arrangement that the trial made clear.**

So, the wise arrangement became all the more clear when, at the time of the trial, the hypocrites bowed out of the harm's way while true Muslims stood undaunted' in the middle of the battle front. Surely a trial that afflicts [one] by God's leave is sweeter than honey and more desirable than any blessing. However, this world being a world of trial, mischief-mongers too have full freedom of action. Yet such happenings, though tragic in appearance, have a good side to them as well, for in this way Muslims are put to the test. In this way, it becomes clear who are the trustworthy and who are not. He lightened the grave calamity met by the believers and possessors of insight on the Day of Uḥud by saying that the encounter was by God's leave. (in order that He might test the believers.) who were patient, firm and were not shaken,.

167.text:
"and expose the hypocrites" opens the verse with the other work of the day of the fight, and the sources read the exposing as the drawing out of the men who had carried the name of faith while their hearts stood with the enemy. "When it was said to them" names the call that came to that company, and "Come fight in the cause of Allah or at least defend yourselves, they replied" names the words of the call and the answer that met it, since the men were invited to the field or to the guard of their own houses and drew back from both. "If we had known there was fighting" and "we would have definitely gone with you" name the excuse that was put forward, and the sources read the two sentences as the speech of men who weighed the fight by their own advantage and not by the command that had reached them. "They were closer to disbelief than to belief on that day" names the state of the company itself, and "for saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts" names the shape of the fault, since the tongue carried a word that the heart never held. "Allah is All-Knowing of what they hide" closes the verse with the knowledge that sees the hidden as it sees the open. The verses before it had named the trial that separated the sincere from the false, and this verse shows the false being separated in the hour of the call, while the verse after it puts the word of those men over the graves of the men who had fallen. The sources also carry the scene of the city on that day, when the word went out to the men to march with the messenger and the company that had sat behind the walls sent back an excuse instead of an answer, so that the verse reads as the portrait of a people whose tongues were with the community and whose hearts were with their own safety.

**The call to fight or to defend themselves.**

(And that He might know the hypocrites) and that He might see the hypocrites, 'Abdullah Ibn Ubayy and his followers, returning to Medina, (unto whom it was said) 'Abdullah Ibn Jubayr said to them: (Come) to Uhud and (fight in the way of Allah, or defend yourselves) and your wives and children against the enemy, or increase the number of believers. Ubayy and his companions ‘Come now fight in the way of God His enemies or defend’ us against the enemy by increasing the multitude of our fighters if you are not going to fight; they said ‘If we knew how if we were skilled enough to fight we would follow you’. When they were told to fight in Allah’s path, or to defend their womenfolk and their people, they said, ‘Had we known that you were going to fight properly, then we would have followed you; but you actually throw yourselves to death! (They answered: If we knew) there was (aught of fighting we would follow you) to Uhud.

**The excuse that they had not known of the fighting.**

(What is the matter with you?) When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say: (They answered: If we knew) there was (aught of fighting we would follow you) to Uhud. "Had we known that fighting will take place, we would certainly have followed you. ("Had we known that fighting will take place, we would certainly have followed you.") meaning, according to Mujahid, if we knew that you would fight today, we would join you, but we think you will not fight. When they were told to fight in Allah’s path, or to defend their womenfolk and their people, they said, ‘Had we known that you were going to fight properly, then we would have followed you; but you actually throw yourselves to death! Ubayy and his companions ‘Come now fight in the way of God His enemies or defend’ us against the enemy by increasing the multitude of our fighters if you are not going to fight; they said ‘If we knew how if we were skilled enough to fight we would follow you’.

**Nearer to disbelief than to belief.**

(On that day they were nearer disbelief than faith) or the believers; it is also said that this means: their return to disbelief and the disbelievers was closer than their return to faith and the believers. God then said showing them to be liars They that day were nearer to unbelief than to belief for what they manifested of their forsaking the believers whereas before they had been outwardly nearer to belief; saying with their mouths that which was not in their hearts for even if they had known how to fight they would not have followed you. And He did this in order to demonstrate who the hypocrites were!

**The mouths and the hearts that Allah knows.**

Similarly when the one who is tired wants to break things off he becomes weary of being together and says That was that. God then said showing them to be liars They that day were nearer to unbelief than to belief for what they manifested of their forsaking the believers whereas before they had been outwardly nearer to belief; saying with their mouths that which was not in their hearts for even if they had known how to fight they would not have followed you. And God knows best what they hide of hypocrisy. Allah knows best what they hide in their breasts, and will repay them accordingly. Verily they gave honey to drink [to their enemies] but He plotted to put poison in it for them. (What is the matter with you?) When a single disaster smites you, although you smote (your enemies) with one twice as great, you say:

**The hypocrites who bowed out of the way.**

So, the wise arrangement became all the more clear when, at the time of the trial, the hypocrites bowed out of the harm's way while true Muslims stood undaunted' in the middle of the battle front. One such wise arrangement is that Allah will 'see' His true believers, and the hypocrites too, that is, the sincerity of Muslims and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become so clear that everybody could see it for himself. Here, the reference to Allah's knowing or seeing means seeing in the perspective of our own sense-experience in the mortal world. Otherwise, as far as Allah is concerned, He knows and sees everything, all the time. And He did this in order to demonstrate who the hypocrites were! In the face of unfavourable situations, the insincere fall away, while the true believers persevere because of their total trust in God. Then He spoke of those who were not sincere comrades how they offered excuses and were lazy.

**The believers who stood and the hypocrites who bowed out.**

So, the wise arrangement became all the more clear when, at the time of the trial, the hypocrites bowed out of the harm's way while true Muslims stood undaunted' in the middle of the battle front. One such wise arrangement is that Allah will 'see' His true believers, and the hypocrites too, that is, the sincerity of Muslims and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become so clear that everybody could see it for himself. And He did this in order to demonstrate who the hypocrites were! In the face of unfavourable situations, the insincere fall away, while the true believers persevere because of their total trust in God. In this way, it becomes clear who are the trustworthy and who are not. In the confrontation between truth and untruth, truth is always destined to have the final victory, because truth always has God on its side. Furthermore, God’s mercy is all the more focussed upon them, when, after incurring loss due to their inadvertent mistakes, the believers turn to God once again in all patience and humility. Then He spoke of those who were not sincere comrades how they offered excuses and were lazy. Immediately later, in verse 166, the words fa bi idhnillahi: indicate that whatever happened there was with the leave and will of Allah Almighty operating behind which are many wise divine arrangements, some of them having been explained earlier.

168.text:
"Those who sat at home" opens the verse with the company that stayed behind the walls of Madīnah when the call to the field had gone out, and the sources read the sitting as the choosing of their own safety over the command that had reached them. "saying about their brothers, Had they listened to us, they would not have been killed, Say, O Prophet" names the word that this company sent after the dead, and the sources read the sentence as the talk of men who measured the graves of the fallen by the counsel they had given and set their own opinion above the decree of God. "Try not to die if what you say is true" closes the verse with the answer that turns their claim back upon their own bodies, and the sources read the sentence as the challenge that shows the emptiness of the boast, since the men who could not keep death from their brothers could not keep it from themselves either. The verses before it had named the call that these men answered with an excuse, and this verse names the word that they spoke over the men who had gone out, while the verse after it lifts the company of the fallen above death itself and sets them alive with their Lord. The sources also note that death is written for every soul, and they read the verse as the closing of the mouth that claimed a wisdom which belonged to God alone. The whole passage turns on the two companies, the men who went out and the men who sat, and the sources read the verse as the line that divides the speech of faith from the speech of fear.

**Those who sat at home.**

They are (Those who, while they sat at home) and refrained from jihad, (said of their brethren) the hypocrites in Medina: Those who stayed behind from fighting, and said of their relatives who suffered on the day of Uḥud that if they had done as they said and not gone to fight then they would not have been killed, tell them, O Prophet, in reply, to keep death away from themselves when it arrives, if they are telling the truth in their claim that they would not have been killed if they had listened to them; and that the reason they themselves escaped death was because they stayed behind from fighting in Allah’s cause. And Allah has full knowledge of what they conceal (They are) the ones who said about their killed brethren while they themselves sat (at home): ((They are) the ones who said about their killed brethren while they themselves sat (at home): "If only they had listened to us, they would not have been killed.") had they listened to our advice and not gone out, they would not have met their demise. Muhammad and his Companions by remaining in Medina (had been guided by us they would not have been slain) in their military expedition.

**The killed brethren and the men who sat at home.**

((They are) the ones who said about their killed brethren while they themselves sat (at home): "If only they had listened to us, they would not have been killed.") had they listened to our advice and not gone out, they would not have met their demise. And Allah has full knowledge of what they conceal (They are) the ones who said about their killed brethren while they themselves sat (at home): They are (Those who, while they sat at home) and refrained from jihad, (said of their brethren) the hypocrites in Medina: Muhammad and his Companions by remaining in Medina (had been guided by us they would not have been slain) in their military expedition. Those who stayed behind from fighting, and said of their relatives who suffered on the day of Uḥud that if they had done as they said and not gone to fight then they would not have been killed, tell them, O Prophet, in reply, to keep death away from themselves when it arrives, if they are telling the truth in their claim that they would not have been killed if they had listened to them; and that the reason they themselves escaped death was because they stayed behind from fighting in Allah’s cause.

**Then avert death from yourselves.**

Those who alladhīna substitutes for the previous alladhīna or constitutes an adjectival qualification of it said to their brothers in religion whilst they themselves had stayed put refraining from joining the struggle ‘Had they the martyrs at Uhud or those who stayed put with us obeyed us they would not have been slain’. Say to them ‘Then avert ward off death from yourselves if you speak the truth’ in that staying put delivers one from it sc. from death. Those who stayed behind from fighting, and said of their relatives who suffered on the day of Uḥud that if they had done as they said and not gone to fight then they would not have been killed, tell them, O Prophet, in reply, to keep death away from themselves when it arrives, if they are telling the truth in their claim that they would not have been killed if they had listened to them; and that the reason they themselves escaped death was because they stayed behind from fighting in Allah’s cause. (Then avert death from yourselves if ye are truthful) in your claim. Then avert death from yourselves if you speak the truth. Say to them O Muḥammad [Then] extend the life of your souls istadīmū lil-anfusikum al-ḥayāt and defend them from the attacks of death wa-idfaʿū ʿanhā hujūma al-wafāt.

**The hearts that made a mistake and will not acknowledge it.**

Their hearts tell them that they have made a great mistake in not making sacrifices for the cause of truth, but by speaking ill of those who have done so, they want to keep up a pretence that they are in the right. People realize their mistake in their hearts, but they do not want to acknowledge it. In order to justify their course of action, they utter such words as even their own hearts attest to as being false. These thoughts are blameworthy and these hearts have retreated from witnessing the true nature of things. Those who relied upon their lower selves-having been seduced by them to prefer their own whims-and then opposed those who gave themselves over to the decrees of divine fate said If only they had heeded the warning about going out to the battle they would have been safe. How would they be able to do thatḍ How preposterous! This is entirely meaningless and those who speak of such things are never serious.

**The death that is decreed for every soul.**

But death is decreed for all human beings by God. The foolish speak of those who sacrifice their lives in the path of God as if it is only they who die, as if those who are striving towards worldly ends do not taste death. Incurring a seeming loss in God’s path is a positive happening, because those who have sacrificed everything for God are the ones most deserving of God’s rewards. Those who stayed behind from fighting, and said of their relatives who suffered on the day of Uḥud that if they had done as they said and not gone to fight then they would not have been killed, tell them, O Prophet, in reply, to keep death away from themselves when it arrives, if they are telling the truth in their claim that they would not have been killed if they had listened to them; and that the reason they themselves escaped death was because they stayed behind from fighting in Allah’s cause. (Then avert death from yourselves if ye are truthful) in your claim.

169.text:
"Never think of those martyred in the cause of Allah as dead, In fact, they are alive with their Lord" opens the verse with the correction that is put to the whole community, and the sources read the sentence as the forbidding of the thought that the men who fell on the field had been taken away and lost, and they note that the address is to the prophet himself so that the community may hear it from his mouth. The same words name the state that the men have entered, and the sources read the sentence as the plain statement of a life that death on the field had opened instead of ending, with the Lord named as the host at whose side the men are kept. "well provided for" closes the verse with the gift that is set before them, and the sources read the sentence as the provision that comes to them in the presence of their Lord, and they carry the account of the souls of the men of Uhud placed in the bodies of green birds that move among the rivers of the garden. The verses before it had named the men who sat at home and measured the graves of their brothers, and this verse answers that speech with the life that the fallen have entered, while the verses after it name the joy of those men over the bounty given to them and their gladness for the brothers who are still to come. The sources also weigh the honour of the men who lay down their lives, and they read the verse as the opening of the passage that lifts the rank of the martyrs above the reach of the grief of the world.

**Those who are slain in the way of Allah.**

(Think not) consider not (of those, who are slain in the way of Allah) on the Day of Badr and Uhud, (as dead) like any other dead people. Do not think, O Prophet, that those who have been killed struggling for the sake of Allah are dead. The following was revealed regarding martyrs Count not those who were slain read qutilū or quttilū in God’s way that is for the sake of His religion as dead but rather that they are living with their Lord their spirits inside green birds that take wing freely wherever they wish in Paradise as reported in a hadīth; provided for by Him with the fruits of Paradise. Count not those who were killed in God's path as dead. After the idolators defeated the Muslims (at Uhud), they started on their way back home, but soon they were concerned because they did not finish off the Muslims in Al-Madīnah, so they set out to make that battle the final one.

**The souls that are alive and receiving provision.**

Allah states that even though the martyrs were killed in this life, their souls are alive and receiving provisions in the Dwelling of Everlasting Life. Rather, they are alive with their Lord in His generosity, provided with blessings that we do not know about. (Nay, they are living) they are like the living. The very first distinction of martyrs mentioned here is that they have not died; rather, they have begun to live eternally. The answer is given by this very verse where it is said that the shuhada', i.e., those killed in the way of Allah, are blessed with provisions of Paradise from Him, and it is obvious that 'rizq' (provision or sustenance) is needed by and given to the living. Now, that the interim life of Barzakh is established as common to all, what is so special about shuhada' (martyrs)?

**The provision that is given to them.**

(With their Lord they have provision) they are given gifts. Allah states that even though the martyrs were killed in this life, their souls are alive and receiving provisions in the Dwelling of Everlasting Life. Nevertheless, there are times when the effect of their special life does show up on their bodies buried in this world, that is, the earth they rest in does not eat them up but leaves them good and intact (Qurtubi). There are no easy answers to questions such as - what is that distinct status and what is the nature of that life?

**The ranks of those who sacrifice their lives.**

The special merits and ranks of those who sacrifice their lives in the way of Allah. Inci-dentally, there is another cause of comfort here in the martyrdom of Muslims in the battle, for Allah has conferred such rewards on them so that others should envy them. God says that, on the contrary, what they call death is in fact the true, real life, which they have entered through the gateway of death. But they ought to know that the believers’ ‘dead’ have a far better ‘life’ than those among the non-believers who are alive: in the Hereafter, they rejoice in the bliss they have attained through sacrifice for the cause of God. At this point, it is worth noticing that their death and burial in a grave is something physically witnessed and realized by many, yet the Qur'an has, in several verses, clearly instructed that they should not be addressed or taken as dead. (No soul that has a good standing with Allah and dies would wish to go back to the life of this world, except for the martyr. He would like to be returned to this life so that he could be martyred again, for he tastes the honor achieved from martyrdom.) Muslim collected this Hadith. He who lives through the Real is happy indeed with Him.

**The speech of the men who called them lost.**

They said that Muslims were being slain meaninglessly at the instance of their leader—the Prophet. That is why sacrificing their lives for the cause of the Hereafter appears to them as self-destruction. Satan’s way is to take in hand those people whom he finds closer to him, and prevent them from advancing towards religion, by showing them the ‘dreadful’ consequences of such a step. Anas said, "A part of the Qur'an was revealed about them, but was later abrogated, 'Convey to our people that we met Allah and He was pleased with us and made us pleased.'" "O God, if the body's spirit is deprived of You, it will be a captive corpse, but if someone is killed in Your path hoping for union with You, he will live forever. " Indeed, when friends are wounded in the Friend's street, that is a good omen, for gambling away the spirit in the gaming-house of passion is their habit and disposition. He has clothed me with abasement in His love abasement in love for the likes of Him is eminence.

170.text:
"rejoicing in Allah's bounties and being delighted for those yet to join them" opens the verse with the state of the men who have been given the new life, and the sources read the rejoicing as the joy of hearts that have tasted the honour of their Lord, with the bounty named as the gift that was poured on them after the field. The same words name the second part of their joy, and the sources read the sentence as the gladness of the men over the brothers who are still in the world, since the waiting of those who are left behind is the waiting of men whom the same gift is kept. "There will be no fear for them" and "nor will they grieve" close the two greetings that are set over them, and the sources read the pair as the ending of every dread and every sorrow for the company that has passed into the presence of its Lord. The verses before it had named the life that these men were given, and this verse names the joy in which that life is spent, while the verse after it repeats their gladness over the grace and the bounty of their Lord and the reward that is never withheld from the believers. The sources also carry the account of the news that comes to the men of the garden when one of their brothers in the world is about to join them, and they read the verse as the comfort that was sent down for the families that had been left behind at Madīnah, since the men of the garden are told of the brothers who are walking towards them.

**The bounty in which they rejoice.**

(Jubilant (are they) because of that which Allah hath bestowed upon them of His bounty) of His honouring, (rejoicing for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind:) rejoicing because their brothers who are still in this world will join them because they have been given the good news that they will (that there shall no fear come upon them) when others are struck with fear (neither shall they grieve) when others grieve. They are delighted and rejoicing in what Allah has given them from His grace, and looking forward to meeting their brothers who are still on earth. Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty and rejoicing for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind that no fear shall befall them neither shall they grieve. Rejoicing farihīna a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person governing yurzaqūn ‘sustained’ in what God has given them of His bounty and they are rejoicing joyful for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind from among their believing brothers allādhīna ‘those who’ may be substituted by what follows sc. Count not those who were slain in God's way as dead but rather liv ing with their Lord provided for [by Him]. So, in summation, their first merit as pointed out in this verse is their distinct perennial life; the second is their being well-provided from Allah and the third is that they shall always be happy with Allah's blessings and grace. The fourth merit is the good news given to them about their relatives and circle of friends they left behind in the mortal world that they too shall deserve the same blessings and ranks with their Lord if they remain good in deeds and are active in Jihad (170-171).

**Those who have not yet joined them.**

And rejoicing for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind: If they are killed during a similar struggle, then they will receive the same grace as them. ‘rejoicing…that no fear’ that no fear shall befall them those that have not yet joined them neither shall they grieve in the Hereafter meaning they rejoice for their brothers’ future security and felicity allā of allā khawfun is an-lā meaning bi-an lā. Those who know that their loved ones are waiting for them while they are in comfort and ease [in the garden] would not take pleasure in living without being with them. Al-Suddi says that a shahld is informed beforehand when one of his close friend or relative is about to die. The news that a certain person was coming to them makes them as happy as one would usually be when an old friend, long separated by time and distance, comes to meet him. The Holy Prophet said to the noble Companions: 'When your brothers-in-faith fell martyrs at the battle of Uhud, Allah Almighty placed their spirits in the bodies of green birds and set them free.

**No fear upon them and no grief.**

There is no fear on them in terms of what awaits them in the Afterlife, and no sorrow about any worldly fortunes that passed them by. ‘rejoicing…that no fear’ that no fear shall befall them those that have not yet joined them neither shall they grieve in the Hereafter meaning they rejoice for their brothers’ future security and felicity allā of allā khawfun is an-lā meaning bi-an lā. Rejoicing farihīna a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person governing yurzaqūn ‘sustained’ in what God has given them of His bounty and they are rejoicing joyful for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind from among their believing brothers allādhīna ‘those who’ may be substituted by what follows sc. They are delighted and rejoicing in what Allah has given them from His grace, and looking forward to meeting their brothers who are still on earth. (Think not of those as dead who are killed in the way of Allah. Nay, they are alive, with their Lord, and they have provision.)

**The news that comes to them of the brothers who fell.**

The background of the revelation of this verse as narrated by Abu Dawud on sound authorities from Sayyidna Ibn Abbas is as follows. The Holy Prophet said to the noble Companions: 'When your brothers-in-faith fell martyrs at the battle of Uhud, Allah Almighty placed their spirits in the bodies of green birds and set them free. They get their sustenance from the streams and fruit-trees of the Paradise following which they return to special candelabrums held suspending for them underneath the 'throne' ('arsh) of the All-Merciful. When they noticed the luxury of their life there, they said, 'Can anyone tell them (their grieving friends and relatives in the world) about how we live here so that they stop grieving about us and go about striving in Jihad as we did.' Allah Almighty said, 'We shall let them know about this state of yours.' Thereupon, this verse was revealed (Qurtubi). (When your brothers were killed in Uhud, Allah placed their souls inside green birds that tend to the rivers of Paradise and eat from its fruits. They then return to golden lamps hanging in the shade of the Throne. When they tasted the delight of their food, drink and dwelling, they said, 'We wish that our brothers knew what Allah gave us so that they will not abandon Jihad or warfare.' Allah said, 'I will convey the news for you.') Allah revealed these and the following Ayat,.

**The life that is given to the spirits.**

Life in remembrance of the Real-after the lower selves have been anni hilated in the good pleasure of the Real-is more perfect than remaining with the blessings of created beings and being veiled from the Real. It is said that the one whose heir is the Living is one who does not disappear and cannot die even if he is killed: Surely bodies have been brought into existence for death so the slaying of a human being in God without doubt is best. So, in summation, their first merit as pointed out in this verse is their distinct perennial life; the second is their being well-provided from Allah and the third is that they shall always be happy with Allah's blessings and grace. Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty and rejoicing for the sake of those who have not joined them but are left behind that no fear shall befall them neither shall they grieve.

171.text:
"They are joyful for receiving Allah's grace and bounty" opens the verse with the joy that is drawn out once more, and the sources read the grace as the gift that was not earned and the bounty as the increase that follows it, so that the men of the garden are given twice over. "and that Allah does not deny the reward of the believers" closes the verse with the ground on which their joy rests, and the sources read the sentence as the promise that the wage of the faithful is kept whole and is never cut, so that no man who spent himself in the cause of his Lord is left without his portion. The verses before it had named the gladness of the company over the brothers who were still to join them, and this verse names the wage that is kept for the men who are still in the field, while the verses after it turn to those who answered the call of God and His messenger after they had been wounded. The sources also read the joy of the men as a joy that belongs to the world of certainty, and they place the spirits that were given as a gift and the bodies that were made a road beside the reward that is never wasted.

**They rejoice in the grace and the bounty.**

(They rejoice because of favour from Allah) because of a reward from Allah (and kindness) and honour, (and that Allah wasteth not) thwarts not (the wage of the believers) regarding jihad, i.e. that which befalls them in the course of jihad. They rejoice in the great reward that awaits them from Allah, and the increase of great reward, and that Allah does not let the reward of those who have faith go to waste, but repays it completely, and increases it. They rejoice in blessings from God and bounty, and that God does not leave to waste the wage of the faithful, those who answered God and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them. Joyful in grace in the reward and bounty in addition to it from God and that read wa-anna as a supplement to ni‘matin or wa-inna to denote a new clause God does not let the wage of believers go to waste but rewards them. Those who bow their heads before the command of God and the Messenger in passion for the religion made their own dear spirits the target of the enemy's arrows. So, in summation, their first merit as pointed out in this verse is their distinct perennial life; the second is their being well-provided from Allah and the third is that they shall always be happy with Allah's blessings and grace.

**The reward of the believers that is not wasted.**

They rejoice in blessings from God and bounty, and that God does not leave to waste the wage of the faithful, those who answered God and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them. They rejoice in the great reward that awaits them from Allah, and the increase of great reward, and that Allah does not let the reward of those who have faith go to waste, but repays it completely, and increases it. Joyful in grace in the reward and bounty in addition to it from God and that read wa-anna as a supplement to ni‘matin or wa-inna to denote a new clause God does not let the wage of believers go to waste but rewards them. (They rejoice because of favour from Allah) because of a reward from Allah (and kindness) and honour, (and that Allah wasteth not) thwarts not (the wage of the believers) regarding jihad, i.e. that which befalls them in the course of jihad. The fourth merit is the good news given to them about their relatives and circle of friends they left behind in the mortal world that they too shall deserve the same blessings and ranks with their Lord if they remain good in deeds and are active in Jihad (170-171).

**The spirits that were made a gift.**

Those who bow their heads before the command of God and the Messenger in passion for the religion made their own dear spirits the target of the enemy's arrows. They made their spirits a gift, their bodies a path, and their hearts a sacrifice. They bought that suffering and wounding with spirit and heart. Some of them thought nothing of trial and took the tribulation into their spirits and hearts, asking for union with Us. Some of them saw trial, and they fled to paradise and well-being.

**The men who derided the death of the believers.**

The martyrdom of the believers was derided by the hypocrites. They said that Muslims were being slain meaninglessly at the instance of their leader—the Prophet. The non-believers know only the profit and loss of this world. That is why sacrificing their lives for the cause of the Hereafter appears to them as self-destruction. But they ought to know that the believers’ ‘dead’ have a far better ‘life’ than those among the non-believers who are alive: in the Hereafter, they rejoice in the bliss they have attained through sacrifice for the cause of God. They exaggerate the power and the resources of the opponents of Islam in order to awe the believers.

172.text:
"As for those who responded to the call of Allah and His Messenger after their injury" opens the verse with the company that went out again from Madīnah while the wounds of Uhud were still on them, and the sources read the answering as the obedience that met the call of the messenger on the second day, when the word went out to march after the enemy and the men who had been hurt on the field stood up once more. "those of them who did good and were mindful of Allah will have a great reward" closes the verse with the promise that is set on that company, and the sources read the doing of good as the excellence that was added to the obedience and the mindfulness as the guard that kept the hearts from the second fall, with the great reward named as the wage that no measure can hold. The verses before it had named the joy of the men of the garden over their brothers, and this verse names the company that answered the call while the news of the graves was still fresh, while the verse after it names the men whose faith grew in the hour of the warning. The sources carry the announcement that the messenger made to the community on the second day, when the men who had carried the wounded of Uhud were asked to go out again after the enemy, and they read the answer of those men as the measure of a faith that had been tested once and had not broken. The road of that second march is read by the sources as the proof of the obedience that the verse praises, since the company that had lost its brothers and had taken its own wounds did not sit down behind the walls but stood up at the word of the messenger and walked out again, and the trade that the men carried with them on that road is read as a sign that they had left the whole outcome in the hand of their Lord, since a company that had been promised a reward for its going did not need to weigh the profit of the market on the same scale. The sources also read the obedience of the community as obedience to God himself, since the command of the messenger carries the command of the One who sent him, and they set the men of the second march beside the archers of the hill.

**Those who answered the call of Allah and the Messenger.**

(As for those who heard the call of Allah) answered Allah by obeying Him (and His messenger) by accompanying him in the lesser Badr (after the harm) on the Day of Uhud (befell them (in the fight); for such of them as do right) by accompanying the Prophet ﷺ at the lesser Badr (and ward off (evil) ward off contravention against Allah and disobeying the Messenger, (there is great reward) abundant reward in Paradise,. Those who alladhīna is the subject responded to God and the Messenger to his call to set out for battle when Abū Sufyān and his companions wanted to resume hostilities they agreed with the Prophet s that the encounter would be at the annual market-fair of Badr a year from the date of Uhud; after the wounds had afflicted them at Uhud — the predicate of the subject alladhīna is what follows for all those who were virtuous by obeying him and feared to disobey him shall be a great wage namely Paradise. Those who responded to the instruction of Allah and His Messenger when they were called to go out and fight for the sake of Allah, and to meet the idolaters in the battle of Ḥamrā’ Al-Asad, which followed the battle of Uḥud, after they had suffered wounds on the day of Uḥud, their wounds did not stop them from responding to the call of Allah and His Messenger. In its ultimate reality, the command of the Messenger of Allah is the command of Allah. But, in this particular verse, when the obedience of those people is praised, the command was attributed to both Allah and His Messenger as evident from the words of the text: ‌ : 'Those who responded to the call of Allah and the Messenger. As for those irreligious deviants who reject Hadith and belittle the status of the Messenger of Allah by restricting it to that of a courier (God forbid), a simple statement, that Allah Almighty has openly declared the command of the Messenger as His own, should be enough to understand the truth - if understanding is what they seek. It has been said in the first verse that despite injuries and hardships from the Battle of Uhud, when Allah and His Messenger called them up for another Jihad, they were ready for that too.

**The wound that they had received at Uhud.**

Allah then mentioned their accompaniment of the Prophet ﷺ in the lesser Badr (Badr al-Sughra), saying: Those who alladhīna is the subject responded to God and the Messenger to his call to set out for battle when Abū Sufyān and his companions wanted to resume hostilities they agreed with the Prophet s that the encounter would be at the annual market-fair of Badr a year from the date of Uhud; after the wounds had afflicted them at Uhud — the predicate of the subject alladhīna is what follows for all those who were virtuous by obeying him and feared to disobey him shall be a great wage namely Paradise.

In its ultimate reality, the command of the Messenger of Allah is the command of Allah. But, in this particular verse, when the obedience of those people is praised, the command was attributed to both Allah and His Messenger as evident from the words of the text: ‌ : 'Those who responded to the call of Allah and the Messenger. As for those irreligious deviants who reject Hadith and belittle the status of the Messenger of Allah by restricting it to that of a courier (God forbid), a simple statement, that Allah Almighty has openly declared the command of the Messenger as His own, should be enough to understand the truth - if understanding is what they seek. 173.text:
"Those who were warned" opens the verse with the company that was met on the road by men who came with a message of fear, and the sources read the warning as the word that the caravan of the enemy and its friends spread through Madīnah, so that the believers might turn back from the march and leave the field to their enemies. "Your enemies have mobilized their forces against you" names the word that those men carried, and "so fear them" names the end that the warning was meant to reach, since the purpose of the whole speech was to put dread into the hearts of the community. "the warning only made them grow stronger in faith and they replied" names the answer that the community gave, and the sources read the growing as the increase of certainty that came with the news itself, so that the danger that was meant to break the men only fixed them more firmly in their trust. "Allah alone is sufficient as an aid for us and He is the best Protector" closes the verse with the word that the community sent back over the road, and the sources read the sentence as the leaving of the whole affair in the hand of the One who is enough for every need. The verses before it had named the company that answered the call after the wound, and this verse shows what that company met on the way and how it answered, while the verses after it name the face of the enemy on the day that followed. The sources also read the sentence of the community as a word of trust that walks beside the use of every means, since the men had gathered their strength and taken their road before they left the outcome with their Protector.

**The warning that was sent to the believers.**

(Lo! the people) Abu Sufyan and his men (have gathered against you) at the Lutaymah, the latter being a market near Makkah, (therefore fear them) fear going out to fight them. Some of the idolaters said to them that the Quraysh, led by Abū Sufyān, had come together in great numbers to fight against them and to finish them off, warning them against meeting them. Mas‘ūd al-Ashja‘ī said ‘The people Abū Sufyān and his companions have gathered their multitudes against you in order to exterminate you therefore fear them’ and do not go out to encounter them; but that saying increased them in faith in their belief in God and in certainty and they said ‘God is sufficient for us He will deal fully for us with their affair; an excellent Guardian is He’ the One to whom the matter is entrusted. When they reached Dhu'l-Hulayfah, the Bedouins and other people came to them, saying: 'Abu Sufyan is going to attack you', but they only said: 'Allah is Sufficient for us! They gave the people of the caravan some money and induced them to spread rumours in Madīnah that would strike terror into the hearts of the Muslims. When they reached Madīnah, they started saying that they had seen themselves that the Makkans were gathering a large force and intended to attack Madīnah once again.

**The faith that grew at the warning.**

this only (increased the faith of them) emboldened them even more (and they cried: Allah is sufficient for us!) Allah is sufficient to give victory. But their words and attempts to scare them only increased their reliance on Allah and their trust in His promise. Those to whom people said The people have gathered against you therefore fear them ; but that increased them in faith and they said God is sufficient for us an excellent Guardian is He. [Whenever] events in the present world confused them outwardly the gleams from unveilings Ṭawāliʿ min al-kushūfāt opened up for them in their innermost selves asrār and they increased in one level of certainty after another. Mas‘ūd al-Ashja‘ī said ‘The people Abū Sufyān and his companions have gathered their multitudes against you in order to exterminate you therefore fear them’ and do not go out to encounter them; but that saying increased them in faith in their belief in God and in certainty and they said ‘God is sufficient for us He will deal fully for us with their affair; an excellent Guardian is He’ the One to whom the matter is entrusted. That is, blessed are such people who heard the news that the enemy has assembled a big fighting force against them and also the advice that they should fear them and avoid fighting - still, this news further increased the fervour of their faith. As obvious, the Faith of these noble souls was perfect from the very first day they had embraced Islam, therefore, the reference to the increase in Faith in these two verses (172-173) means the increase in the qualitative contents and end-results of Faith.

**Allah is sufficient for us.**

this only (increased the faith of them) emboldened them even more (and they cried: Allah is sufficient for us!) Allah is sufficient to give victory. Most Excellent is He in Whom we trust!' And so Allah, exalted is He revealed about them (Those unto whom men said: Lo! the people have gathered against you, therefor fear them) [3:173] up to His saying ( and Allah is of Infinite Bounty) [3:174] . So they went out to meet them, saying that Allah was enough for them and that He is the best Protector, while committing their lives to Him. Mas‘ūd al-Ashja‘ī said ‘The people Abū Sufyān and his companions have gathered their multitudes against you in order to exterminate you therefore fear them’ and do not go out to encounter them; but that saying increased them in faith in their belief in God and in certainty and they said ‘God is sufficient for us He will deal fully for us with their affair; an excellent Guardian is He’ the One to whom the matter is entrusted. The Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, said to his Companions: 'Would a group gather for war for Allah's sake and seek their enemy, for this is more prone to cause damage to the enemy and more likely to drive them away for a distance?' A group set off, despite of what Allah knew of their extreme exhaustion. The rumour about the Makkans actually benefited the Muslims, as they were now forewarned of their enemies’ intentions.

**The trust that the believers place in their Protector.**

Among the signs of certainty is the reliance of hearts in God alone with the severing of any hope of imagined aid and support from created beings. (Most Excellent is He in Whom we trust!) our trust is in Allah. So they went out to meet them, saying that Allah was enough for them and that He is the best Protector, while committing their lives to Him. Placing trust in Allah after having forsaken available physical means is no Sunnah (established practice) of the Messenger of Allah . Allah censures inaction but it is your duty to use means, following which, when you find yourself powerless against odds, then say: 'Allah is all-sufficient for me, and the best one to trust in.'. However, the Muslims’ total trust in God was a guarantee that the planning of the enemies would prove counter-productive.

**The means that are used beside the trust.**

It means that he collected and used all physical means which were available to him and it was only after that he said: 'Allah is all-sufficient for us.' This, then, is the most authentic form of Tawakkul (Trust in Allah) taught by the Holy Qur'an, personally practiced by the Holy Prophet and this was what he made others around him do. All physical means which we have in the life of this world are blessings from Allah. Placing trust in Allah after having forsaken available physical means is no Sunnah (established practice) of the Messenger of Allah . Allah censures inaction but it is your duty to use means, following which, when you find yourself powerless against odds, then say: 'Allah is all-sufficient for me, and the best one to trust in.'. When the Makkans learnt that the Muslim force was advancing towards them, they thought that the Muslims had mustered fresh forces. They immediately fled to Makkah, giving up all thoughts of attacking Madīnah again. They thus set out with the Prophet s and arrived at the market-fair of Badr but God had cast terror into the hearts of Abū Sufyān and his followers and so they did not turn up. They the believers had merchandise with them and so they traded and made profits.
